# API Reference ¶

The following section outlines the API of discord.py.

Note

This module uses the Python logging module to log diagnostic and errors in an output independent way. If the logging module is not configured, these logs will not be output anywhere. See [Setting Up Logging](https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/logging.html#logging-setup) for more information on how to set up and use the logging module with discord.py.

## Version Related Info ¶

There are two main ways to query version information about the library. For guarantees, check [Version Guarantees](https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/version_guarantees.html#version-guarantees).

<dl><dt>discord.version_info<a href="#discord.version_info" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A named tuple that is similar to <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/sys.html#sys.version_info" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>sys.version_info</code></a>.

Just like <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/sys.html#sys.version_info" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>sys.version_info</code></a> the valid values for <code>releaselevel</code> are ‘alpha’, ‘beta’, ‘candidate’ and ‘final’.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>discord.__version__<a href="#discord.__version__" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A string representation of the version. e.g. <code>'1.0.0rc1'</code>. This is based off of <a href="https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0440">**PEP 440**</a>.

</dd></dl>

<dl><dt>*class*discord.Client(***, *intents*, ***options*)<a href="#discord.Client" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Represents a client connection that connects to Discord. This class is used to interact with the Discord WebSocket and API.

<dl><dt>async with x</dt>
<dd>

Asynchronously initialises the client and automatically cleans up.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl>

A number of options can be passed to the <a href="#discord.Client" title="discord.Client"><code>Client</code></a>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **max\_messages** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) –

  The maximum number of messages to store in the internal message cache. This defaults to <code>1000</code>. Passing in <code>None</code> disables the message cache.

  Changed in version 1.3: Allow disabling the message cache and change the default size to <code>1000</code>.
- **proxy** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – Proxy URL.
- **proxy\_auth** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.aiohttp.org/en/stable/client_reference.html#aiohttp.BasicAuth" title="(in aiohttp v3.13)"><code>aiohttp.BasicAuth</code></a>]) – An object that represents proxy HTTP Basic Authorization.
- **shard\_id** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) – Integer starting at <code>0</code> and less than <a href="#discord.ShardInfo.shard_count" title="discord.ShardInfo.shard_count"><code>shard_count</code></a>.
- **shard\_count** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) – The total number of shards.
- **application\_id** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The client’s application ID.
- **intents** (<a href="#discord.Intents" title="discord.Intents"><code>Intents</code></a>) –

  The intents that you want to enable for the session. This is a way of disabling and enabling certain gateway events from triggering and being sent.

  New in version 1.5.

  Changed in version 2.0: Parameter is now required.
- **member\_cache\_flags** (<a href="#discord.MemberCacheFlags" title="discord.MemberCacheFlags"><code>MemberCacheFlags</code></a>) –

  Allows for finer control over how the library caches members. If not given, defaults to cache as much as possible with the currently selected intents.

  New in version 1.5.
- **chunk\_guilds\_at\_startup** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Indicates if <a href="#discord.on_ready" title="discord.on_ready"><code>on_ready()</code></a> should be delayed to chunk all guilds at start-up if necessary. This operation is incredibly slow for large amounts of guilds. The default is <code>True</code> if <a href="#discord.Intents.members" title="discord.Intents.members"><code>Intents.members</code></a> is <code>True</code>.

  New in version 1.5.
- **status** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.Status" title="discord.Status"><code>Status</code></a>]) – A status to start your presence with upon logging on to Discord.
- **activity** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.BaseActivity" title="discord.BaseActivity"><code>BaseActivity</code></a>]) – An activity to start your presence with upon logging on to Discord.
- **allowed\_mentions** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.AllowedMentions" title="discord.AllowedMentions"><code>AllowedMentions</code></a>]) –

  Control how the client handles mentions by default on every message sent.

  New in version 1.4.
- **heartbeat\_timeout** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>float</code></a>) – The maximum numbers of seconds before timing out and restarting the WebSocket in the case of not receiving a HEARTBEAT\_ACK. Useful if processing the initial packets take too long to the point of disconnecting you. The default timeout is 60 seconds.
- **guild\_ready\_timeout** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>float</code></a>) –

  The maximum number of seconds to wait for the GUILD\_CREATE stream to end before preparing the member cache and firing READY. The default timeout is 2 seconds.

  New in version 1.4.
- **assume\_unsync\_clock** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to assume the system clock is unsynced. This applies to the ratelimit handling code. If this is set to <code>True</code>, the default, then the library uses the time to reset a rate limit bucket given by Discord. If this is <code>False</code> then your system clock is used to calculate how long to sleep for. If this is set to <code>False</code> it is recommended to sync your system clock to Google’s NTP server.

  New in version 1.3.
- **enable\_debug\_events** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to enable events that are useful only for debugging gateway related information.

  Right now this involves <a href="#discord.on_socket_raw_receive" title="discord.on_socket_raw_receive"><code>on_socket_raw_receive()</code></a> and <a href="#discord.on_socket_raw_send" title="discord.on_socket_raw_send"><code>on_socket_raw_send()</code></a>. If this is <code>False</code> then those events will not be dispatched (due to performance considerations). To enable these events, this must be set to <code>True</code>. Defaults to <code>False</code>.

  New in version 2.0.
- **enable\_raw\_presences** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to manually enable or disable the <a href="#discord.on_raw_presence_update" title="discord.on_raw_presence_update"><code>on_raw_presence_update()</code></a> event.

  Setting this flag to <code>True</code> requires <a href="#discord.Intents.presences" title="discord.Intents.presences"><code>Intents.presences</code></a> to be enabled.

  By default, this flag is set to <code>True</code> only when <a href="#discord.Intents.presences" title="discord.Intents.presences"><code>Intents.presences</code></a> is enabled and <a href="#discord.Intents.members" title="discord.Intents.members"><code>Intents.members</code></a> is disabled, otherwise it’s set to <code>False</code>.

  New in version 2.5.
- **http\_trace** (<a href="https://docs.aiohttp.org/en/stable/tracing_reference.html#aiohttp.TraceConfig" title="(in aiohttp v3.13)"><code>aiohttp.TraceConfig</code></a>) –

  The trace configuration to use for tracking HTTP requests the library does using <code>aiohttp</code>. This allows you to check requests the library is using. For more information, check the <a href="https://docs.aiohttp.org/en/stable/client_advanced.html#client-tracing">aiohttp documentation</a>.

  New in version 2.0.
- **max\_ratelimit\_timeout** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>float</code></a>]) –

  The maximum number of seconds to wait when a non-global rate limit is encountered. If a request requires sleeping for more than the seconds passed in, then <a href="#discord.RateLimited" title="discord.RateLimited"><code>RateLimited</code></a> will be raised. By default, there is no timeout limit. In order to prevent misuse and unnecessary bans, the minimum value this can be set to is <code>30.0</code> seconds.

  New in version 2.0.
- **connector** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.aiohttp.org/en/stable/client_reference.html#aiohttp.BaseConnector" title="(in aiohttp v3.13)"><code>aiohttp.BaseConnector</code></a>]) –

  The aiohttp connector to use for this client. This can be used to control underlying aiohttp behavior, such as setting a dns resolver or sslcontext.

  New in version 2.5.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>ws<a href="#discord.Client.ws" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The websocket gateway the client is currently connected to. Could be <code>None</code>.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>@event<a href="#discord.Client.event" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A decorator that registers an event to listen to.

You can find more info about the events on the <a href="#discord-api-events">documentation below</a>.

The events must be a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine" title="(in Python v3.14)">coroutine</a>, if not, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> is raised.

Example

```
@client.event
async def on_ready():
    print('Ready!')

```

Changed in version 2.0: <code>coro</code> parameter is now positional-only.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – The coroutine passed is not actually a coroutine.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*latency<a href="#discord.Client.latency" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Measures latency between a HEARTBEAT and a HEARTBEAT\_ACK in seconds.

This could be referred to as the Discord WebSocket protocol latency.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>float</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>is_ws_ratelimited()<a href="#discord.Client.is_ws_ratelimited" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>: Whether the websocket is currently rate limited.

This can be useful to know when deciding whether you should query members using HTTP or via the gateway.

New in version 1.6.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*property*user<a href="#discord.Client.user" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Represents the connected client. <code>None</code> if not logged in.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="#discord.ClientUser" title="discord.ClientUser"><code>ClientUser</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*guilds<a href="#discord.Client.guilds" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The guilds that the connected client is a member of.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>

Sequence\[<a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*emojis<a href="#discord.Client.emojis" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The emojis that the connected client has.

Note

This does not include the emojis that are owned by the application. Use <a href="#discord.Client.fetch_application_emoji" title="discord.Client.fetch_application_emoji"><code>fetch_application_emoji()</code></a> to get those.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Sequence\[<a href="#discord.Emoji" title="discord.Emoji"><code>Emoji</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*stickers<a href="#discord.Client.stickers" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The stickers that the connected client has.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Sequence\[<a href="#discord.GuildSticker" title="discord.GuildSticker"><code>GuildSticker</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*soundboard_sounds<a href="#discord.Client.soundboard_sounds" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The soundboard sounds that the connected client has.

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>: Specifies if the client’s internal cache is ready for use.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*await* on_error(*event_method*, */*, **args*, ***kwargs*)<a href="#discord.Client.on_error" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

The default error handler provided by the client.

By default this logs to the library logger however it could be overridden to have a different implementation. Check <a href="#discord.on_error" title="discord.on_error"><code>on_error()</code></a> for more details.

Changed in version 2.0: <code>event_method</code> parameter is now positional-only and instead of writing to <code>sys.stderr</code> it logs instead.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*await* before_identify_hook(*shard_id*, ***, *initial=False*)<a href="#discord.Client.before_identify_hook" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

A hook that is called before IDENTIFYing a session. This is useful if you wish to have more control over the synchronization of multiple IDENTIFYing clients.

The default implementation sleeps for 5 seconds.

New in version 1.4.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **shard\_id** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The shard ID that requested being IDENTIFY’d
- **initial** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether this IDENTIFY is the first initial IDENTIFY.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* setup_hook()<a href="#discord.Client.setup_hook" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

A coroutine to be called to setup the bot, by default this is blank.

To perform asynchronous setup after the bot is logged in but before it has connected to the Websocket, overwrite this coroutine.

This is only called once, in <a href="#discord.Client.login" title="discord.Client.login"><code>login()</code></a>, and will be called before any events are dispatched, making it a better solution than doing such setup in the <a href="#discord.on_ready" title="discord.on_ready"><code>on_ready()</code></a> event.

Warning

Since this is called *before* the websocket connection is made therefore anything that waits for the websocket will deadlock, this includes things like <a href="#discord.Client.wait_for" title="discord.Client.wait_for"><code>wait_for()</code></a> and <a href="#discord.Client.wait_until_ready" title="discord.Client.wait_until_ready"><code>wait_until_ready()</code></a>.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*await* login(*token*)<a href="#discord.Client.login" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Logs in the client with the specified credentials and calls the <a href="#discord.Client.setup_hook" title="discord.Client.setup_hook"><code>setup_hook()</code></a>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**token** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The authentication token. Do not prefix this token with anything as the library will do it for you.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.LoginFailure" title="discord.LoginFailure">**LoginFailure**</a> – The wrong credentials are passed.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – An unknown HTTP related error occurred, usually when it isn’t 200 or the known incorrect credentials passing status code.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* connect(***, *reconnect=True*)<a href="#discord.Client.connect" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Creates a websocket connection and lets the websocket listen to messages from Discord. This is a loop that runs the entire event system and miscellaneous aspects of the library. Control is not resumed until the WebSocket connection is terminated.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**reconnect** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – If we should attempt reconnecting, either due to internet failure or a specific failure on Discord’s part. Certain disconnects that lead to bad state will not be handled (such as invalid sharding payloads or bad tokens).

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.GatewayNotFound" title="discord.GatewayNotFound">**GatewayNotFound**</a> – If the gateway to connect to Discord is not found. Usually if this is thrown then there is a Discord API outage.
- <a href="#discord.ConnectionClosed" title="discord.ConnectionClosed">**ConnectionClosed**</a> – The websocket connection has been terminated.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* close()<a href="#discord.Client.close" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Closes the connection to Discord.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>clear()<a href="#discord.Client.clear" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Clears the internal state of the bot.

After this, the bot can be considered “re-opened”, i.e. <a href="#discord.Client.is_closed" title="discord.Client.is_closed"><code>is_closed()</code></a> and <a href="#discord.Client.is_ready" title="discord.Client.is_ready"><code>is_ready()</code></a> both return <code>False</code> along with the bot’s internal cache cleared.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*await* start(*token*, ***, *reconnect=True*)<a href="#discord.Client.start" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

A shorthand coroutine for <a href="#discord.Client.login" title="discord.Client.login"><code>login()</code></a> + <a href="#discord.Client.connect" title="discord.Client.connect"><code>connect()</code></a>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **token** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The authentication token. Do not prefix this token with anything as the library will do it for you.
- **reconnect** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – If we should attempt reconnecting, either due to internet failure or a specific failure on Discord’s part. Certain disconnects that lead to bad state will not be handled (such as invalid sharding payloads or bad tokens).

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – An unexpected keyword argument was received.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>run(*token*, ***, *reconnect=True*, *log_handler=...*, *log_formatter=...*, *log_level=...*, *root_logger=False*)<a href="#discord.Client.run" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A blocking call that abstracts away the event loop initialisation from you.

If you want more control over the event loop then this function should not be used. Use <a href="#discord.Client.start" title="discord.Client.start"><code>start()</code></a> coroutine or <a href="#discord.Client.connect" title="discord.Client.connect"><code>connect()</code></a> + <a href="#discord.Client.login" title="discord.Client.login"><code>login()</code></a>.

This function also sets up the logging library to make it easier for beginners to know what is going on with the library. For more advanced users, this can be disabled by passing <code>None</code> to the <code>log_handler</code> parameter.

Warning

This function must be the last function to call due to the fact that it is blocking. That means that registration of events or anything being called after this function call will not execute until it returns.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **token** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The authentication token. Do not prefix this token with anything as the library will do it for you.
- **reconnect** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – If we should attempt reconnecting, either due to internet failure or a specific failure on Discord’s part. Certain disconnects that lead to bad state will not be handled (such as invalid sharding payloads or bad tokens).
- **log\_handler** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.html#logging.Handler" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>logging.Handler</code></a>]) –

  The log handler to use for the library’s logger. If this is <code>None</code> then the library will not set up anything logging related. Logging will still work if <code>None</code> is passed, though it is your responsibility to set it up.

  The default log handler if not provided is <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.handlers.html#logging.StreamHandler" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>logging.StreamHandler</code></a>.

  New in version 2.0.
- **log\_formatter** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.html#logging.Formatter" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>logging.Formatter</code></a>) –

  The formatter to use with the given log handler. If not provided then it defaults to a colour based logging formatter (if available).

  New in version 2.0.
- **log\_level** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) –

  The default log level for the library’s logger. This is only applied if the <code>log_handler</code> parameter is not <code>None</code>. Defaults to <code>logging.INFO</code>.

  New in version 2.0.
- **root\_logger** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to set up the root logger rather than the library logger. By default, only the library logger (<code>'discord'</code>) is set up. If this is set to <code>True</code> then the root logger is set up as well.

  Defaults to <code>False</code>.

  New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>is_closed()<a href="#discord.Client.is_closed" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

</dl><dl><dt>*for ... in* get_all_channels()<a href="#discord.Client.get_all_channels" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A generator that retrieves every <a href="#discord.abc.GuildChannel" title="discord.abc.GuildChannel"><code>abc.GuildChannel</code></a> the client can ‘access’.

This is equivalent to:

```
for guild in client.guilds:
    for channel in guild.channels:
        yield channel

```

Note

Just because you receive a <a href="#discord.abc.GuildChannel" title="discord.abc.GuildChannel"><code>abc.GuildChannel</code></a> does not mean that you can communicate in said channel. <a href="#discord.abc.GuildChannel.permissions_for" title="discord.abc.GuildChannel.permissions_for"><code>abc.GuildChannel.permissions_for()</code></a> should be used for that.

<dl><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.abc.GuildChannel" title="discord.abc.GuildChannel"><code>abc.GuildChannel</code></a> – A channel the client can ‘access’.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*for ... in* get_all_members()<a href="#discord.Client.get_all_members" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns a generator with every <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> the client can see.

This is equivalent to:

```
for guild in client.guilds:
    for member in guild.members:
        yield member

```

<dl><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> – A member the client can see.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* wait_until_ready()<a href="#discord.Client.wait_until_ready" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Waits until the client’s internal cache is all ready.

Warning

Calling this inside <a href="#discord.Client.setup_hook" title="discord.Client.setup_hook"><code>setup_hook()</code></a> can lead to a deadlock.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>wait_for(*event*, */*, ***, *check=None*, *timeout=None*)<a href="#discord.Client.wait_for" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Waits for a WebSocket event to be dispatched.

This could be used to wait for a user to reply to a message, or to react to a message, or to edit a message in a self-contained way.

The <code>timeout</code> parameter is passed onto <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#asyncio.wait_for" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>asyncio.wait_for()</code></a>. By default, it does not timeout. Note that this does propagate the <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-exceptions.html#asyncio.TimeoutError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>asyncio.TimeoutError</code></a> for you in case of timeout and is provided for ease of use.

In case the event returns multiple arguments, a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#tuple" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>tuple</code></a> containing those arguments is returned instead. Please check the <a href="#discord-api-events">documentation</a> for a list of events and their parameters.

This function returns the **first event that meets the requirements**.

Examples

Waiting for a user reply:

```
@client.event
async def on_message(message):
    if message.content.startswith('$greet'):
        channel = message.channel
        await channel.send('Say hello!')

        def check(m):
            return m.content == 'hello' and m.channel == channel

        msg = await client.wait_for('message', check=check)
        await channel.send(f'Hello {msg.author}!')

```

Waiting for a thumbs up reaction from the message author:

```
@client.event
async def on_message(message):
    if message.content.startswith('$thumb'):
        channel = message.channel
        await channel.send('Send me that 👍 reaction, mate')

        def check(reaction, user):
            return user == message.author and str(reaction.emoji) == '👍'

        try:
            reaction, user = await client.wait_for('reaction_add', timeout=60.0, check=check)
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            await channel.send('👎')
        else:
            await channel.send('👍')

```

Changed in version 2.0: <code>event</code> parameter is now positional-only.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **event** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The event name, similar to the <a href="#discord-api-events">event reference</a>, but without the <code>on_</code> prefix, to wait for.
- **check** (Optional\[Callable\[…, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>]]) – A predicate to check what to wait for. The arguments must meet the parameters of the event being waited for.
- **timeout** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>float</code></a>]) – The number of seconds to wait before timing out and raising <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-exceptions.html#asyncio.TimeoutError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>asyncio.TimeoutError</code></a>.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-exceptions.html#asyncio.TimeoutError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**asyncio.TimeoutError**</a> – If a timeout is provided and it was reached.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

Returns no arguments, a single argument, or a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#tuple" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>tuple</code></a> of multiple arguments that mirrors the parameters passed in the <a href="#discord-api-events">event reference</a>.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

Any

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* change_presence(***, *activity=None*, *status=None*)<a href="#discord.Client.change_presence" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Changes the client’s presence.

Example

```
game = discord.Game("with the API")
await client.change_presence(status=discord.Status.idle, activity=game)

```

Changed in version 2.0: Removed the <code>afk</code> keyword-only parameter.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **activity** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.BaseActivity" title="discord.BaseActivity"><code>BaseActivity</code></a>]) – The activity being done. <code>None</code> if no currently active activity is done.
- **status** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.Status" title="discord.Status"><code>Status</code></a>]) – Indicates what status to change to. If <code>None</code>, then <a href="#discord.Status.online" title="discord.Status.online"><code>Status.online</code></a> is used.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – If the <code>activity</code> parameter is not the proper type.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*async for ... in* fetch_guilds(***, *limit=200*, *before=None*, *after=None*, *with_counts=True*)<a href="#discord.Client.fetch_guilds" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Retrieves an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterator" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterator</a> that enables receiving your guilds.

Note

Using this, you will only receive <a href="#discord.Guild.owner" title="discord.Guild.owner"><code>Guild.owner</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Guild.icon" title="discord.Guild.icon"><code>Guild.icon</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Guild.id" title="discord.Guild.id"><code>Guild.id</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Guild.name" title="discord.Guild.name"><code>Guild.name</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Guild.approximate_member_count" title="discord.Guild.approximate_member_count"><code>Guild.approximate_member_count</code></a>, and <a href="#discord.Guild.approximate_presence_count" title="discord.Guild.approximate_presence_count"><code>Guild.approximate_presence_count</code></a> per <a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a>.

Note

This method is an API call. For general usage, consider <a href="#discord.Client.guilds" title="discord.Client.guilds"><code>guilds</code></a> instead.

Examples

Usage

```
async for guild in client.fetch_guilds(limit=150):
    print(guild.name)

```

Flattening into a list

```
guilds = [guild async for guild in client.fetch_guilds(limit=150)]
# guilds is now a list of Guild...

```

All parameters are optional.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **limit** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) –

  The number of guilds to retrieve. If <code>None</code>, it retrieves every guild you have access to. Note, however, that this would make it a slow operation. Defaults to <code>200</code>.

  Changed in version 2.0: The default has been changed to 200.
- **before** (Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]) – Retrieves guilds before this date or object. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.
- **after** (Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]) – Retrieve guilds after this date or object. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.
- **with\_counts** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to include count information in the guilds. This fills the <a href="#discord.Guild.approximate_member_count" title="discord.Guild.approximate_member_count"><code>Guild.approximate_member_count</code></a> and <a href="#discord.Guild.approximate_presence_count" title="discord.Guild.approximate_presence_count"><code>Guild.approximate_presence_count</code></a> attributes without needing any privileged intents. Defaults to <code>True</code>.

  New in version 2.3.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Getting the guilds failed.

</dd><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a> – The guild with the guild data parsed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_template(*code*)<a href="#discord.Client.fetch_template" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The template is invalid.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_guild(*guild_id*, */*, ***, *with_counts=True*)<a href="#discord.Client.fetch_guild" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

Note

This method is an API call. For general usage, consider <a href="#discord.Client.get_guild" title="discord.Client.get_guild"><code>get_guild()</code></a> instead.

Changed in version 2.0: <code>guild_id</code> parameter is now positional-only.

This fills the <a href="#discord.Guild.approximate_member_count" title="discord.Guild.approximate_member_count"><code>Guild.approximate_member_count</code></a> and <a href="#discord.Guild.approximate_presence_count" title="discord.Guild.approximate_presence_count"><code>Guild.approximate_presence_count</code></a> attributes without needing any privileged intents. Defaults to <code>True</code>.

  New in version 2.0.

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Getting the guild failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>

<a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_guild_preview(*guild_id*)<a href="#discord.Client.fetch_guild_preview" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

</dl><dl><dt>*await* create_guild(***, *name*, *icon=...*, *code=...*)<a href="#discord.Client.create_guild" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_invite(*url*, ***, *with_counts=True*, *with_expiration=True*, *scheduled_event_id=None*)<a href="#discord.Client.fetch_invite" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Gets an <a href="#discord.Invite" title="discord.Invite"><code>Invite</code></a> from a discord.gg URL or ID.

Note

If the invite is for a guild you have not joined, the guild and channel attributes of the returned <a href="#discord.Invite" title="discord.Invite"><code>Invite</code></a> will be <a href="#discord.PartialInviteGuild" title="discord.PartialInviteGuild"><code>PartialInviteGuild</code></a> and <a href="#discord.PartialInviteChannel" title="discord.PartialInviteChannel"><code>PartialInviteChannel</code></a> respectively.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **url** (Union\[<a href="#discord.Invite" title="discord.Invite"><code>Invite</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The Discord invite ID or URL (must be a discord.gg URL).
- **with\_counts** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to include count information in the invite. This fills the <a href="#discord.Invite.approximate_member_count" title="discord.Invite.approximate_member_count"><code>Invite.approximate_member_count</code></a> and <a href="#discord.Invite.approximate_presence_count" title="discord.Invite.approximate_presence_count"><code>Invite.approximate_presence_count</code></a> fields.
- **with\_expiration** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to include the expiration date of the invite. This fills the <a href="#discord.Invite.expires_at" title="discord.Invite.expires_at"><code>Invite.expires_at</code></a> field.

  New in version 2.0.

  Deprecated since version 2.6: This parameter is deprecated and will be removed in a future version as it is no longer needed to fill the <a href="#discord.Invite.expires_at" title="discord.Invite.expires_at"><code>Invite.expires_at</code></a> field.
- **scheduled\_event\_id** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) –

  The ID of the scheduled event this invite is for.

  Note

  It is not possible to provide a url that contains an <code>event_id</code> parameter when using this parameter.

  New in version 2.0.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – The url contains an <code>event_id</code>, but <code>scheduled_event_id</code> has also been provided.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The invite has expired or is invalid.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Getting the invite failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The invite from the URL/ID.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Invite" title="discord.Invite"><code>Invite</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* delete_invite(*invite*, */*, ***, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Client.delete_invite" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_entitlement(*entitlement_id*, */*)<a href="#discord.Client.fetch_entitlement" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

<dd>

**entitlement\_id** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The entitlement’s ID to fetch from.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – An entitlement with this ID does not exist.
- <a href="#discord.MissingApplicationID" title="discord.MissingApplicationID">**MissingApplicationID**</a> – The application ID could not be found.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Fetching the entitlement failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The entitlement you requested.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Entitlement" title="discord.Entitlement"><code>Entitlement</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*async for ... in* entitlements(***, *limit=100*, *before=None*, *after=None*, *skus=None*, *user=None*, *guild=None*, *exclude_ended=False*, *exclude_deleted=True*)<a href="#discord.Client.entitlements" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Retrieves an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterator" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterator</a> of the <a href="#discord.Entitlement" title="discord.Entitlement"><code>Entitlement</code></a> that applications has.

New in version 2.4.

Examples

Usage

```
async for entitlement in client.entitlements(limit=100):
    print(entitlement.user_id, entitlement.ends_at)

```

Flattening into a list

```
entitlements = [entitlement async for entitlement in client.entitlements(limit=100)]
# entitlements is now a list of Entitlement...

```

All parameters are optional.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **limit** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) – The number of entitlements to retrieve. If <code>None</code>, it retrieves every entitlement for this application. Note, however, that this would make it a slow operation. Defaults to <code>100</code>.
- **before** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve entitlements before this date or entitlement. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.
- **after** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve entitlements after this date or entitlement. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.
- **skus** (Optional\[Sequence\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>]]) – A list of SKUs to filter by.
- **user** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>]) – The user to filter by.
- **guild** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>]) – The guild to filter by.
- **exclude\_ended** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to exclude ended entitlements. Defaults to <code>False</code>.
- **exclude\_deleted** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to exclude deleted entitlements. Defaults to <code>True</code>.

  New in version 2.5.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.MissingApplicationID" title="discord.MissingApplicationID">**MissingApplicationID**</a> – The application ID could not be found.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Fetching the entitlements failed.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – Both <code>after</code> and <code>before</code> were provided, as Discord does not support this type of pagination.

</dd><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Entitlement" title="discord.Entitlement"><code>Entitlement</code></a> – The entitlement with the application.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* create_entitlement(*sku*, *owner*, *owner_type*)<a href="#discord.Client.create_entitlement" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

<dl><dt>*class*discord.AutoShardedClient(**args*, *intents*, ***kwargs*)<a href="#discord.AutoShardedClient" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A client similar to <a href="#discord.Client" title="discord.Client"><code>Client</code></a> except it handles the complications of sharding for the user into a more manageable and transparent single process bot.

When using this client, you will be able to use it as-if it was a regular <a href="#discord.Client" title="discord.Client"><code>Client</code></a> with a single shard when implementation wise internally it is split up into multiple shards. This allows you to not have to deal with IPC or other complicated infrastructure.

It is recommended to use this client only if you have surpassed at least 1000 guilds.

If no <a href="#discord.ShardInfo.shard_count" title="discord.ShardInfo.shard_count"><code>shard_count</code></a> is provided, then the library will use the Bot Gateway endpoint call to figure out how many shards to use.

If a <code>shard_ids</code> parameter is given, then those shard IDs will be used to launch the internal shards. Note that <a href="#discord.ShardInfo.shard_count" title="discord.ShardInfo.shard_count"><code>shard_count</code></a> must be provided if this is used. By default, when omitted, the client will launch shards from 0 to <code>shard_count - 1</code>.

<dl><dt>async with x</dt>
<dd>

Asynchronously initialises the client and automatically cleans up.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl>

<dl><dt>shard_ids<a href="#discord.AutoShardedClient.shard_ids" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

An optional list of shard\_ids to launch the shards with.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[List\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>shard_connect_timeout<a href="#discord.AutoShardedClient.shard_connect_timeout" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The maximum number of seconds to wait before timing out when launching a shard. Defaults to 180 seconds.

New in version 2.4.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>float</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*latency<a href="#discord.AutoShardedClient.latency" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Measures latency between a HEARTBEAT and a HEARTBEAT\_ACK in seconds.

This operates similarly to <a href="#discord.Client.latency" title="discord.Client.latency"><code>Client.latency()</code></a> except it uses the average latency of every shard’s latency. To get a list of shard latency, check the <a href="#discord.AutoShardedClient.latencies" title="discord.AutoShardedClient.latencies"><code>latencies</code></a> property. Returns <code>nan</code> if there are no shards ready.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>float</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*latencies<a href="#discord.AutoShardedClient.latencies" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A list of latencies between a HEARTBEAT and a HEARTBEAT\_ACK in seconds.

This returns a list of tuples with elements <code>(shard_id, latency)</code>.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

List\[Tuple\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>float</code></a>]]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>get_shard(*shard_id*, */*)<a href="#discord.AutoShardedClient.get_shard" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Gets the shard information at a given shard ID or <code>None</code> if not found.

Changed in version 2.0: <code>shard_id</code> parameter is now positional-only.

<dl><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

Information about the shard with given ID. <code>None</code> if not found.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="#discord.ShardInfo" title="discord.ShardInfo"><code>ShardInfo</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*shards<a href="#discord.AutoShardedClient.shards" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns a mapping of shard IDs to their respective info object.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Mapping\[int, <a href="#discord.ShardInfo" title="discord.ShardInfo"><code>ShardInfo</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_session_start_limits()<a href="#discord.AutoShardedClient.fetch_session_start_limits" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Get the session start limits.

This is not typically needed, and will be handled for you by default.

At the point where you are launching multiple instances with manual shard ranges and are considered required to use large bot sharding by Discord, this function when used along IPC and a before\_identity\_hook can speed up session start.

New in version 2.5.

<dl><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

A class containing the session start limits

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.SessionStartLimits" title="discord.SessionStartLimits"><code>SessionStartLimits</code></a>

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.GatewayNotFound" title="discord.GatewayNotFound">**GatewayNotFound**</a> – The gateway was unreachable

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* connect(***, *reconnect=True*)<a href="#discord.AutoShardedClient.connect" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Creates a websocket connection and lets the websocket listen to messages from Discord. This is a loop that runs the entire event system and miscellaneous aspects of the library. Control is not resumed until the WebSocket connection is terminated.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**reconnect** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – If we should attempt reconnecting, either due to internet failure or a specific failure on Discord’s part. Certain disconnects that lead to bad state will not be handled (such as invalid sharding payloads or bad tokens).

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.GatewayNotFound" title="discord.GatewayNotFound">**GatewayNotFound**</a> – If the gateway to connect to Discord is not found. Usually if this is thrown then there is a Discord API outage.
- <a href="#discord.ConnectionClosed" title="discord.ConnectionClosed">**ConnectionClosed**</a> – The websocket connection has been terminated.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* close()<a href="#discord.AutoShardedClient.close" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Closes the connection to Discord.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*await* change_presence(***, *activity=None*, *status=None*, *shard_id=None*)<a href="#discord.AutoShardedClient.change_presence" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Changes the client’s presence.

Example:

```
game = discord.Game("with the API")
await client.change_presence(status=discord.Status.idle, activity=game)

```

Changed in version 2.0: Removed the <code>afk</code> keyword-only parameter.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **activity** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.BaseActivity" title="discord.BaseActivity"><code>BaseActivity</code></a>]) – The activity being done. <code>None</code> if no currently active activity is done.
- **status** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.Status" title="discord.Status"><code>Status</code></a>]) – Indicates what status to change to. If <code>None</code>, then <a href="#discord.Status.online" title="discord.Status.online"><code>Status.online</code></a> is used.
- **shard\_id** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) – The shard\_id to change the presence to. If not specified or <code>None</code>, then it will change the presence of every shard the bot can see.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – If the <code>activity</code> parameter is not of proper type.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>is_ws_ratelimited()<a href="#discord.AutoShardedClient.is_ws_ratelimited" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>: Whether the websocket is currently rate limited.

This can be useful to know when deciding whether you should query members using HTTP or via the gateway.

This implementation checks if any of the shards are rate limited. For more granular control, consider <a href="#discord.ShardInfo.is_ws_ratelimited" title="discord.ShardInfo.is_ws_ratelimited"><code>ShardInfo.is_ws_ratelimited()</code></a>.

New in version 1.6.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl>

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **custom\_install\_url** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The new custom authorization URL for the application. Can be <code>None</code> to remove the URL.
- **description** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The new application description. Can be <code>None</code> to remove the description.
- **role\_connections\_verification\_url** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The new application’s connection verification URL which will render the application as a verification method in the guild’s role verification configuration. Can be <code>None</code> to remove the URL.
- **install\_params\_scopes** (Optional\[List\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]]) – The new list of <a href="https://discord.com/developers/docs/topics/oauth2#shared-resources-oauth2-scopes">OAuth2 scopes</a> of the <a href="#discord.AppInfo.install_params" title="discord.AppInfo.install_params"><code>install_params</code></a>. Can be <code>None</code> to remove the scopes.
- **install\_params\_permissions** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.Permissions" title="discord.Permissions"><code>Permissions</code></a>]) – The new permissions of the <a href="#discord.AppInfo.install_params" title="discord.AppInfo.install_params"><code>install_params</code></a>. Can be <code>None</code> to remove the permissions.
- **flags** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.ApplicationFlags" title="discord.ApplicationFlags"><code>ApplicationFlags</code></a>]) –

  The new application’s flags. Only limited intent flags (<a href="#discord.ApplicationFlags.gateway_presence_limited" title="discord.ApplicationFlags.gateway_presence_limited"><code>gateway_presence_limited</code></a>, <a href="#discord.ApplicationFlags.gateway_guild_members_limited" title="discord.ApplicationFlags.gateway_guild_members_limited"><code>gateway_guild_members_limited</code></a>, <a href="#discord.ApplicationFlags.gateway_message_content_limited" title="discord.ApplicationFlags.gateway_message_content_limited"><code>gateway_message_content_limited</code></a>) can be edited. Can be <code>None</code> to remove the flags.

  Warning

  Editing the limited intent flags leads to the termination of the bot.
- **icon** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bytes</code></a>]) – The new application’s icon as a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-bytes-like-object" title="(in Python v3.14)">bytes-like object</a>. Can be <code>None</code> to remove the icon.
- **cover\_image** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bytes</code></a>]) – The new application’s cover image as a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-bytes-like-object" title="(in Python v3.14)">bytes-like object</a> on a store embed. The cover image is only available if the application is a game sold on Discord. Can be <code>None</code> to remove the image.
- **interactions\_endpoint\_url** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The new interactions endpoint url of the application to receive interactions over this endpoint rather than over the gateway. Can be <code>None</code> to remove the URL.
- **tags** (Optional\[List\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]]) – The new list of tags describing the functionality of the application. Can be <code>None</code> to remove the tags.
- **guild\_install\_scopes** (Optional\[List\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]]) –

  The new list of <a href="https://discord.com/developers/docs/topics/oauth2#shared-resources-oauth2-scopes">OAuth2 scopes</a> of the default guild installation context. Can be <code>None</code> to remove the scopes.
- **guild\_install\_permissions** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.Permissions" title="discord.Permissions"><code>Permissions</code></a>]) –

  The new permissions of the default guild installation context. Can be <code>None</code> to remove the permissions.
- **user\_install\_scopes** (Optional\[List\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]]) –

  The new list of <a href="https://discord.com/developers/docs/topics/oauth2#shared-resources-oauth2-scopes">OAuth2 scopes</a> of the default user installation context. Can be <code>None</code> to remove the scopes.
- **user\_install\_permissions** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.Permissions" title="discord.Permissions"><code>Permissions</code></a>]) –

  The new permissions of the default user installation context. Can be <code>None</code> to remove the permissions.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for editing the application. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Editing the application failed
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – The image format passed in to <code>icon</code> or <code>cover_image</code> is invalid. This is also raised when <code>install_params_scopes</code> and <code>install_params_permissions</code> are incompatible with each other, or when <code>guild_install_scopes</code> and <code>guild_install_permissions</code> are incompatible with each other.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The newly updated application info.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.AppInfo" title="discord.AppInfo"><code>AppInfo</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl>

<dl><dt>*class*discord.VoiceClient<a href="#discord.VoiceClient" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Represents a Discord voice connection.

You do not create these, you typically get them from e.g. <a href="#discord.VoiceChannel.connect" title="discord.VoiceChannel.connect"><code>VoiceChannel.connect()</code></a>.

Warning

In order to use PCM based AudioSources, you must have the opus library installed on your system and loaded through <a href="#discord.opus.load_opus" title="discord.opus.load_opus"><code>opus.load_opus()</code></a>. Otherwise, your AudioSources must be opus encoded (e.g. using <a href="#discord.FFmpegOpusAudio" title="discord.FFmpegOpusAudio"><code>FFmpegOpusAudio</code></a>) or the library will not be able to transmit audio.

  How long to wait for the move to complete.

  New in version 2.4.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-exceptions.html#asyncio.TimeoutError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**asyncio.TimeoutError**</a> – The move did not complete in time, but may still be ongoing.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>is_connected()<a href="#discord.VoiceClient.is_connected" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Indicates if the voice client is connected to voice.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>play(*source*, ***, *after=None*, *application='audio'*, *bitrate=128*, *fec=True*, *expected_packet_loss=0.15*, *bandwidth='full'*, *signal_type='auto'*)<a href="#discord.VoiceClient.play" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Plays an <a href="#discord.AudioSource" title="discord.AudioSource"><code>AudioSource</code></a>.

The finalizer, <code>after</code> is called after the source has been exhausted or an error occurred.

If an error happens while the audio player is running, the exception is caught and the audio player is then stopped. If no after callback is passed, any caught exception will be logged using the library logger.

Extra parameters may be passed to the internal opus encoder if a PCM based source is used. Otherwise, they are ignored.

Changed in version 2.0: Instead of writing to <code>sys.stderr</code>, the library’s logger is used.

Changed in version 2.4: Added encoder parameters as keyword arguments.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **source** (<a href="#discord.AudioSource" title="discord.AudioSource"><code>AudioSource</code></a>) – The audio source we’re reading from.
- **after** (Callable\[\[Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#Exception" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>Exception</code></a>]], Any]) – The finalizer that is called after the stream is exhausted. This function must have a single parameter, <code>error</code>, that denotes an optional exception that was raised during playing.
- **application** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – Configures the encoder’s intended application. Can be one of: <code>'audio'</code>, <code>'voip'</code>, <code>'lowdelay'</code>. Defaults to <code>'audio'</code>.
- **bitrate** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – Configures the bitrate in the encoder. Can be between <code>16</code> and <code>512</code>. Defaults to <code>128</code>.
- **fec** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Configures the encoder’s use of inband forward error correction. Defaults to <code>True</code>.
- **expected\_packet\_loss** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>float</code></a>) – Configures the encoder’s expected packet loss percentage. Requires FEC. Defaults to <code>0.15</code>.
- **bandwidth** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – Configures the encoder’s bandpass. Can be one of: <code>'narrow'</code>, <code>'medium'</code>, <code>'wide'</code>, <code>'superwide'</code>, <code>'full'</code>. Defaults to <code>'full'</code>.
- **signal\_type** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – Configures the type of signal being encoded. Can be one of: <code>'auto'</code>, <code>'voice'</code>, <code>'music'</code>. Defaults to <code>'auto'</code>.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.ClientException" title="discord.ClientException">**ClientException**</a> – Already playing audio or not connected.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – Source is not a <a href="#discord.AudioSource" title="discord.AudioSource"><code>AudioSource</code></a> or after is not a callable.
- <a href="#discord.opus.OpusNotLoaded" title="discord.opus.OpusNotLoaded">**OpusNotLoaded**</a> – Source is not opus encoded and opus is not loaded.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – An improper value was passed as an encoder parameter.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>is_playing()<a href="#discord.VoiceClient.is_playing" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Indicates if we’re currently playing audio.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>is_paused()<a href="#discord.VoiceClient.is_paused" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

</dd></dl><dl><dt>resume()<a href="#discord.VoiceClient.resume" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="#discord.AudioSource" title="discord.AudioSource"><code>AudioSource</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>send_audio_packet(*data*, ***, *encode=True*)<a href="#discord.VoiceClient.send_audio_packet" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Sends an audio packet composed of the data.

You must be connected to play audio.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **data** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bytes</code></a>) – The <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-bytes-like-object" title="(in Python v3.14)">bytes-like object</a> denoting PCM or Opus voice data.
- **encode** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Indicates if <code>data</code> should be encoded into Opus.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.ClientException" title="discord.ClientException">**ClientException**</a> – You are not connected.
- <a href="#discord.opus.OpusError" title="discord.opus.OpusError">**opus.OpusError**</a> – Encoding the data failed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl>

<dl><dt>*class*discord.VoiceProtocol(*client*, *channel*)<a href="#discord.VoiceProtocol" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A class that represents the Discord voice protocol.

This is an abstract class. The library provides a concrete implementation under <a href="#discord.VoiceClient" title="discord.VoiceClient"><code>VoiceClient</code></a>.

This class allows you to implement a protocol to allow for an external method of sending voice, such as <a href="https://github.com/freyacodes/Lavalink">Lavalink</a> or a native library implementation.

These classes are passed to <a href="#discord.VoiceChannel.connect" title="discord.VoiceChannel.connect"><code>abc.Connectable.connect</code></a>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **client** (<a href="#discord.Client" title="discord.Client"><code>Client</code></a>) – The client (or its subclasses) that started the connection request.
- **channel** (<a href="#discord.abc.Connectable" title="discord.abc.Connectable"><code>abc.Connectable</code></a>) – The voice channel that is being connected to.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*await* on_voice_state_update(*data*, */*)<a href="#discord.VoiceProtocol.on_voice_state_update" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

An abstract method that is called when the client’s voice state has changed. This corresponds to <code>VOICE_STATE_UPDATE</code>.

Warning

This method is not the same as the event. See: <a href="#discord.on_voice_state_update" title="discord.on_voice_state_update"><code>on_voice_state_update()</code></a>

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**data** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>dict</code></a>) – The raw <a href="https://discord.com/developers/docs/resources/voice#voice-state-object">voice state payload</a>.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* on_voice_server_update(*data*, */*)<a href="#discord.VoiceProtocol.on_voice_server_update" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

An abstract method that is called when initially connecting to voice. This corresponds to <code>VOICE_SERVER_UPDATE</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**data** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>dict</code></a>) – The raw <a href="https://discord.com/developers/docs/topics/gateway-events#voice-server-update">voice server update payload</a>.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* connect(***, *timeout*, *reconnect*, *self_deaf=False*, *self_mute=False*)<a href="#discord.VoiceProtocol.connect" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

An abstract method called when the client initiates the connection request.

When a connection is requested initially, the library calls the constructor under <code>__init__</code> and then calls <a href="#discord.VoiceProtocol.connect" title="discord.VoiceProtocol.connect"><code>connect()</code></a>. If <a href="#discord.VoiceProtocol.connect" title="discord.VoiceProtocol.connect"><code>connect()</code></a> fails at some point then <a href="#discord.VoiceProtocol.disconnect" title="discord.VoiceProtocol.disconnect"><code>disconnect()</code></a> is called.

Within this method, to start the voice connection flow it is recommended to use <a href="#discord.Guild.change_voice_state" title="discord.Guild.change_voice_state"><code>Guild.change_voice_state()</code></a> to start the flow. After which, <a href="#discord.VoiceProtocol.on_voice_server_update" title="discord.VoiceProtocol.on_voice_server_update"><code>on_voice_server_update()</code></a> and <a href="#discord.on_voice_state_update" title="discord.on_voice_state_update"><code>on_voice_state_update()</code></a> will be called. The order that these two are called is unspecified.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **timeout** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>float</code></a>) – The timeout for the connection.
- **reconnect** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether reconnection is expected.
- **self\_mute** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Indicates if the client should be self-muted.

- **self\_deaf** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Indicates if the client should be self-deafened.

  New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* disconnect(***, *force*)<a href="#discord.VoiceProtocol.disconnect" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

An abstract method called when the client terminates the connection.

See <a href="#discord.VoiceProtocol.cleanup" title="discord.VoiceProtocol.cleanup"><code>cleanup()</code></a>.

**force** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether the disconnection was forced.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>cleanup()<a href="#discord.VoiceProtocol.cleanup" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This method *must* be called to ensure proper clean-up during a disconnect.

It is advisable to call this from within <a href="#discord.VoiceProtocol.disconnect" title="discord.VoiceProtocol.disconnect"><code>disconnect()</code></a> when you are completely done with the voice protocol instance.

This method removes it from the internal state cache that keeps track of currently alive voice clients. Failure to clean-up will cause subsequent connections to report that it’s still connected.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl>

<dl><dt>*class*discord.AudioSource<a href="#discord.AudioSource" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Represents an audio stream.

The audio stream can be Opus encoded or not, however if the audio stream is not Opus encoded then the audio format must be 16-bit 48KHz stereo PCM.

Warning

The audio source reads are done in a separate thread.

<dl><dt>read()<a href="#discord.AudioSource.read" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Reads 20ms worth of audio.

Subclasses must implement this.

If the audio is complete, then returning an empty <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-bytes-like-object" title="(in Python v3.14)">bytes-like object</a> to signal this is the way to do so.

If <a href="#discord.AudioSource.is_opus" title="discord.AudioSource.is_opus"><code>is_opus()</code></a> method returns <code>True</code>, then it must return 20ms worth of Opus encoded audio. Otherwise, it must be 20ms worth of 16-bit 48KHz stereo PCM, which is about 3,840 bytes per frame (20ms worth of audio).

<dl><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

A bytes like object that represents the PCM or Opus data.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bytes</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>is_opus()<a href="#discord.AudioSource.is_opus" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Checks if the audio source is already encoded in Opus.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>cleanup()<a href="#discord.AudioSource.cleanup" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when clean-up is needed to be done.

Useful for clearing buffer data or processes after it is done playing audio.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl>

### FFmpegOpusAudio ¶

Methods

- cls [FFmpegOpusAudio.probe](#discord.FFmpegOpusAudio.probe)
