<dl><dt>*class*discord.FFmpegOpusAudio(*source*, ***, *bitrate=None*, *codec=None*, *executable='ffmpeg'*, *pipe=False*, *stderr=None*, *before_options=None*, *options=None*)<a href="#discord.FFmpegOpusAudio" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

An audio source from FFmpeg (or AVConv).

This launches a sub-process to a specific input file given. However, rather than producing PCM packets like <a href="#discord.FFmpegPCMAudio" title="discord.FFmpegPCMAudio"><code>FFmpegPCMAudio</code></a> does that need to be encoded to Opus, this class produces Opus packets, skipping the encoding step done by the library.

Alternatively, instead of instantiating this class directly, you can use <a href="#discord.FFmpegOpusAudio.from_probe" title="discord.FFmpegOpusAudio.from_probe"><code>FFmpegOpusAudio.from_probe()</code></a> to probe for bitrate and codec information. This can be used to opportunistically skip pointless re-encoding of existing Opus audio data for a boost in performance at the cost of a short initial delay to gather the information. The same can be achieved by passing <code>copy</code> to the <code>codec</code> parameter, but only if you know that the input source is Opus encoded beforehand.

New in version 1.3.

Warning

You must have the ffmpeg or avconv executable in your path environment variable in order for this to work.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **source** (Union\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/io.html#io.BufferedIOBase" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>io.BufferedIOBase</code></a>]) – The input that ffmpeg will take and convert to Opus bytes. If <code>pipe</code> is <code>True</code> then this is a file-like object that is passed to the stdin of ffmpeg.
- **bitrate** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The bitrate in kbps to encode the output to. Defaults to <code>128</code>.
- **codec** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) –

  The codec to use to encode the audio data. Normally this would be just <code>libopus</code>, but is used by <a href="#discord.FFmpegOpusAudio.from_probe" title="discord.FFmpegOpusAudio.from_probe"><code>FFmpegOpusAudio.from_probe()</code></a> to opportunistically skip pointlessly re-encoding Opus audio data by passing <code>copy</code> as the codec value. Any values other than <code>copy</code>, <code>opus</code>, or <code>libopus</code> will be considered <code>libopus</code>. Defaults to <code>libopus</code>.

  Warning

  Do not provide this parameter unless you are certain that the audio input is already Opus encoded. For typical use <a href="#discord.FFmpegOpusAudio.from_probe" title="discord.FFmpegOpusAudio.from_probe"><code>FFmpegOpusAudio.from_probe()</code></a> should be used to determine the proper value for this parameter.
- **executable** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) –

  The executable name (and path) to use. Defaults to <code>ffmpeg</code>.

  Warning

  Since this class spawns a subprocess, care should be taken to not pass in an arbitrary executable name when using this parameter.
- **pipe** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – If <code>True</code>, denotes that <code>source</code> parameter will be passed to the stdin of ffmpeg. Defaults to <code>False</code>.
- **stderr** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-file-object" title="(in Python v3.14)">file object</a>]) – A file-like object to pass to the Popen constructor.
- **before\_options** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – Extra command line arguments to pass to ffmpeg before the <code>-i</code> flag.
- **options** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – Extra command line arguments to pass to ffmpeg after the <code>-i</code> flag.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.ClientException" title="discord.ClientException">**ClientException**</a> – The subprocess failed to be created.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*classmethod await* from_probe(*source*, ***, *method=None*, ***kwargs*)<a href="#discord.FFmpegOpusAudio.from_probe" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

A factory method that creates a <a href="#discord.FFmpegOpusAudio" title="discord.FFmpegOpusAudio"><code>FFmpegOpusAudio</code></a> after probing the input source for audio codec and bitrate information.

Examples

Use this function to create an <a href="#discord.FFmpegOpusAudio" title="discord.FFmpegOpusAudio"><code>FFmpegOpusAudio</code></a> instance instead of the constructor:

```
source = await discord.FFmpegOpusAudio.from_probe("song.webm")
voice_client.play(source)

```

If you are on Windows and don’t have ffprobe installed, use the <code>fallback</code> method to probe using ffmpeg instead:

```
source = await discord.FFmpegOpusAudio.from_probe("song.webm", method='fallback')
voice_client.play(source)

```

Using a custom method of determining codec and bitrate:

```
def custom_probe(source, executable):
    # some analysis code here
    return codec, bitrate

source = await discord.FFmpegOpusAudio.from_probe("song.webm", method=custom_probe)
voice_client.play(source)

```

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **source** – Identical to the <code>source</code> parameter for the constructor.
- **method** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>, Callable\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]]]) – The probing method used to determine bitrate and codec information. As a string, valid values are <code>native</code> to use ffprobe (or avprobe) and <code>fallback</code> to use ffmpeg (or avconv). As a callable, it must take two string arguments, <code>source</code> and <code>executable</code>. Both parameters are the same values passed to this factory function. <code>executable</code> will default to <code>ffmpeg</code> if not provided as a keyword argument.
- **kwargs** – The remaining parameters to be passed to the <a href="#discord.FFmpegOpusAudio" title="discord.FFmpegOpusAudio"><code>FFmpegOpusAudio</code></a> constructor, excluding <code>bitrate</code> and <code>codec</code>.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#AttributeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**AttributeError**</a> – Invalid probe method, must be <code>'native'</code> or <code>'fallback'</code>.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – Invalid value for <code>probe</code> parameter, must be <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a> or a callable.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

An instance of this class.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.FFmpegOpusAudio" title="discord.FFmpegOpusAudio"><code>FFmpegOpusAudio</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*classmethod await* probe(*source*, ***, *method=None*, *executable=None*)<a href="#discord.FFmpegOpusAudio.probe" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

- **method** – Identical to the <code>method</code> parameter for <a href="#discord.FFmpegOpusAudio.from_probe" title="discord.FFmpegOpusAudio.from_probe"><code>FFmpegOpusAudio.from_probe()</code></a>.
- **executable** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – Identical to the <code>executable</code> parameter for <a href="#discord.FFmpegOpusAudio" title="discord.FFmpegOpusAudio"><code>FFmpegOpusAudio</code></a>.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>

</dl><dl><dt>read()<a href="#discord.FFmpegOpusAudio.read" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

### Opus Library ¶

<dl><dt>discord.opus.load_opus(*name*)<a href="#discord.opus.load_opus" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Loads the libopus shared library for use with voice.

If this function is not called then the library uses the function <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/ctypes.html#ctypes.util.find_library" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>ctypes.util.find_library()</code></a> and then loads that one if available.

Not loading a library and attempting to use PCM based AudioSources will lead to voice not working.

This function propagates the exceptions thrown.

Warning

The bitness of the library must match the bitness of your python interpreter. If the library is 64-bit then your python interpreter must be 64-bit as well. Usually if there’s a mismatch in bitness then the load will throw an exception.

Note

On Windows, this function should not need to be called as the binaries are automatically loaded.

Note

On Windows, the .dll extension is not necessary. However, on Linux the full extension is required to load the library, e.g. <code>libopus.so.1</code>. On Linux however, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/ctypes.html#ctypes.util.find_library" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>ctypes.util.find_library()</code></a> will usually find the library automatically without you having to call this.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The filename of the shared library.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.opus.is_loaded()<a href="#discord.opus.is_loaded" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Function to check if opus lib is successfully loaded either via the <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/ctypes.html#ctypes.util.find_library" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>ctypes.util.find_library()</code></a> call of <a href="#discord.opus.load_opus" title="discord.opus.load_opus"><code>load_opus()</code></a>.

This must return <code>True</code> for voice to work.

<dl><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

Indicates if the opus library has been loaded.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl>

## Event Reference ¶

This section outlines the different types of events listened by [`Client`](#discord.Client "discord.Client").

There are two ways to register an event, the first way is through the use of [`Client.event()`](#discord.Client.event "discord.Client.event"). The second way is through subclassing [`Client`](#discord.Client "discord.Client") and overriding the specific events. For example:

```
import discord

class MyClient(discord.Client):
    async def on_message(self, message):
        if message.author == self.user:
            return

        if message.content.startswith('$hello'):
            await message.channel.send('Hello World!')

```

If an event handler raises an exception, [`on_error()`](#discord.on_error "discord.on_error") will be called to handle it, which defaults to logging the traceback and ignoring the exception.

Warning

All the events must be a [*coroutine*](https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine). If they aren’t, then you might get unexpected errors. In order to turn a function into a coroutine they must be `async def` functions.

### Connection ¶

<dl><dt>discord.on_connect()<a href="#discord.on_connect" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when the client has successfully connected to Discord. This is not the same as the client being fully prepared, see <a href="#discord.on_ready" title="discord.on_ready"><code>on_ready()</code></a> for that.

The warnings on <a href="#discord.on_ready" title="discord.on_ready"><code>on_ready()</code></a> also apply.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>discord.on_disconnect()<a href="#discord.on_disconnect" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when the client has disconnected from Discord, or a connection attempt to Discord has failed. This could happen either through the internet being disconnected, explicit calls to close, or Discord terminating the connection one way or the other.

This function can be called many times without a corresponding <a href="#discord.on_connect" title="discord.on_connect"><code>on_connect()</code></a> call.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>discord.on_shard_connect(*shard_id*)<a href="#discord.on_shard_connect" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Similar to <a href="#discord.on_connect" title="discord.on_connect"><code>on_connect()</code></a> except used by <a href="#discord.AutoShardedClient" title="discord.AutoShardedClient"><code>AutoShardedClient</code></a> to denote when a particular shard ID has connected to Discord.

New in version 1.4.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**shard\_id** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The shard ID that has connected.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_shard_disconnect(*shard_id*)<a href="#discord.on_shard_disconnect" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Similar to <a href="#discord.on_disconnect" title="discord.on_disconnect"><code>on_disconnect()</code></a> except used by <a href="#discord.AutoShardedClient" title="discord.AutoShardedClient"><code>AutoShardedClient</code></a> to denote when a particular shard ID has disconnected from Discord.

New in version 1.4.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**shard\_id** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The shard ID that has disconnected.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl>

### Debug ¶

<dl><dt>discord.on_error(*event*, **args*, ***kwargs*)<a href="#discord.on_error" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Usually when an event raises an uncaught exception, a traceback is logged to stderr and the exception is ignored. If you want to change this behaviour and handle the exception for whatever reason yourself, this event can be overridden. Which, when done, will suppress the default action of printing the traceback.

The information of the exception raised and the exception itself can be retrieved with a standard call to <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/sys.html#sys.exc_info" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>sys.exc_info()</code></a>.

Note

<code>on_error</code> will only be dispatched to <a href="#discord.Client.event" title="discord.Client.event"><code>Client.event()</code></a>.

It will not be received by <a href="#discord.Client.wait_for" title="discord.Client.wait_for"><code>Client.wait_for()</code></a>, or, if used, <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/ext/commands/api.html#ext-commands-api-bot">Bots</a> listeners such as <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/ext/commands/api.html#discord.ext.commands.Bot.listen" title="discord.ext.commands.Bot.listen"><code>listen()</code></a> or <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/ext/commands/api.html#discord.ext.commands.Cog.listener" title="discord.ext.commands.Cog.listener"><code>listener()</code></a>.

Changed in version 2.0: The traceback is now logged rather than printed.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **event** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The name of the event that raised the exception.
- **args** – The positional arguments for the event that raised the exception.
- **kwargs** – The keyword arguments for the event that raised the exception.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_socket_event_type(*event_type*)<a href="#discord.on_socket_event_type" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called whenever a websocket event is received from the WebSocket.

This is mainly useful for logging how many events you are receiving from the Discord gateway.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**event\_type** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The event type from Discord that is received, e.g. <code>'READY'</code>.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_socket_raw_receive(*msg*)<a href="#discord.on_socket_raw_receive" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called whenever a message is completely received from the WebSocket, before it’s processed and parsed. This event is always dispatched when a complete message is received and the passed data is not parsed in any way.

This is only really useful for grabbing the WebSocket stream and debugging purposes.

This requires setting the <code>enable_debug_events</code> setting in the <a href="#discord.Client" title="discord.Client"><code>Client</code></a>.

Note

This is only for the messages received from the client WebSocket. The voice WebSocket will not trigger this event.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**msg** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The message passed in from the WebSocket library.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_socket_raw_send(*payload*)<a href="#discord.on_socket_raw_send" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called whenever a send operation is done on the WebSocket before the message is sent. The passed parameter is the message that is being sent to the WebSocket.

This is only really useful for grabbing the WebSocket stream and debugging purposes.

This requires setting the <code>enable_debug_events</code> setting in the <a href="#discord.Client" title="discord.Client"><code>Client</code></a>.

Note

This is only for the messages sent from the client WebSocket. The voice WebSocket will not trigger this event.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**payload** (Union\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bytes</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The message that is about to be passed on to the WebSocket library. It can be <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bytes</code></a> to denote a binary message or <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a> to denote a regular text message.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl>

### Gateway ¶

<dl><dt>discord.on_ready()<a href="#discord.on_ready" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when the client is done preparing the data received from Discord. Usually after login is successful and the <a href="#discord.Client.guilds" title="discord.Client.guilds"><code>Client.guilds</code></a> and co. are filled up.

Warning

This function is not guaranteed to be the first event called. Likewise, this function is **not** guaranteed to only be called once. This library implements reconnection logic and thus will end up calling this event whenever a RESUME request fails.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>discord.on_resumed()<a href="#discord.on_resumed" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when the client has resumed a session.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>discord.on_shard_ready(*shard_id*)<a href="#discord.on_shard_ready" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Similar to <a href="#discord.on_ready" title="discord.on_ready"><code>on_ready()</code></a> except used by <a href="#discord.AutoShardedClient" title="discord.AutoShardedClient"><code>AutoShardedClient</code></a> to denote when a particular shard ID has become ready.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**shard\_id** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The shard ID that is ready.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_shard_resumed(*shard_id*)<a href="#discord.on_shard_resumed" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Similar to <a href="#discord.on_resumed" title="discord.on_resumed"><code>on_resumed()</code></a> except used by <a href="#discord.AutoShardedClient" title="discord.AutoShardedClient"><code>AutoShardedClient</code></a> to denote when a particular shard ID has resumed a session.

New in version 1.4.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**shard\_id** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The shard ID that has resumed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl>

### Guilds ¶

<dl><dt>discord.on_guild_available(*guild*)<a href="#discord.on_guild_available" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dt>discord.on_guild_unavailable(*guild*)<a href="#discord.on_guild_unavailable" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a guild becomes available or unavailable. The guild must have existed in the <a href="#discord.Client.guilds" title="discord.Client.guilds"><code>Client.guilds</code></a> cache.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.guilds" title="discord.Intents.guilds"><code>Intents.guilds</code></a> to be enabled.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**guild** – The <a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a> that has changed availability.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_guild_join(*guild*)<a href="#discord.on_guild_join" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a <a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a> is either created by the <a href="#discord.Client" title="discord.Client"><code>Client</code></a> or when the <a href="#discord.Client" title="discord.Client"><code>Client</code></a> joins a guild.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.guilds" title="discord.Intents.guilds"><code>Intents.guilds</code></a> to be enabled.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**guild** (<a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a>) – The guild that was joined.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_guild_remove(*guild*)<a href="#discord.on_guild_remove" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a <a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a> is removed from the <a href="#discord.Client" title="discord.Client"><code>Client</code></a>.

This happens through, but not limited to, these circumstances:

- The client got banned.
- The client got kicked.
- The client left the guild.
- The client or the guild owner deleted the guild.

In order for this event to be invoked then the <a href="#discord.Client" title="discord.Client"><code>Client</code></a> must have been part of the guild to begin with. (i.e. it is part of <a href="#discord.Client.guilds" title="discord.Client.guilds"><code>Client.guilds</code></a>)

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.guilds" title="discord.Intents.guilds"><code>Intents.guilds</code></a> to be enabled.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**guild** (<a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a>) – The guild that got removed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_guild_update(*before*, *after*)<a href="#discord.on_guild_update" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a <a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a> updates, for example:

- Changed name
- Changed AFK channel
- Changed AFK timeout
- etc

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.guilds" title="discord.Intents.guilds"><code>Intents.guilds</code></a> to be enabled.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **before** (<a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a>) – The guild prior to being updated.
- **after** (<a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a>) – The guild after being updated.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_guild_emojis_update(*guild*, *before*, *after*)<a href="#discord.on_guild_emojis_update" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a <a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a> adds or removes <a href="#discord.Emoji" title="discord.Emoji"><code>Emoji</code></a>.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.emojis_and_stickers" title="discord.Intents.emojis_and_stickers"><code>Intents.emojis_and_stickers</code></a> to be enabled.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **guild** (<a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a>) – The guild who got their emojis updated.
- **before** (Sequence\[<a href="#discord.Emoji" title="discord.Emoji"><code>Emoji</code></a>]) – A list of emojis before the update.
- **after** (Sequence\[<a href="#discord.Emoji" title="discord.Emoji"><code>Emoji</code></a>]) – A list of emojis after the update.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_guild_stickers_update(*guild*, *before*, *after*)<a href="#discord.on_guild_stickers_update" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a <a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a> updates its stickers.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.emojis_and_stickers" title="discord.Intents.emojis_and_stickers"><code>Intents.emojis_and_stickers</code></a> to be enabled.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **guild** (<a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a>) – The guild who got their stickers updated.
- **before** (Sequence\[<a href="#discord.GuildSticker" title="discord.GuildSticker"><code>GuildSticker</code></a>]) – A list of stickers before the update.
- **after** (Sequence\[<a href="#discord.GuildSticker" title="discord.GuildSticker"><code>GuildSticker</code></a>]) – A list of stickers after the update.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_audit_log_entry_create(*entry*)<a href="#discord.on_audit_log_entry_create" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a <a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a> gets a new audit log entry. You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.view_audit_log" title="discord.Permissions.view_audit_log"><code>view_audit_log</code></a> to receive this.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.moderation" title="discord.Intents.moderation"><code>Intents.moderation</code></a> to be enabled.

New in version 2.2.

Warning

Audit log entries received through the gateway are subject to data retrieval from cache rather than REST. This means that some data might not be present when you expect it to be. For example, the <a href="#discord.AuditLogEntry.target" title="discord.AuditLogEntry.target"><code>AuditLogEntry.target</code></a> attribute will usually be a <a href="#discord.Object" title="discord.Object"><code>discord.Object</code></a> and the <a href="#discord.AuditLogEntry.user" title="discord.AuditLogEntry.user"><code>AuditLogEntry.user</code></a> attribute will depend on user and member cache.

To get the user ID of entry, <a href="#discord.AuditLogEntry.user_id" title="discord.AuditLogEntry.user_id"><code>AuditLogEntry.user_id</code></a> can be used instead.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**entry** (<a href="#discord.AuditLogEntry" title="discord.AuditLogEntry"><code>AuditLogEntry</code></a>) – The audit log entry that was created.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_invite_create(*invite*)<a href="#discord.on_invite_create" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when an <a href="#discord.Invite" title="discord.Invite"><code>Invite</code></a> is created. You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_channels" title="discord.Permissions.manage_channels"><code>manage_channels</code></a> to receive this.

New in version 1.3.

Note

There is a rare possibility that the <a href="#discord.Invite.guild" title="discord.Invite.guild"><code>Invite.guild</code></a> and <a href="#discord.Invite.channel" title="discord.Invite.channel"><code>Invite.channel</code></a> attributes will be of <a href="#discord.Object" title="discord.Object"><code>Object</code></a> rather than the respective models.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.invites" title="discord.Intents.invites"><code>Intents.invites</code></a> to be enabled.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**invite** (<a href="#discord.Invite" title="discord.Invite"><code>Invite</code></a>) – The invite that was created.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_invite_delete(*invite*)<a href="#discord.on_invite_delete" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when an <a href="#discord.Invite" title="discord.Invite"><code>Invite</code></a> is deleted. You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_channels" title="discord.Permissions.manage_channels"><code>manage_channels</code></a> to receive this.

New in version 1.3.

Note

There is a rare possibility that the <a href="#discord.Invite.guild" title="discord.Invite.guild"><code>Invite.guild</code></a> and <a href="#discord.Invite.channel" title="discord.Invite.channel"><code>Invite.channel</code></a> attributes will be of <a href="#discord.Object" title="discord.Object"><code>Object</code></a> rather than the respective models.

Outside of those two attributes, the only other attribute guaranteed to be filled by the Discord gateway for this event is <a href="#discord.Invite.code" title="discord.Invite.code"><code>Invite.code</code></a>.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.invites" title="discord.Intents.invites"><code>Intents.invites</code></a> to be enabled.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**invite** (<a href="#discord.Invite" title="discord.Invite"><code>Invite</code></a>) – The invite that was deleted.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl>

### Members ¶

<dl><dt>discord.on_member_join(*member*)<a href="#discord.on_member_join" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> joins a <a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a>.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.members" title="discord.Intents.members"><code>Intents.members</code></a> to be enabled.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**member** (<a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>) – The member who joined.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_member_remove(*member*)<a href="#discord.on_member_remove" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> leaves a <a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a>.

If the guild or member could not be found in the internal cache this event will not be called, you may use <a href="#discord.on_raw_member_remove" title="discord.on_raw_member_remove"><code>on_raw_member_remove()</code></a> instead.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.members" title="discord.Intents.members"><code>Intents.members</code></a> to be enabled.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**member** (<a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>) – The member who left.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_raw_member_remove(*payload*)<a href="#discord.on_raw_member_remove" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> leaves a <a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a>.

Unlike <a href="#discord.on_member_remove" title="discord.on_member_remove"><code>on_member_remove()</code></a> this is called regardless of the guild or member being in the internal cache.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.members" title="discord.Intents.members"><code>Intents.members</code></a> to be enabled.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**payload** (<a href="#discord.RawMemberRemoveEvent" title="discord.RawMemberRemoveEvent"><code>RawMemberRemoveEvent</code></a>) – The raw event payload data.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_member_update(*before*, *after*)<a href="#discord.on_member_update" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> updates their profile.

This is called when one or more of the following things change:

- nickname
- roles
- pending
- timeout
- guild avatar
- flags

Due to a Discord limitation, this event is not dispatched when a member’s timeout expires.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.members" title="discord.Intents.members"><code>Intents.members</code></a> to be enabled.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **before** (<a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>) – The updated member’s old info.
- **after** (<a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>) – The updated member’s updated info.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_user_update(*before*, *after*)<a href="#discord.on_user_update" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a <a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a> updates their profile.

This is called when one or more of the following things change:

- avatar
- username
- discriminator
- primary guild

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.members" title="discord.Intents.members"><code>Intents.members</code></a> to be enabled.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **before** (<a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a>) – The updated user’s old info.
- **after** (<a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a>) – The updated user’s updated info.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_member_ban(*guild*, *user*)<a href="#discord.on_member_ban" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a user gets banned from a <a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a>.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.moderation" title="discord.Intents.moderation"><code>Intents.moderation</code></a> to be enabled.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **guild** (<a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a>) – The guild the user got banned from.
- **user** (Union\[<a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>]) – The user that got banned. Can be either <a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a> or <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> depending if the user was in the guild or not at the time of removal.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_member_unban(*guild*, *user*)<a href="#discord.on_member_unban" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a <a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a> gets unbanned from a <a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a>.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.moderation" title="discord.Intents.moderation"><code>Intents.moderation</code></a> to be enabled.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **guild** (<a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a>) – The guild the user got unbanned from.
- **user** (<a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a>) – The user that got unbanned.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_presence_update(*before*, *after*)<a href="#discord.on_presence_update" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> updates their presence.

This is called when one or more of the following things change:

- status
- activity

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.presences" title="discord.Intents.presences"><code>Intents.presences</code></a> and <a href="#discord.Intents.members" title="discord.Intents.members"><code>Intents.members</code></a> to be enabled.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **before** (<a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>) – The updated member’s old info.
- **after** (<a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>) – The updated member’s updated info.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_raw_presence_update(*payload*)<a href="#discord.on_raw_presence_update" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> updates their presence.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.presences" title="discord.Intents.presences"><code>Intents.presences</code></a> to be enabled.

Unlike <a href="#discord.on_presence_update" title="discord.on_presence_update"><code>on_presence_update()</code></a>, when enabled, this is called regardless of the state of internal guild and member caches, and **does not** provide a comparison between the previous and updated states of the <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>.

Important

By default, this event is only dispatched when <a href="#discord.Intents.presences" title="discord.Intents.presences"><code>Intents.presences</code></a> is enabled **and** <a href="#discord.Intents.members" title="discord.Intents.members"><code>Intents.members</code></a> is disabled.

You can manually override this behaviour by setting the **enable\_raw\_presences** flag in the <a href="#discord.Client" title="discord.Client"><code>Client</code></a>, however <a href="#discord.Intents.presences" title="discord.Intents.presences"><code>Intents.presences</code></a> is always required for this event to work.

New in version 2.5.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**payload** (<a href="#discord.RawPresenceUpdateEvent" title="discord.RawPresenceUpdateEvent"><code>RawPresenceUpdateEvent</code></a>) – The raw presence update event model.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl>

### Messages ¶

<dl><dt>discord.on_message(*message*)<a href="#discord.on_message" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> is created and sent.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.messages" title="discord.Intents.messages"><code>Intents.messages</code></a> to be enabled.

Warning

Your bot’s own messages and private messages are sent through this event. This can lead cases of ‘recursion’ depending on how your bot was programmed. If you want the bot to not reply to itself, consider checking the user IDs. Note that <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/ext/commands/api.html#discord.ext.commands.Bot" title="discord.ext.commands.Bot"><code>Bot</code></a> does not have this problem.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**message** (<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>) – The current message.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_message_edit(*before*, *after*)<a href="#discord.on_message_edit" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> receives an update event. If the message is not found in the internal message cache, then these events will not be called. Messages might not be in cache if the message is too old or the client is participating in high traffic guilds.

If this occurs increase the <a href="#discord.Client" title="discord.Client"><code>max_messages</code></a> parameter or use the <a href="#discord.on_raw_message_edit" title="discord.on_raw_message_edit"><code>on_raw_message_edit()</code></a> event instead.

The following non-exhaustive cases trigger this event:

- A message has been pinned or unpinned.
- The message content has been changed.
- The message has received an embed.
  > - For performance reasons, the embed server does not do this in a “consistent” manner.
- The message’s embeds were suppressed or unsuppressed.
- A call message has received an update to its participants or ending time.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.messages" title="discord.Intents.messages"><code>Intents.messages</code></a> to be enabled.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **before** (<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>) – The previous version of the message.
- **after** (<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>) – The current version of the message.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_message_delete(*message*)<a href="#discord.on_message_delete" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a message is deleted. If the message is not found in the internal message cache, then this event will not be called. Messages might not be in cache if the message is too old or the client is participating in high traffic guilds.

If this occurs increase the <a href="#discord.Client" title="discord.Client"><code>max_messages</code></a> parameter or use the <a href="#discord.on_raw_message_delete" title="discord.on_raw_message_delete"><code>on_raw_message_delete()</code></a> event instead.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.messages" title="discord.Intents.messages"><code>Intents.messages</code></a> to be enabled.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**message** (<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>) – The deleted message.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_bulk_message_delete(*messages*)<a href="#discord.on_bulk_message_delete" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when messages are bulk deleted. If none of the messages deleted are found in the internal message cache, then this event will not be called. If individual messages were not found in the internal message cache, this event will still be called, but the messages not found will not be included in the messages list. Messages might not be in cache if the message is too old or the client is participating in high traffic guilds.

If this occurs increase the <a href="#discord.Client" title="discord.Client"><code>max_messages</code></a> parameter or use the <a href="#discord.on_raw_bulk_message_delete" title="discord.on_raw_bulk_message_delete"><code>on_raw_bulk_message_delete()</code></a> event instead.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.messages" title="discord.Intents.messages"><code>Intents.messages</code></a> to be enabled.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**messages** (List\[<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>]) – The messages that have been deleted.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_raw_message_edit(*payload*)<a href="#discord.on_raw_message_edit" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a message is edited. Unlike <a href="#discord.on_message_edit" title="discord.on_message_edit"><code>on_message_edit()</code></a>, this is called regardless of the state of the internal message cache.

If the message is found in the message cache, it can be accessed via <a href="#discord.RawMessageUpdateEvent.cached_message" title="discord.RawMessageUpdateEvent.cached_message"><code>RawMessageUpdateEvent.cached_message</code></a>. The cached message represents the message before it has been edited. For example, if the content of a message is modified and triggers the <a href="#discord.on_raw_message_edit" title="discord.on_raw_message_edit"><code>on_raw_message_edit()</code></a> coroutine, the <a href="#discord.RawMessageUpdateEvent.cached_message" title="discord.RawMessageUpdateEvent.cached_message"><code>RawMessageUpdateEvent.cached_message</code></a> will return a <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> object that represents the message before the content was modified.

Due to the inherently raw nature of this event, the data parameter coincides with the raw data given by the <a href="https://discord.com/developers/docs/topics/gateway-events#message-update">gateway</a>.

Since the data payload can be partial, care must be taken when accessing stuff in the dictionary. One example of a common case of partial data is when the <code>'content'</code> key is inaccessible. This denotes an “embed” only edit, which is an edit in which only the embeds are updated by the Discord embed server.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.messages" title="discord.Intents.messages"><code>Intents.messages</code></a> to be enabled.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**payload** (<a href="#discord.RawMessageUpdateEvent" title="discord.RawMessageUpdateEvent"><code>RawMessageUpdateEvent</code></a>) – The raw event payload data.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_raw_message_delete(*payload*)<a href="#discord.on_raw_message_delete" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a message is deleted. Unlike <a href="#discord.on_message_delete" title="discord.on_message_delete"><code>on_message_delete()</code></a>, this is called regardless of the message being in the internal message cache or not.

If the message is found in the message cache, it can be accessed via <a href="#discord.RawMessageDeleteEvent.cached_message" title="discord.RawMessageDeleteEvent.cached_message"><code>RawMessageDeleteEvent.cached_message</code></a>

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.messages" title="discord.Intents.messages"><code>Intents.messages</code></a> to be enabled.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**payload** (<a href="#discord.RawMessageDeleteEvent" title="discord.RawMessageDeleteEvent"><code>RawMessageDeleteEvent</code></a>) – The raw event payload data.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_raw_bulk_message_delete(*payload*)<a href="#discord.on_raw_bulk_message_delete" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a bulk delete is triggered. Unlike <a href="#discord.on_bulk_message_delete" title="discord.on_bulk_message_delete"><code>on_bulk_message_delete()</code></a>, this is called regardless of the messages being in the internal message cache or not.

If the messages are found in the message cache, they can be accessed via <a href="#discord.RawBulkMessageDeleteEvent.cached_messages" title="discord.RawBulkMessageDeleteEvent.cached_messages"><code>RawBulkMessageDeleteEvent.cached_messages</code></a>

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.messages" title="discord.Intents.messages"><code>Intents.messages</code></a> to be enabled.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**payload** (<a href="#discord.RawBulkMessageDeleteEvent" title="discord.RawBulkMessageDeleteEvent"><code>RawBulkMessageDeleteEvent</code></a>) – The raw event payload data.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl>

### Polls ¶

<dl><dt>discord.on_poll_vote_add(*user*, *answer*)<a href="#discord.on_poll_vote_add" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dt>discord.on_poll_vote_remove(*user*, *answer*)<a href="#discord.on_poll_vote_remove" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a <a href="#discord.Poll" title="discord.Poll"><code>Poll</code></a> gains or loses a vote. If the <code>user</code> or <code>answer</code>’s poll parent message are not cached then this event will not be called.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.message_content" title="discord.Intents.message_content"><code>Intents.message_content</code></a> and <a href="#discord.Intents.polls" title="discord.Intents.polls"><code>Intents.polls</code></a> to be enabled.

Note

If the poll allows multiple answers and the user removes or adds multiple votes, this event will be called as many times as votes that are added or removed.

New in version 2.4.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **user** (Union\[<a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>]) – The user that performed the action.
- **answer** (<a href="#discord.PollAnswer" title="discord.PollAnswer"><code>PollAnswer</code></a>) – The answer the user voted or removed their vote from.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_raw_poll_vote_add(*payload*)<a href="#discord.on_raw_poll_vote_add" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dt>discord.on_raw_poll_vote_remove(*payload*)<a href="#discord.on_raw_poll_vote_remove" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a <a href="#discord.Poll" title="discord.Poll"><code>Poll</code></a> gains or loses a vote. Unlike <a href="#discord.on_poll_vote_add" title="discord.on_poll_vote_add"><code>on_poll_vote_add()</code></a> and <a href="#discord.on_poll_vote_remove" title="discord.on_poll_vote_remove"><code>on_poll_vote_remove()</code></a> this is called regardless of the state of the internal user and message cache.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.message_content" title="discord.Intents.message_content"><code>Intents.message_content</code></a> and <a href="#discord.Intents.polls" title="discord.Intents.polls"><code>Intents.polls</code></a> to be enabled.

Note

If the poll allows multiple answers and the user removes or adds multiple votes, this event will be called as many times as votes that are added or removed.

New in version 2.4.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**payload** (<a href="#discord.RawPollVoteActionEvent" title="discord.RawPollVoteActionEvent"><code>RawPollVoteActionEvent</code></a>) – The raw event payload data.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl>

### Reactions ¶

<dl><dt>discord.on_reaction_add(*reaction*, *user*)<a href="#discord.on_reaction_add" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a message has a reaction added to it. Similar to <a href="#discord.on_message_edit" title="discord.on_message_edit"><code>on_message_edit()</code></a>, if the message is not found in the internal message cache, then this event will not be called. Consider using <a href="#discord.on_raw_reaction_add" title="discord.on_raw_reaction_add"><code>on_raw_reaction_add()</code></a> instead.

Note

To get the <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> being reacted, access it via <a href="#discord.Reaction.message" title="discord.Reaction.message"><code>Reaction.message</code></a>.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.reactions" title="discord.Intents.reactions"><code>Intents.reactions</code></a> to be enabled.

Note

This doesn’t require <a href="#discord.Intents.members" title="discord.Intents.members"><code>Intents.members</code></a> within a guild context, but due to Discord not providing updated user information in a direct message it’s required for direct messages to receive this event. Consider using <a href="#discord.on_raw_reaction_add" title="discord.on_raw_reaction_add"><code>on_raw_reaction_add()</code></a> if you need this and do not otherwise want to enable the members intent.

Warning

This event does not have a way of differentiating whether a reaction is a burst reaction (also known as “super reaction”) or not. If you need this, consider using <a href="#discord.on_raw_reaction_add" title="discord.on_raw_reaction_add"><code>on_raw_reaction_add()</code></a> instead.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **reaction** (<a href="#discord.Reaction" title="discord.Reaction"><code>Reaction</code></a>) – The current state of the reaction.
- **user** (Union\[<a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>, <a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a>]) – The user who added the reaction.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_reaction_remove(*reaction*, *user*)<a href="#discord.on_reaction_remove" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a message has a reaction removed from it. Similar to on\_message\_edit, if the message is not found in the internal message cache, then this event will not be called.

Note

To get the message being reacted, access it via <a href="#discord.Reaction.message" title="discord.Reaction.message"><code>Reaction.message</code></a>.

This requires both <a href="#discord.Intents.reactions" title="discord.Intents.reactions"><code>Intents.reactions</code></a> and <a href="#discord.Intents.members" title="discord.Intents.members"><code>Intents.members</code></a> to be enabled.

Note

Consider using <a href="#discord.on_raw_reaction_remove" title="discord.on_raw_reaction_remove"><code>on_raw_reaction_remove()</code></a> if you need this and do not want to enable the members intent.

Warning

This event does not have a way of differentiating whether a reaction is a burst reaction (also known as “super reaction”) or not. If you need this, consider using <a href="#discord.on_raw_reaction_remove" title="discord.on_raw_reaction_remove"><code>on_raw_reaction_remove()</code></a> instead.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **reaction** (<a href="#discord.Reaction" title="discord.Reaction"><code>Reaction</code></a>) – The current state of the reaction.
- **user** (Union\[<a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>, <a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a>]) – The user whose reaction was removed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_reaction_clear(*message*, *reactions*)<a href="#discord.on_reaction_clear" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a message has all its reactions removed from it. Similar to <a href="#discord.on_message_edit" title="discord.on_message_edit"><code>on_message_edit()</code></a>, if the message is not found in the internal message cache, then this event will not be called. Consider using <a href="#discord.on_raw_reaction_clear" title="discord.on_raw_reaction_clear"><code>on_raw_reaction_clear()</code></a> instead.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.reactions" title="discord.Intents.reactions"><code>Intents.reactions</code></a> to be enabled.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **message** (<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>) – The message that had its reactions cleared.
- **reactions** (List\[<a href="#discord.Reaction" title="discord.Reaction"><code>Reaction</code></a>]) – The reactions that were removed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_reaction_clear_emoji(*reaction*)<a href="#discord.on_reaction_clear_emoji" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a message has a specific reaction removed from it. Similar to <a href="#discord.on_message_edit" title="discord.on_message_edit"><code>on_message_edit()</code></a>, if the message is not found in the internal message cache, then this event will not be called. Consider using <a href="#discord.on_raw_reaction_clear_emoji" title="discord.on_raw_reaction_clear_emoji"><code>on_raw_reaction_clear_emoji()</code></a> instead.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.reactions" title="discord.Intents.reactions"><code>Intents.reactions</code></a> to be enabled.

New in version 1.3.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**reaction** (<a href="#discord.Reaction" title="discord.Reaction"><code>Reaction</code></a>) – The reaction that got cleared.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_raw_reaction_add(*payload*)<a href="#discord.on_raw_reaction_add" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a message has a reaction added. Unlike <a href="#discord.on_reaction_add" title="discord.on_reaction_add"><code>on_reaction_add()</code></a>, this is called regardless of the state of the internal message cache.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.reactions" title="discord.Intents.reactions"><code>Intents.reactions</code></a> to be enabled.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**payload** (<a href="#discord.RawReactionActionEvent" title="discord.RawReactionActionEvent"><code>RawReactionActionEvent</code></a>) – The raw event payload data.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_raw_reaction_remove(*payload*)<a href="#discord.on_raw_reaction_remove" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a message has a reaction removed. Unlike <a href="#discord.on_reaction_remove" title="discord.on_reaction_remove"><code>on_reaction_remove()</code></a>, this is called regardless of the state of the internal message cache.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.reactions" title="discord.Intents.reactions"><code>Intents.reactions</code></a> to be enabled.

**payload** (<a href="#discord.RawReactionActionEvent" title="discord.RawReactionActionEvent"><code>RawReactionActionEvent</code></a>) – The raw event payload data.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_raw_reaction_clear(*payload*)<a href="#discord.on_raw_reaction_clear" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a message has all its reactions removed. Unlike <a href="#discord.on_reaction_clear" title="discord.on_reaction_clear"><code>on_reaction_clear()</code></a>, this is called regardless of the state of the internal message cache.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.reactions" title="discord.Intents.reactions"><code>Intents.reactions</code></a> to be enabled.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**payload** (<a href="#discord.RawReactionClearEvent" title="discord.RawReactionClearEvent"><code>RawReactionClearEvent</code></a>) – The raw event payload data.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_raw_reaction_clear_emoji(*payload*)<a href="#discord.on_raw_reaction_clear_emoji" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a message has a specific reaction removed from it. Unlike <a href="#discord.on_reaction_clear_emoji" title="discord.on_reaction_clear_emoji"><code>on_reaction_clear_emoji()</code></a> this is called regardless of the state of the internal message cache.

Called when a <a href="#discord.StageInstance" title="discord.StageInstance"><code>StageInstance</code></a> is created or deleted for a <a href="#discord.StageChannel" title="discord.StageChannel"><code>StageChannel</code></a>.

New in version 2.0.

<dd>

Called whenever a thread is created.

Note that you can get the guild from <a href="#discord.Thread.guild" title="discord.Thread.guild"><code>Thread.guild</code></a>.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.guilds" title="discord.Intents.guilds"><code>Intents.guilds</code></a> to be enabled.

New in version 2.0.

<dd>

Called whenever a thread is joined.

Note that you can get the guild from <a href="#discord.Thread.guild" title="discord.Thread.guild"><code>Thread.guild</code></a>.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.guilds" title="discord.Intents.guilds"><code>Intents.guilds</code></a> to be enabled.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>

**thread** (<a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a>) – The thread that got joined.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_thread_update(*before*, *after*)<a href="#discord.on_thread_update" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called whenever a thread is updated. If the thread could not be found in the internal cache this event will not be called. Threads will not be in the cache if they are archived.

If you need this information use <a href="#discord.on_raw_thread_update" title="discord.on_raw_thread_update"><code>on_raw_thread_update()</code></a> instead.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.guilds" title="discord.Intents.guilds"><code>Intents.guilds</code></a> to be enabled.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **before** (<a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a>) – The updated thread’s old info.
- **after** (<a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a>) – The updated thread’s new info.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_thread_remove(*thread*)<a href="#discord.on_thread_remove" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called whenever a thread is removed. This is different from a thread being deleted.

Note that you can get the guild from <a href="#discord.Thread.guild" title="discord.Thread.guild"><code>Thread.guild</code></a>.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.guilds" title="discord.Intents.guilds"><code>Intents.guilds</code></a> to be enabled.

Warning

Due to technical limitations, this event might not be called as soon as one expects. Since the library tracks thread membership locally, the API only sends updated thread membership status upon being synced by joining a thread.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**thread** (<a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a>) – The thread that got removed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_thread_delete(*thread*)<a href="#discord.on_thread_delete" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called whenever a thread is deleted. If the thread could not be found in the internal cache this event will not be called. Threads will not be in the cache if they are archived.

If you need this information use <a href="#discord.on_raw_thread_delete" title="discord.on_raw_thread_delete"><code>on_raw_thread_delete()</code></a> instead.

Note that you can get the guild from <a href="#discord.Thread.guild" title="discord.Thread.guild"><code>Thread.guild</code></a>.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.guilds" title="discord.Intents.guilds"><code>Intents.guilds</code></a> to be enabled.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**thread** (<a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a>) – The thread that got deleted.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_raw_thread_update(*payload*)<a href="#discord.on_raw_thread_update" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called whenever a thread is updated. Unlike <a href="#discord.on_thread_update" title="discord.on_thread_update"><code>on_thread_update()</code></a> this is called regardless of the thread being in the internal thread cache or not.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.guilds" title="discord.Intents.guilds"><code>Intents.guilds</code></a> to be enabled.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**payload** (<a href="#discord.RawThreadUpdateEvent" title="discord.RawThreadUpdateEvent"><code>RawThreadUpdateEvent</code></a>) – The raw event payload data.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_raw_thread_delete(*payload*)<a href="#discord.on_raw_thread_delete" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called whenever a thread is deleted. Unlike <a href="#discord.on_thread_delete" title="discord.on_thread_delete"><code>on_thread_delete()</code></a> this is called regardless of the thread being in the internal thread cache or not.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.guilds" title="discord.Intents.guilds"><code>Intents.guilds</code></a> to be enabled.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**payload** (<a href="#discord.RawThreadDeleteEvent" title="discord.RawThreadDeleteEvent"><code>RawThreadDeleteEvent</code></a>) – The raw event payload data.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_thread_member_join(*member*)<a href="#discord.on_thread_member_join" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dt>discord.on_thread_member_remove(*member*)<a href="#discord.on_thread_member_remove" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a <a href="#discord.ThreadMember" title="discord.ThreadMember"><code>ThreadMember</code></a> leaves or joins a <a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a>.

You can get the thread a member belongs in by accessing <a href="#discord.ThreadMember.thread" title="discord.ThreadMember.thread"><code>ThreadMember.thread</code></a>.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.members" title="discord.Intents.members"><code>Intents.members</code></a> to be enabled.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>

**member** (<a href="#discord.ThreadMember" title="discord.ThreadMember"><code>ThreadMember</code></a>) – The member who joined or left.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_raw_thread_member_remove(*payload*)<a href="#discord.on_raw_thread_member_remove" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a <a href="#discord.ThreadMember" title="discord.ThreadMember"><code>ThreadMember</code></a> leaves a <a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a>. Unlike <a href="#discord.on_thread_member_remove" title="discord.on_thread_member_remove"><code>on_thread_member_remove()</code></a> this is called regardless of the member being in the internal thread’s members cache or not.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>

### Voice ¶

<dl><dt>discord.on_voice_state_update(*member*, *before*, *after*)<a href="#discord.on_voice_state_update" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> changes their <a href="#discord.VoiceState" title="discord.VoiceState"><code>VoiceState</code></a>.

The following, but not limited to, examples illustrate when this event is called:

- A member joins a voice or stage channel.
- A member leaves a voice or stage channel.
- A member is muted or deafened by their own accord.
- A member is muted or deafened by a guild administrator.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.voice_states" title="discord.Intents.voice_states"><code>Intents.voice_states</code></a> to be enabled.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **member** (<a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>) – The member whose voice states changed.
- **before** (<a href="#discord.VoiceState" title="discord.VoiceState"><code>VoiceState</code></a>) – The voice state prior to the changes.
- **after** (<a href="#discord.VoiceState" title="discord.VoiceState"><code>VoiceState</code></a>) – The voice state after the changes.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.on_voice_channel_effect(*effect*)<a href="#discord.on_voice_channel_effect" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Called when a <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> sends a <a href="#discord.VoiceChannelEffect" title="discord.VoiceChannelEffect"><code>VoiceChannelEffect</code></a> in a voice channel the bot is in.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.voice_states" title="discord.Intents.voice_states"><code>Intents.voice_states</code></a> to be enabled.

New in version 2.5.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**effect** (<a href="#discord.VoiceChannelEffect" title="discord.VoiceChannelEffect"><code>VoiceChannelEffect</code></a>) – The effect that is sent.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl>

## Utility Functions ¶

<dl><dt>discord.utils.find(*predicate*, *iterable*, */*)<a href="#discord.utils.find" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A helper to return the first element found in the sequence that meets the predicate. For example:

```
member = discord.utils.find(lambda m: m.name == 'Mighty', channel.guild.members)

```

would find the first <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> whose name is ‘Mighty’ and return it. If an entry is not found, then <code>None</code> is returned.

This is different from <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#filter" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>filter()</code></a> due to the fact it stops the moment it finds a valid entry.

Changed in version 2.0: Both parameters are now positional-only.

Changed in version 2.0: The <code>iterable</code> parameter supports <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterable" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterable</a>s.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **predicate** – A function that returns a boolean-like result.
- **iterable** (Union\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>collections.abc.Iterable</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.AsyncIterable" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>collections.abc.AsyncIterable</code></a>]) – The iterable to search through. Using a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.AsyncIterable" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>collections.abc.AsyncIterable</code></a>, makes this function return a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-coroutine" title="(in Python v3.14)">coroutine</a>.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.utils.get(*iterable*, */*, ***attrs*)<a href="#discord.utils.get" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A helper that returns the first element in the iterable that meets all the traits passed in <code>attrs</code>. This is an alternative for <a href="#discord.utils.find" title="discord.utils.find"><code>find()</code></a>.

When multiple attributes are specified, they are checked using logical AND, not logical OR. Meaning they have to meet every attribute passed in and not one of them.

To have a nested attribute search (i.e. search by <code>x.y</code>) then pass in <code>x__y</code> as the keyword argument.

If nothing is found that matches the attributes passed, then <code>None</code> is returned.

Changed in version 2.0: The <code>iterable</code> parameter is now positional-only.

Changed in version 2.0: The <code>iterable</code> parameter supports <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterable" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterable</a>s.

Examples

Basic usage:

```
member = discord.utils.get(message.guild.members, name='Foo')

```

Multiple attribute matching:

```
channel = discord.utils.get(guild.voice_channels, name='Foo', bitrate=64000)

```

Nested attribute matching:

```
channel = discord.utils.get(client.get_all_channels(), guild__name='Cool', name='general')

```

Async iterables:

```
msg = await discord.utils.get(channel.history(), author__name='Dave')

```

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **iterable** (Union\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>collections.abc.Iterable</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.AsyncIterable" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>collections.abc.AsyncIterable</code></a>]) – The iterable to search through. Using a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.AsyncIterable" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>collections.abc.AsyncIterable</code></a>, makes this function return a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-coroutine" title="(in Python v3.14)">coroutine</a>.
- **\*\*attrs** – Keyword arguments that denote attributes to search with.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.utils.setup_logging(***, *handler=...*, *formatter=...*, *level=...*, *root=True*)<a href="#discord.utils.setup_logging" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A helper function to setup logging.

This is superficially similar to <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.html#logging.basicConfig" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>logging.basicConfig()</code></a> but uses different defaults and a colour formatter if the stream can display colour.

This is used by the <a href="#discord.Client" title="discord.Client"><code>Client</code></a> to set up logging if <code>log_handler</code> is not <code>None</code>.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **handler** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.html#logging.Handler" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>logging.Handler</code></a>) –

  The log handler to use for the library’s logger.

  The default log handler if not provided is <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.handlers.html#logging.StreamHandler" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>logging.StreamHandler</code></a>.
- **formatter** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.html#logging.Formatter" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>logging.Formatter</code></a>) – The formatter to use with the given log handler. If not provided then it defaults to a colour based logging formatter (if available). If colour is not available then a simple logging formatter is provided.
- **level** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The default log level for the library’s logger. Defaults to <code>logging.INFO</code>.
- **root** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to set up the root logger rather than the library logger. Unlike the default for <a href="#discord.Client" title="discord.Client"><code>Client</code></a>, this defaults to <code>True</code>.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* discord.utils.maybe_coroutine(*f*, **args*, ***kwargs*)<a href="#discord.utils.maybe_coroutine" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

A helper function that will await the result of a function if it’s a coroutine or return the result if it’s not.

This is useful for functions that may or may not be coroutines.

New in version 2.2.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **f** (*Callable**\[**...**,* *Any**]*) – The function or coroutine to call.
- **\*args** – The arguments to pass to the function.
- **\*\*kwargs** – The keyword arguments to pass to the function.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The result of the function or coroutine.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

Any

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.utils.snowflake_time(*id*, */*)<a href="#discord.utils.snowflake_time" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns the creation time of the given snowflake.

Changed in version 2.0: The <code>id</code> parameter is now positional-only.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**id** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The snowflake ID.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

An aware datetime in UTC representing the creation time of the snowflake.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.utils.time_snowflake(*dt*, */*, ***, *high=False*)<a href="#discord.utils.time_snowflake" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns a numeric snowflake pretending to be created at the given date.

When using as the lower end of a range, use <code>time_snowflake(dt, high=False) - 1</code> to be inclusive, <code>high=True</code> to be exclusive.

When using as the higher end of a range, use <code>time_snowflake(dt, high=True) + 1</code> to be inclusive, <code>high=False</code> to be exclusive.

Changed in version 2.0: The <code>high</code> parameter is now keyword-only and the <code>dt</code> parameter is now positional-only.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **dt** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>) – A datetime object to convert to a snowflake. If naive, the timezone is assumed to be local time.
- **high** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether or not to set the lower 22 bit to high or low.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The snowflake representing the time given.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>discord.utils.oauth_url(*client_id*, ***, *permissions=...*, *guild=...*, *redirect_uri=...*, *scopes=...*, *disable_guild_select=False*, *state=...*)<a href="#discord.utils.oauth_url" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Changed in version 2.0: <code>permissions</code>, <code>guild</code>, <code>redirect_uri</code>, <code>scopes</code> and <code>state</code> parameters are now keyword-only.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>

- **permissions** (<a href="#discord.Permissions" title="discord.Permissions"><code>Permissions</code></a>) – The permissions you’re requesting. If not given then you won’t be requesting any permissions.

- **state** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) –

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The OAuth2 URL for inviting the bot into guilds.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
