<dl><dt>*class*discord.abc.Messageable<a href="#discord.abc.Messageable" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

An ABC that details the common operations on a model that can send messages.

The following classes implement this ABC:

- <a href="#discord.TextChannel" title="discord.TextChannel"><code>TextChannel</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.VoiceChannel" title="discord.VoiceChannel"><code>VoiceChannel</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.StageChannel" title="discord.StageChannel"><code>StageChannel</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.DMChannel" title="discord.DMChannel"><code>DMChannel</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.GroupChannel" title="discord.GroupChannel"><code>GroupChannel</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.PartialMessageable" title="discord.PartialMessageable"><code>PartialMessageable</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>
- <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/ext/commands/api.html#discord.ext.commands.Context" title="discord.ext.commands.Context"><code>Context</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a>

<dl><dt>*async with* typing()<a href="#discord.abc.Messageable.typing" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns an asynchronous context manager that allows you to send a typing indicator to the destination for an indefinite period of time, or 10 seconds if the context manager is called using <code>await</code>.

Example Usage:

```
async with channel.typing():
    # simulate something heavy
    await asyncio.sleep(20)

await channel.send('Done!')

```

Example Usage:

```
await channel.typing()
# Do some computational magic for about 10 seconds
await channel.send('Done!')

```

Changed in version 2.0: This no longer works with the <code>with</code> syntax, <code>async with</code> must be used instead.

Changed in version 2.0: Added functionality to <code>await</code> the context manager to send a typing indicator for 10 seconds.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*await* send(*content=None*, ***, *tts=False*, *embed=None*, *embeds=None*, *file=None*, *files=None*, *stickers=None*, *delete_after=None*, *nonce=None*, *allowed_mentions=None*, *reference=None*, *mention_author=None*, *view=None*, *suppress_embeds=False*, *silent=False*, *poll=None*)<a href="#discord.abc.Messageable.send" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Sends a message to the destination with the content given.

The content must be a type that can convert to a string through <code>str(content)</code>. If the content is set to <code>None</code> (the default), then the <code>embed</code> parameter must be provided.

To upload a single file, the <code>file</code> parameter should be used with a single <a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a> object. To upload multiple files, the <code>files</code> parameter should be used with a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#list" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>list</code></a> of <a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a> objects. **Specifying both parameters will lead to an exception**.

To upload a single embed, the <code>embed</code> parameter should be used with a single <a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a> object. To upload multiple embeds, the <code>embeds</code> parameter should be used with a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#list" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>list</code></a> of <a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a> objects. **Specifying both parameters will lead to an exception**.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> or <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>ValueError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **content** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The content of the message to send.
- **tts** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Indicates if the message should be sent using text-to-speech.
- **embed** (<a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a>) – The rich embed for the content.
- **embeds** (List\[<a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a>]) –

  A list of embeds to upload. Must be a maximum of 10.

  New in version 2.0.
- **file** (<a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a>) – The file to upload.
- **files** (List\[<a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a>]) – A list of files to upload. Must be a maximum of 10.
- **nonce** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The nonce to use for sending this message. If the message was successfully sent, then the message will have a nonce with this value.
- **delete\_after** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>float</code></a>) – If provided, the number of seconds to wait in the background before deleting the message we just sent. If the deletion fails, then it is silently ignored.
- **allowed\_mentions** (<a href="#discord.AllowedMentions" title="discord.AllowedMentions"><code>AllowedMentions</code></a>) –

  Controls the mentions being processed in this message. If this is passed, then the object is merged with <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a>. The merging behaviour only overrides attributes that have been explicitly passed to the object, otherwise it uses the attributes set in <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a>. If no object is passed at all then the defaults given by <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a> are used instead.

  New in version 1.4.
- **reference** (Union\[<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>, <a href="#discord.MessageReference" title="discord.MessageReference"><code>MessageReference</code></a>, <a href="#discord.PartialMessage" title="discord.PartialMessage"><code>PartialMessage</code></a>]) –

  A reference to the <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> to which you are referencing, this can be created using <a href="#discord.Message.to_reference" title="discord.Message.to_reference"><code>to_reference()</code></a> or passed directly as a <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>. In the event of a replying reference, you can control whether this mentions the author of the referenced message using the <a href="#discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user" title="discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user"><code>replied_user</code></a> attribute of <code>allowed_mentions</code> or by setting <code>mention_author</code>.

  New in version 1.6.
- **mention\_author** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>]) –

  If set, overrides the <a href="#discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user" title="discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user"><code>replied_user</code></a> attribute of <code>allowed_mentions</code>.

  New in version 1.6.
- **view** (Union\[<a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.ui.View" title="discord.ui.View"><code>discord.ui.View</code></a>, <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.ui.LayoutView" title="discord.ui.LayoutView"><code>discord.ui.LayoutView</code></a>]) –

  A Discord UI View to add to the message.

  New in version 2.0.
- **stickers** (Sequence\[Union\[<a href="#discord.GuildSticker" title="discord.GuildSticker"><code>GuildSticker</code></a>, <a href="#discord.StickerItem" title="discord.StickerItem"><code>StickerItem</code></a>]]) –

  A list of stickers to upload. Must be a maximum of 3.

  New in version 2.0.
- **suppress\_embeds** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to suppress embeds for the message. This sends the message without any embeds if set to <code>True</code>.

  New in version 2.0.
- **silent** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to suppress push and desktop notifications for the message. This will increment the mention counter in the UI, but will not actually send a notification.

  New in version 2.2.
- **poll** (<a href="#discord.Poll" title="discord.Poll"><code>Poll</code></a>) –

  The poll to send with this message.

  New in version 2.4.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Sending the message failed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to send the message.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – You sent a message with the same nonce as one that has been explicitly deleted shortly earlier.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – The <code>files</code> or <code>embeds</code> list is not of the appropriate size.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – You specified both <code>file</code> and <code>files</code>, or you specified both <code>embed</code> and <code>embeds</code>, or the <code>reference</code> object is not a <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>, <a href="#discord.MessageReference" title="discord.MessageReference"><code>MessageReference</code></a> or <a href="#discord.PartialMessage" title="discord.PartialMessage"><code>PartialMessage</code></a>.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The message that was sent.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_message(*id*, */*)<a href="#discord.abc.Messageable.fetch_message" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

Retrieves a single <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> from the destination.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**id** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The message ID to look for.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The specified message was not found.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the permissions required to get a message.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Retrieving the message failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>

The message asked for.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>pins(***, *limit=50*, *before=None*, *oldest_first=False*)<a href="#discord.abc.Messageable.pins" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Retrieves an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterator" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterator</a> of the pinned messages in the channel.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.view_channel" title="discord.Permissions.view_channel"><code>view_channel</code></a> and <a href="#discord.Permissions.read_message_history" title="discord.Permissions.read_message_history"><code>read_message_history</code></a> in order to use this.

Changed in version 2.6: Due to a change in Discord’s API, this now returns a paginated iterator instead of a list.

For backwards compatibility, you can still retrieve a list of pinned messages by using <code>await</code> on the returned object. This is however deprecated.

Note

Due to a limitation with the Discord API, the <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> object returned by this method does not contain complete <a href="#discord.Message.reactions" title="discord.Message.reactions"><code>Message.reactions</code></a> data.

Examples

Usage

```
counter = 0
async for message in channel.pins(limit=250):
    counter += 1

```

Flattening into a list:

```
messages = [message async for message in channel.pins(limit=50)]
# messages is now a list of Message...

```

All parameters are optional.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **limit** (*Optional**\[*<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)">*int*</a>*]*) –

  The number of pinned messages to retrieve. If <code>None</code>, it retrieves every pinned message in the channel. Note, however, that this would make it a slow operation. Defaults to <code>50</code>.

  New in version 2.6.
- **before** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>, <a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>]]) –

  Retrieve pinned messages before this time or snowflake. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.

  New in version 2.6.
- **oldest\_first** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  If set to <code>True</code>, return messages in oldest pin-&gt;newest pin order. Defaults to <code>False</code>.

  New in version 2.6.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the permission to retrieve pinned messages.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Retrieving the pinned messages failed.

</dd><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> – The pinned message with <a href="#discord.Message.pinned_at" title="discord.Message.pinned_at"><code>Message.pinned_at</code></a> set.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*async for ... in* history(***, *limit=100*, *before=None*, *after=None*, *around=None*, *oldest_first=None*)<a href="#discord.abc.Messageable.history" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterator" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterator</a> that enables receiving the destination’s message history.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.read_message_history" title="discord.Permissions.read_message_history"><code>read_message_history</code></a> to do this.

Examples

Usage

```
counter = 0
async for message in channel.history(limit=200):
    if message.author == client.user:
        counter += 1

```

Flattening into a list:

```
messages = [message async for message in channel.history(limit=123)]
# messages is now a list of Message...

```

All parameters are optional.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **limit** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) – The number of messages to retrieve. If <code>None</code>, retrieves every message in the channel. Note, however, that this would make it a slow operation.
- **before** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve messages before this date or message. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.
- **after** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve messages after this date or message. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.
- **around** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve messages around this date or message. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time. When using this argument, the maximum limit is 101. Note that if the limit is an even number then this will return at most limit + 1 messages.
- **oldest\_first** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>]) – If set to <code>True</code>, return messages in oldest-&gt;newest order. Defaults to <code>True</code> if <code>after</code> is specified, otherwise <code>False</code>.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to get channel message history.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – The request to get message history failed.

</dd><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> – The message with the message data parsed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl>

- **cls** (Type\[<a href="#discord.VoiceProtocol" title="discord.VoiceProtocol"><code>VoiceProtocol</code></a>]) – A type that subclasses <a href="#discord.VoiceProtocol" title="discord.VoiceProtocol"><code>VoiceProtocol</code></a> to connect with. Defaults to <a href="#discord.VoiceClient" title="discord.VoiceClient"><code>VoiceClient</code></a>.

- <a href="#discord.opus.OpusNotLoaded" title="discord.opus.OpusNotLoaded">**OpusNotLoaded**</a> – The opus library has not been loaded.

## Discord Models ¶

Models are classes that are received from Discord and are not meant to be created by the user of the library.

Danger

The classes listed below are **not intended to be created by users** and are also **read-only**.

For example, this means that you should not make your own [`User`](#discord.User "discord.User") instances nor should you modify the [`User`](#discord.User "discord.User") instance yourself.

If you want to get one of these model classes instances they’d have to be through the cache, and a common way of doing so is through the [`utils.find()`](#discord.utils.find "discord.utils.find") function or attributes of model classes that you receive from the events specified in the [Event Reference](#discord-api-events).

Note

Nearly all classes here have [\_\_slots\_\_](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/datamodel.html#slots "(in Python v3.14)") defined which means that it is impossible to have dynamic attributes to the data classes.

</dl><dl><dt>*await* edit(***, *username=...*, *avatar=...*, *banner=...*)<a href="#discord.ClientUser.edit" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Edits the current profile of the client.

Note

To upload an avatar, a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-bytes-like-object" title="(in Python v3.14)">bytes-like object</a> must be passed in that represents the image being uploaded. If this is done through a file then the file must be opened via <code>open('some_filename', 'rb')</code> and the <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-bytes-like-object" title="(in Python v3.14)">bytes-like object</a> is given through the use of <code>fp.read()</code>.

Changed in version 2.0: The edit is no longer in-place, instead the newly edited client user is returned.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>ValueError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **username** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The new username you wish to change to.
- **avatar** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bytes</code></a>]) – A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-bytes-like-object" title="(in Python v3.14)">bytes-like object</a> representing the image to upload. Could be <code>None</code> to denote no avatar. Only image formats supported for uploading are JPEG, PNG, GIF, and WEBP.
- **banner** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bytes</code></a>]) –

  A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-bytes-like-object" title="(in Python v3.14)">bytes-like object</a> representing the image to upload. Could be <code>None</code> to denote no banner. Only image formats supported for uploading are JPEG, PNG, GIF and WEBP.

  New in version 2.4.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Editing your profile failed.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – Wrong image format passed for <code>avatar</code>.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>

The newly edited client user.

</dl><dl><dt>*async with* typing()<a href="#discord.User.typing" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns an asynchronous context manager that allows you to send a typing indicator to the destination for an indefinite period of time, or 10 seconds if the context manager is called using <code>await</code>.

Example Usage:

```
async with channel.typing():
    # simulate something heavy
    await asyncio.sleep(20)

await channel.send('Done!')

```

Example Usage:

```
await channel.typing()
# Do some computational magic for about 10 seconds
await channel.send('Done!')

```

Changed in version 2.0: This no longer works with the <code>with</code> syntax, <code>async with</code> must be used instead.

Changed in version 2.0: Added functionality to <code>await</code> the context manager to send a typing indicator for 10 seconds.

</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_message(*id*, */*)<a href="#discord.User.fetch_message" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Retrieves a single <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> from the destination.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**id** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The message ID to look for.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The specified message was not found.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the permissions required to get a message.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Retrieving the message failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The message asked for.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*async for ... in* history(***, *limit=100*, *before=None*, *after=None*, *around=None*, *oldest_first=None*)<a href="#discord.User.history" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterator" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterator</a> that enables receiving the destination’s message history.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.read_message_history" title="discord.Permissions.read_message_history"><code>read_message_history</code></a> to do this.

Examples

Usage

```
counter = 0
async for message in channel.history(limit=200):
    if message.author == client.user:
        counter += 1

```

Flattening into a list:

```
messages = [message async for message in channel.history(limit=123)]
# messages is now a list of Message...

```

All parameters are optional.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **limit** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) – The number of messages to retrieve. If <code>None</code>, retrieves every message in the channel. Note, however, that this would make it a slow operation.
- **before** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve messages before this date or message. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.
- **after** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve messages after this date or message. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.
- **around** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve messages around this date or message. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time. When using this argument, the maximum limit is 101. Note that if the limit is an even number then this will return at most limit + 1 messages.
- **oldest\_first** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>]) – If set to <code>True</code>, return messages in oldest-&gt;newest order. Defaults to <code>True</code> if <code>after</code> is specified, otherwise <code>False</code>.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to get channel message history.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – The request to get message history failed.

</dd><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> – The message with the message data parsed.

</dd></dl></dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>

</dl><dl><dt>pins(***, *limit=50*, *before=None*, *oldest_first=False*)<a href="#discord.User.pins" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Retrieves an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterator" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterator</a> of the pinned messages in the channel.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.view_channel" title="discord.Permissions.view_channel"><code>view_channel</code></a> and <a href="#discord.Permissions.read_message_history" title="discord.Permissions.read_message_history"><code>read_message_history</code></a> in order to use this.

Changed in version 2.6: Due to a change in Discord’s API, this now returns a paginated iterator instead of a list.

For backwards compatibility, you can still retrieve a list of pinned messages by using <code>await</code> on the returned object. This is however deprecated.

Note

Due to a limitation with the Discord API, the <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> object returned by this method does not contain complete <a href="#discord.Message.reactions" title="discord.Message.reactions"><code>Message.reactions</code></a> data.

Examples

Usage

```
counter = 0
async for message in channel.pins(limit=250):
    counter += 1

```

Flattening into a list:

```
messages = [message async for message in channel.pins(limit=50)]
# messages is now a list of Message...

```

All parameters are optional.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **limit** (*Optional**\[*<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)">*int*</a>*]*) –

  The number of pinned messages to retrieve. If <code>None</code>, it retrieves every pinned message in the channel. Note, however, that this would make it a slow operation. Defaults to <code>50</code>.

  New in version 2.6.
- **before** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>, <a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>]]) –

  Retrieve pinned messages before this time or snowflake. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.

  New in version 2.6.
- **oldest\_first** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  If set to <code>True</code>, return messages in oldest pin-&gt;newest pin order. Defaults to <code>False</code>.

  New in version 2.6.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the permission to retrieve pinned messages.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Retrieving the pinned messages failed.

</dd><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> – The pinned message with <a href="#discord.Message.pinned_at" title="discord.Message.pinned_at"><code>Message.pinned_at</code></a> set.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*primary_guild<a href="#discord.User.primary_guild" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns the user’s primary guild.

New in version 2.6.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.PrimaryGuild" title="discord.PrimaryGuild"><code>PrimaryGuild</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* send(*content=None*, ***, *tts=False*, *embed=None*, *embeds=None*, *file=None*, *files=None*, *stickers=None*, *delete_after=None*, *nonce=None*, *allowed_mentions=None*, *reference=None*, *mention_author=None*, *view=None*, *suppress_embeds=False*, *silent=False*, *poll=None*)<a href="#discord.User.send" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Sends a message to the destination with the content given.

The content must be a type that can convert to a string through <code>str(content)</code>. If the content is set to <code>None</code> (the default), then the <code>embed</code> parameter must be provided.

To upload a single file, the <code>file</code> parameter should be used with a single <a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a> object. To upload multiple files, the <code>files</code> parameter should be used with a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#list" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>list</code></a> of <a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a> objects. **Specifying both parameters will lead to an exception**.

To upload a single embed, the <code>embed</code> parameter should be used with a single <a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a> object. To upload multiple embeds, the <code>embeds</code> parameter should be used with a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#list" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>list</code></a> of <a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a> objects. **Specifying both parameters will lead to an exception**.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> or <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>ValueError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **content** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The content of the message to send.
- **tts** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Indicates if the message should be sent using text-to-speech.
- **embed** (<a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a>) – The rich embed for the content.
- **embeds** (List\[<a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a>]) –

  A list of embeds to upload. Must be a maximum of 10.

  New in version 2.0.
- **file** (<a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a>) – The file to upload.
- **files** (List\[<a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a>]) – A list of files to upload. Must be a maximum of 10.
- **nonce** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The nonce to use for sending this message. If the message was successfully sent, then the message will have a nonce with this value.
- **delete\_after** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>float</code></a>) – If provided, the number of seconds to wait in the background before deleting the message we just sent. If the deletion fails, then it is silently ignored.
- **allowed\_mentions** (<a href="#discord.AllowedMentions" title="discord.AllowedMentions"><code>AllowedMentions</code></a>) –

  Controls the mentions being processed in this message. If this is passed, then the object is merged with <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a>. The merging behaviour only overrides attributes that have been explicitly passed to the object, otherwise it uses the attributes set in <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a>. If no object is passed at all then the defaults given by <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a> are used instead.

  New in version 1.4.
- **reference** (Union\[<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>, <a href="#discord.MessageReference" title="discord.MessageReference"><code>MessageReference</code></a>, <a href="#discord.PartialMessage" title="discord.PartialMessage"><code>PartialMessage</code></a>]) –

  A reference to the <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> to which you are referencing, this can be created using <a href="#discord.Message.to_reference" title="discord.Message.to_reference"><code>to_reference()</code></a> or passed directly as a <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>. In the event of a replying reference, you can control whether this mentions the author of the referenced message using the <a href="#discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user" title="discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user"><code>replied_user</code></a> attribute of <code>allowed_mentions</code> or by setting <code>mention_author</code>.

  New in version 1.6.
- **mention\_author** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>]) –

  If set, overrides the <a href="#discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user" title="discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user"><code>replied_user</code></a> attribute of <code>allowed_mentions</code>.

  New in version 1.6.
- **view** (Union\[<a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.ui.View" title="discord.ui.View"><code>discord.ui.View</code></a>, <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.ui.LayoutView" title="discord.ui.LayoutView"><code>discord.ui.LayoutView</code></a>]) –

  A Discord UI View to add to the message.

  New in version 2.0.
- **stickers** (Sequence\[Union\[<a href="#discord.GuildSticker" title="discord.GuildSticker"><code>GuildSticker</code></a>, <a href="#discord.StickerItem" title="discord.StickerItem"><code>StickerItem</code></a>]]) –

  A list of stickers to upload. Must be a maximum of 3.

  New in version 2.0.
- **suppress\_embeds** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to suppress embeds for the message. This sends the message without any embeds if set to <code>True</code>.

  New in version 2.0.
- **silent** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to suppress push and desktop notifications for the message. This will increment the mention counter in the UI, but will not actually send a notification.

  New in version 2.2.
- **poll** (<a href="#discord.Poll" title="discord.Poll"><code>Poll</code></a>) –

  The poll to send with this message.

  New in version 2.4.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Sending the message failed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to send the message.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – You sent a message with the same nonce as one that has been explicitly deleted shortly earlier.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – The <code>files</code> or <code>embeds</code> list is not of the appropriate size.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – You specified both <code>file</code> and <code>files</code>, or you specified both <code>embed</code> and <code>embeds</code>, or the <code>reference</code> object is not a <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>, <a href="#discord.MessageReference" title="discord.MessageReference"><code>MessageReference</code></a> or <a href="#discord.PartialMessage" title="discord.PartialMessage"><code>PartialMessage</code></a>.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The message that was sent.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>

</dl><dl><dt>*await* edit(***, *name=...*, *event_type=...*, *actions=...*, *trigger=...*, *enabled=...*, *exempt_roles=...*, *exempt_channels=...*, *reason=...*)<a href="#discord.AutoModRule.edit" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Edits this auto moderation rule.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_guild" title="discord.Permissions.manage_guild"><code>Permissions.manage_guild</code></a> to edit rules.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The new name to change to.
- **event\_type** (<a href="#discord.AutoModRuleEventType" title="discord.AutoModRuleEventType"><code>AutoModRuleEventType</code></a>) – The new event type to change to.
- **actions** (List\[<a href="#discord.AutoModRuleAction" title="discord.AutoModRuleAction"><code>AutoModRuleAction</code></a>]) – The new rule actions to update.
- **trigger** (<a href="#discord.AutoModTrigger" title="discord.AutoModTrigger"><code>AutoModTrigger</code></a>) – The new trigger to update. You can only change the trigger metadata, not the type.
- **enabled** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether the rule should be enabled or not.
- **exempt\_roles** (Sequence\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>]) – The new roles to exempt from the rule.
- **exempt\_channels** (Sequence\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>]) – The new channels to exempt from the rule.
- **reason** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The reason for updating this rule. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permission to edit this rule.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Editing the rule failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The updated auto moderation rule.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.AutoModRule" title="discord.AutoModRule"><code>AutoModRule</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* delete(***, *reason=...*)<a href="#discord.AutoModRule.delete" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Deletes the auto moderation rule.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_guild" title="discord.Permissions.manage_guild"><code>Permissions.manage_guild</code></a> to delete rules.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**reason** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The reason for deleting this rule. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to delete the rule.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Deleting the rule failed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl>

<dl><dt>*class*discord.Attachment<a href="#discord.Attachment" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x == y</dt>

</dd></dl>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>: Whether this attachment is a voice message.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*await* save(*fp*, ***, *seek_begin=True*, *use_cached=False*)<a href="#discord.Attachment.save" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Saves this attachment into a file-like object.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **fp** (Union\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/io.html#io.BufferedIOBase" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>io.BufferedIOBase</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>os.PathLike</code></a>]) – The file-like object to save this attachment to or the filename to use. If a filename is passed then a file is created with that filename and used instead.
- **seek\_begin** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to seek to the beginning of the file after saving is successfully done.
- **use\_cached** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to use <a href="#discord.Attachment.proxy_url" title="discord.Attachment.proxy_url"><code>proxy_url</code></a> rather than <a href="#discord.Attachment.url" title="discord.Attachment.url"><code>url</code></a> when downloading the attachment. This will allow attachments to be saved after deletion more often, compared to the regular URL which is generally deleted right after the message is deleted. Note that this can still fail to download deleted attachments if too much time has passed and it does not work on some types of attachments.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Saving the attachment failed.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The attachment was deleted.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The number of bytes written.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* read(***, *use_cached=False*)<a href="#discord.Attachment.read" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Retrieves the content of this attachment as a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bytes</code></a> object.

New in version 1.1.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**use\_cached** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to use <a href="#discord.Attachment.proxy_url" title="discord.Attachment.proxy_url"><code>proxy_url</code></a> rather than <a href="#discord.Attachment.url" title="discord.Attachment.url"><code>url</code></a> when downloading the attachment. This will allow attachments to be saved after deletion more often, compared to the regular URL which is generally deleted right after the message is deleted. Note that this can still fail to download deleted attachments if too much time has passed and it does not work on some types of attachments.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Downloading the attachment failed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to access this attachment
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The attachment was deleted.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The contents of the attachment.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bytes</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* to_file(***, *filename=...*, *description=...*, *use_cached=False*, *spoiler=False*)<a href="#discord.Attachment.to_file" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Converts the attachment into a <a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a> suitable for sending via <a href="#discord.abc.Messageable.send" title="discord.abc.Messageable.send"><code>abc.Messageable.send()</code></a>.

New in version 1.3.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **filename** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) –

  The filename to use for the file. If not specified then the filename of the attachment is used instead.

  New in version 2.0.
- **description** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) –

  The description to use for the file. If not specified then the description of the attachment is used instead.

  New in version 2.0.
- **use\_cached** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to use <a href="#discord.Attachment.proxy_url" title="discord.Attachment.proxy_url"><code>proxy_url</code></a> rather than <a href="#discord.Attachment.url" title="discord.Attachment.url"><code>url</code></a> when downloading the attachment. This will allow attachments to be saved after deletion more often, compared to the regular URL which is generally deleted right after the message is deleted. Note that this can still fail to download deleted attachments if too much time has passed and it does not work on some types of attachments.

  New in version 1.4.
- **spoiler** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether the file is a spoiler.

  New in version 1.4.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Downloading the attachment failed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to access this attachment
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The attachment was deleted.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The attachment as a file suitable for sending.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl>

<dd>

- **static\_format** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The new format to change it to if the asset isn’t animated. Must be either ‘webp’, ‘jpeg’, ‘jpg’, or ‘png’.

<a href="#discord.Asset" title="discord.Asset"><code>Asset</code></a>

</dl><dl><dt>*await* save(*fp*, ***, *seek_begin=True*)<a href="#discord.Asset.save" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Saves this asset into a file-like object.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **fp** (Union\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/io.html#io.BufferedIOBase" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>io.BufferedIOBase</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>os.PathLike</code></a>]) – The file-like object to save this asset to or the filename to use. If a filename is passed then a file is created with that filename and used instead.
- **seek\_begin** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to seek to the beginning of the file after saving is successfully done.

- <a href="#discord.DiscordException" title="discord.DiscordException">**DiscordException**</a> – There was no internal connection state.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Downloading the asset failed.

<dd>

The number of bytes written.

</dd></dl></dd>

<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>

- **filename** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The filename of the file. If not provided, then the filename from the asset’s URL is used.
- **description** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The description for the file.
- **spoiler** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether the file is a spoiler.

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Downloading the asset failed.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The asset was deleted.

<dd>

The asset as a file suitable for sending.

<dl><dt>*class*discord.Message<a href="#discord.Message" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Represents a message from Discord.

<dl><dt>x == y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two messages are equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x != y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two messages are not equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>hash(x)</dt>
<dd>

Returns the message’s hash.

</dd></dl>

<dl><dt>tts<a href="#discord.Message.tts" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Specifies if the message was done with text-to-speech. This can only be accurately received in <a href="#discord.on_message" title="discord.on_message"><code>on_message()</code></a> due to a discord limitation.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>type<a href="#discord.Message.type" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The type of message. In most cases this should not be checked, but it is helpful in cases where it might be a system message for <a href="#discord.Message.system_content" title="discord.Message.system_content"><code>system_content</code></a>.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.MessageType" title="discord.MessageType"><code>MessageType</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>author<a href="#discord.Message.author" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> that sent the message. If <a href="#discord.Message.channel" title="discord.Message.channel"><code>channel</code></a> is a private channel or the user has the left the guild, then it is a <a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a> instead.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Union\[<a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>, <a href="#discord.abc.User" title="discord.abc.User"><code>abc.User</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>content<a href="#discord.Message.content" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The actual contents of the message. If <a href="#discord.Intents.message_content" title="discord.Intents.message_content"><code>Intents.message_content</code></a> is not enabled this will always be an empty string unless the bot is mentioned or the message is a direct message.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>nonce<a href="#discord.Message.nonce" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The value used by the discord guild and the client to verify that the message is successfully sent. This is not stored long term within Discord’s servers and is only used ephemerally.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[Union\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>embeds<a href="#discord.Message.embeds" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A list of embeds the message has. If <a href="#discord.Intents.message_content" title="discord.Intents.message_content"><code>Intents.message_content</code></a> is not enabled this will always be an empty list unless the bot is mentioned or the message is a direct message.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

List\[<a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>channel<a href="#discord.Message.channel" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The <a href="#discord.TextChannel" title="discord.TextChannel"><code>TextChannel</code></a> or <a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a> that the message was sent from. Could be a <a href="#discord.DMChannel" title="discord.DMChannel"><code>DMChannel</code></a> or <a href="#discord.GroupChannel" title="discord.GroupChannel"><code>GroupChannel</code></a> if it’s a private message.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Union\[<a href="#discord.TextChannel" title="discord.TextChannel"><code>TextChannel</code></a>, <a href="#discord.StageChannel" title="discord.StageChannel"><code>StageChannel</code></a>, <a href="#discord.VoiceChannel" title="discord.VoiceChannel"><code>VoiceChannel</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a>, <a href="#discord.DMChannel" title="discord.DMChannel"><code>DMChannel</code></a>, <a href="#discord.GroupChannel" title="discord.GroupChannel"><code>GroupChannel</code></a>, <a href="#discord.PartialMessageable" title="discord.PartialMessageable"><code>PartialMessageable</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>reference<a href="#discord.Message.reference" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The message that this message references. This is only applicable to message replies (<a href="#discord.MessageType.reply" title="discord.MessageType.reply"><code>MessageType.reply</code></a>), crossposted messages created by a followed channel integration, forwarded messages, and messages of type:

- <a href="#discord.MessageType.pins_add" title="discord.MessageType.pins_add"><code>MessageType.pins_add</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.MessageType.channel_follow_add" title="discord.MessageType.channel_follow_add"><code>MessageType.channel_follow_add</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.MessageType.thread_created" title="discord.MessageType.thread_created"><code>MessageType.thread_created</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.MessageType.thread_starter_message" title="discord.MessageType.thread_starter_message"><code>MessageType.thread_starter_message</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.MessageType.poll_result" title="discord.MessageType.poll_result"><code>MessageType.poll_result</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.MessageType.context_menu_command" title="discord.MessageType.context_menu_command"><code>MessageType.context_menu_command</code></a>

New in version 1.5.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="#discord.MessageReference" title="discord.MessageReference"><code>MessageReference</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>mention_everyone<a href="#discord.Message.mention_everyone" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Specifies if the message mentions everyone.

Note

This does not check if the <code>@everyone</code> or the <code>@here</code> text is in the message itself. Rather this boolean indicates if either the <code>@everyone</code> or the <code>@here</code> text is in the message **and** it did end up mentioning.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>mentions<a href="#discord.Message.mentions" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A list of <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> that were mentioned. If the message is in a private message then the list will be of <a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a> instead. For messages that are not of type <a href="#discord.MessageType.default" title="discord.MessageType.default"><code>MessageType.default</code></a>, this array can be used to aid in system messages. For more information, see <a href="#discord.Message.system_content" title="discord.Message.system_content"><code>system_content</code></a>.

Warning

The order of the mentions list is not in any particular order so you should not rely on it. This is a Discord limitation, not one with the library.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* add_reaction(*emoji*, */*)<a href="#discord.Message.add_reaction" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Adds a reaction to the message.

The emoji may be a unicode emoji or a custom guild <a href="#discord.Emoji" title="discord.Emoji"><code>Emoji</code></a>.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.read_message_history" title="discord.Permissions.read_message_history"><code>read_message_history</code></a> to do this. If nobody else has reacted to the message using this emoji, <a href="#discord.Permissions.add_reactions" title="discord.Permissions.add_reactions"><code>add_reactions</code></a> is required.

Changed in version 2.0: <code>emoji</code> parameter is now positional-only.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**emoji** (Union\[<a href="#discord.Emoji" title="discord.Emoji"><code>Emoji</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Reaction" title="discord.Reaction"><code>Reaction</code></a>, <a href="#discord.PartialEmoji" title="discord.PartialEmoji"><code>PartialEmoji</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The emoji to react with.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Adding the reaction failed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to react to the message.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The emoji you specified was not found.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – The emoji parameter is invalid.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* clear_reaction(*emoji*)<a href="#discord.Message.clear_reaction" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Clears a specific reaction from the message.

The emoji may be a unicode emoji or a custom guild <a href="#discord.Emoji" title="discord.Emoji"><code>Emoji</code></a>.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_messages" title="discord.Permissions.manage_messages"><code>manage_messages</code></a> to do this.

New in version 1.3.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**emoji** (Union\[<a href="#discord.Emoji" title="discord.Emoji"><code>Emoji</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Reaction" title="discord.Reaction"><code>Reaction</code></a>, <a href="#discord.PartialEmoji" title="discord.PartialEmoji"><code>PartialEmoji</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The emoji to clear.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Clearing the reaction failed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to clear the reaction.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The emoji you specified was not found.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – The emoji parameter is invalid.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* clear_reactions()<a href="#discord.Message.clear_reactions" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Removes all the reactions from the message.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_messages" title="discord.Permissions.manage_messages"><code>manage_messages</code></a> to do this.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Removing the reactions failed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to remove all the reactions.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* create_thread(***, *name*, *auto_archive_duration=...*, *slowmode_delay=None*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Message.create_thread" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Creates a public thread from this message.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.create_public_threads" title="discord.Permissions.create_public_threads"><code>create_public_threads</code></a> in order to create a public thread from a message.

The channel this message belongs in must be a <a href="#discord.TextChannel" title="discord.TextChannel"><code>TextChannel</code></a>.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The name of the thread.
- **auto\_archive\_duration** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) –

  The duration in minutes before a thread is automatically hidden from the channel list. If not provided, the channel’s default auto archive duration is used.

  Must be one of <code>60</code>, <code>1440</code>, <code>4320</code>, or <code>10080</code>, if provided.
- **slowmode\_delay** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) – Specifies the slowmode rate limit for user in this channel, in seconds. The maximum value possible is <code>21600</code>. By default no slowmode rate limit if this is <code>None</code>.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for creating a new thread. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to create a thread.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Creating the thread failed.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – This message does not have guild info attached.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The created thread.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* delete(***, *delay=None*)<a href="#discord.Message.delete" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Deletes the message.

Your own messages could be deleted without any proper permissions. However to delete other people’s messages, you must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_messages" title="discord.Permissions.manage_messages"><code>manage_messages</code></a>.

Changed in version 1.1: Added the new <code>delay</code> keyword-only parameter.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**delay** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>float</code></a>]) – If provided, the number of seconds to wait in the background before deleting the message. If the deletion fails then it is silently ignored.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have proper permissions to delete the message.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The message was deleted already
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Deleting the message failed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* end_poll()<a href="#discord.Message.end_poll" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Ends the <a href="#discord.Poll" title="discord.Poll"><code>Poll</code></a> attached to this message.

This can only be done if you are the message author.

If the poll was successfully ended, then it returns the updated <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Ending the poll failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The updated message.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch()<a href="#discord.Message.fetch" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Fetches the partial message to a full <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The message was not found.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the permissions required to get a message.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Retrieving the message failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The full message.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_thread()<a href="#discord.Message.fetch_thread" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Retrieves the public thread attached to this message.

Note

This method is an API call. For general usage, consider <a href="#discord.Message.thread" title="discord.Message.thread"><code>thread</code></a> instead.

New in version 2.4.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.InvalidData" title="discord.InvalidData">**InvalidData**</a> – An unknown channel type was received from Discord or the guild the thread belongs to is not the same as the one in this object points to.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Retrieving the thread failed.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – There is no thread attached to this message.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permission to fetch this channel.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The public thread attached to this message.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* forward(*destination*, ***, *fail_if_not_exists=True*)<a href="#discord.Message.forward" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Forwards this message to a channel.

New in version 2.5.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **destination** (<a href="#discord.abc.Messageable" title="discord.abc.Messageable"><code>Messageable</code></a>) – The channel to forward this message to.
- **fail\_if\_not\_exists** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether replying using the message reference should raise <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException"><code>HTTPException</code></a> if the message no longer exists or Discord could not fetch the message.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Forwarding the message failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The message sent to the channel.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*jump_url<a href="#discord.Message.jump_url" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns a URL that allows the client to jump to this message.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* pin(***, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Message.pin" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Pins the message.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.pin_messages" title="discord.Permissions.pin_messages"><code>pin_messages</code></a> to do this in a non-private channel context.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) –

The reason for pinning the message. Shows up on the audit log.

New in version 1.4.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to pin the message.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The message or channel was not found or deleted.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Pinning the message failed, probably due to the channel having more than 250 pinned messages.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* publish()<a href="#discord.Message.publish" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Publishes this message to the channel’s followers.

The message must have been sent in a news channel. You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.send_messages" title="discord.Permissions.send_messages"><code>send_messages</code></a> to do this.

If the message is not your own then <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_messages" title="discord.Permissions.manage_messages"><code>manage_messages</code></a> is also needed.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to publish this message or the channel is not a news channel.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Publishing the message failed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* remove_reaction(*emoji*, *member*)<a href="#discord.Message.remove_reaction" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Remove a reaction by the member from the message.

The emoji may be a unicode emoji or a custom guild <a href="#discord.Emoji" title="discord.Emoji"><code>Emoji</code></a>.

If the reaction is not your own (i.e. <code>member</code> parameter is not you) then <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_messages" title="discord.Permissions.manage_messages"><code>manage_messages</code></a> is needed.

The <code>member</code> parameter must represent a member and meet the <a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a> abc.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **emoji** (Union\[<a href="#discord.Emoji" title="discord.Emoji"><code>Emoji</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Reaction" title="discord.Reaction"><code>Reaction</code></a>, <a href="#discord.PartialEmoji" title="discord.PartialEmoji"><code>PartialEmoji</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The emoji to remove.
- **member** (<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>) – The member for which to remove the reaction.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Removing the reaction failed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to remove the reaction.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The member or emoji you specified was not found.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – The emoji parameter is invalid.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* reply(*content=None*, ***kwargs*)<a href="#discord.Message.reply" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

A shortcut method to <a href="#discord.abc.Messageable.send" title="discord.abc.Messageable.send"><code>abc.Messageable.send()</code></a> to reply to the <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>.

New in version 1.6.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> or <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>ValueError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to send the message.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – The <code>files</code> list is not of the appropriate size
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – You specified both <code>file</code> and <code>files</code>.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The message that was sent.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
