</dl><dl><dt>clean_content<a href="#discord.Message.clean_content" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A property that returns the content in a “cleaned up” manner. This basically means that mentions are transformed into the way the client shows it. e.g. <code>&lt;#id&gt;</code> will transform into <code>#name</code>.

This will also transform @everyone and @here mentions into non-mentions.

Note

This *does not* affect markdown. If you want to escape or remove markdown then use <a href="#discord.utils.escape_markdown" title="discord.utils.escape_markdown"><code>utils.escape_markdown()</code></a> or <a href="#discord.utils.remove_markdown" title="discord.utils.remove_markdown"><code>utils.remove_markdown()</code></a> respectively, along with this function.

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* edit(***, *content=...*, *embed=...*, *embeds=...*, *attachments=...*, *suppress=False*, *delete_after=None*, *allowed_mentions=...*, *view=...*)<a href="#discord.Message.edit" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Edits the message.

The content must be able to be transformed into a string via <code>str(content)</code>.

Changed in version 1.3: The <code>suppress</code> keyword-only parameter was added.

Changed in version 2.0: Edits are no longer in-place, the newly edited message is returned instead.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **content** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The new content to replace the message with. Could be <code>None</code> to remove the content.
- **embed** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a>]) – The new embed to replace the original with. Could be <code>None</code> to remove the embed.
- **embeds** (List\[<a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a>]) –

  The new embeds to replace the original with. Must be a maximum of 10. To remove all embeds <code>[]</code> should be passed.

  New in version 2.0.
- **attachments** (List\[Union\[<a href="#discord.Attachment" title="discord.Attachment"><code>Attachment</code></a>, <a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a>]]) –

  A list of attachments to keep in the message as well as new files to upload. If <code>[]</code> is passed then all attachments are removed.

  Note

  New files will always appear after current attachments.

  New in version 2.0.
- **suppress** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to suppress embeds for the message. This removes all the embeds if set to <code>True</code>. If set to <code>False</code> this brings the embeds back if they were suppressed. Using this parameter requires <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_messages" title="discord.Permissions.manage_messages"><code>manage_messages</code></a>.
- **delete\_after** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>float</code></a>]) – If provided, the number of seconds to wait in the background before deleting the message we just edited. If the deletion fails, then it is silently ignored.
- **allowed\_mentions** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.AllowedMentions" title="discord.AllowedMentions"><code>AllowedMentions</code></a>]) –

  Controls the mentions being processed in this message. If this is passed, then the object is merged with <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a>. The merging behaviour only overrides attributes that have been explicitly passed to the object, otherwise it uses the attributes set in <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a>. If no object is passed at all then the defaults given by <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a> are used instead.

  New in version 1.4.
- **view** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.ui.View" title="discord.ui.View"><code>View</code></a>, <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.ui.LayoutView" title="discord.ui.LayoutView"><code>LayoutView</code></a>]]) –

  The updated view to update this message with. If <code>None</code> is passed then the view is removed.

  Note

  If you want to update the message to have a <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.ui.LayoutView" title="discord.ui.LayoutView"><code>LayoutView</code></a>, you must explicitly set the <code>content</code>, <code>embed</code>, <code>embeds</code>, and <code>attachments</code> parameters to <code>None</code> if the previous message had any.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Editing the message failed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – Tried to suppress a message without permissions or edited a message’s content or embed that isn’t yours.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – This message does not exist.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – You specified both <code>embed</code> and <code>embeds</code>

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The newly edited message.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* add_files(**files*)<a href="#discord.Message.add_files" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

<dl><dt>*class*discord.Reaction<a href="#discord.Reaction" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Represents a reaction to a message.

Depending on the way this object was created, some of the attributes can have a value of <code>None</code>.

<dl><dt>x == y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two reactions are equal. This works by checking if the emoji is the same. So two messages with the same reaction will be considered “equal”.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x != y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two reactions are not equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>hash(x)</dt>
<dd>

Returns the reaction’s hash.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>str(x)</dt>
<dd>

Returns the string form of the reaction’s emoji.

</dd></dl>

<dl><dt>emoji<a href="#discord.Reaction.emoji" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The reaction emoji. May be a custom emoji, or a unicode emoji.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>: If this is a custom emoji.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*await* remove(*user*)<a href="#discord.Reaction.remove" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Remove the reaction by the provided <a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a> from the message.

If the reaction is not your own (i.e. <code>user</code> parameter is not you) then <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_messages" title="discord.Permissions.manage_messages"><code>manage_messages</code></a> is needed.

The <code>user</code> parameter must represent a user or member and meet the <a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a> abc.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**user** (<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>) – The user or member from which to remove the reaction.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Removing the reaction failed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to remove the reaction.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The user you specified, or the reaction’s message was not found.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* clear()<a href="#discord.Reaction.clear" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Clears this reaction from the message.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_messages" title="discord.Permissions.manage_messages"><code>manage_messages</code></a> to do this.

New in version 1.3.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>ValueError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Clearing the reaction failed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to clear the reaction.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The emoji you specified was not found.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – The emoji parameter is invalid.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*async for ... in* users(***, *limit=None*, *after=None*, *type=None*)<a href="#discord.Reaction.users" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterator" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterator</a> representing the users that have reacted to the message.

The <code>after</code> parameter must represent a member and meet the <a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a> abc.

Changed in version 2.0: <code>limit</code> and <code>after</code> parameters are now keyword-only.

Examples

Usage

```
# I do not actually recommend doing this.
async for user in reaction.users():
    await channel.send(f'{user} has reacted with {reaction.emoji}!')

```

Flattening into a list:

```
users = [user async for user in reaction.users()]
# users is now a list of User...
winner = random.choice(users)
await channel.send(f'{winner} has won the raffle.')

```

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **limit** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) – The maximum number of results to return. If not provided, returns all the users who reacted to the message.
- **after** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>]) – For pagination, reactions are sorted by member.
- **type** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.ReactionType" title="discord.ReactionType"><code>ReactionType</code></a>]) –

  The type of reaction to return users from. If not provided, Discord only returns users of reactions with type <code>normal</code>.

  New in version 2.4.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Getting the users for the reaction failed.

</dd><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

Union\[<a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>] – The member (if retrievable) or the user that has reacted to this message. The case where it can be a <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> is in a guild message context. Sometimes it can be a <a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a> if the member has left the guild.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl>

<dl><dt>*class*discord.Guild<a href="#discord.Guild" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Represents a Discord guild.

This is referred to as a “server” in the official Discord UI.

<dl><dt>x == y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two guilds are equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x != y</dt>
<dd>

</dd></dl><dl><dt>str(x)</dt>
<dd>

</dl><dl><dt>*property*chunked<a href="#discord.Guild.chunked" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns a boolean indicating if the guild is “chunked”.

A chunked guild means that <a href="#discord.Guild.member_count" title="discord.Guild.member_count"><code>member_count</code></a> is equal to the number of members stored in the internal <a href="#discord.Guild.members" title="discord.Guild.members"><code>members</code></a> cache.

If this value returns <code>False</code>, then you should request for offline members.

</dl><dl><dt>get_member_named(*name*, */*)<a href="#discord.Guild.get_member_named" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns the first member found that matches the name provided.

The name is looked up in the following order:

- Username#Discriminator (deprecated)
- Username#0 (deprecated, only gets users that migrated from their discriminator)
- Nickname
- Global name
- Username

If no member is found, <code>None</code> is returned.

Changed in version 2.0: <code>name</code> parameter is now positional-only.

Deprecated since version 2.3: Looking up users via discriminator due to Discord API change.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The name of the member to lookup.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The member in this guild with the associated name. If not found then <code>None</code> is returned.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* create_text_channel(*name*, ***, *reason=None*, *category=None*, *news=False*, *position=...*, *topic=...*, *slowmode_delay=...*, *nsfw=...*, *overwrites=...*, *default_auto_archive_duration=...*, *default_thread_slowmode_delay=...*)<a href="#discord.Guild.create_text_channel" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Creates a <a href="#discord.TextChannel" title="discord.TextChannel"><code>TextChannel</code></a> for the guild.

Note that you must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_channels" title="discord.Permissions.manage_channels"><code>manage_channels</code></a> to create the channel.

The <code>overwrites</code> parameter can be used to create a ‘secret’ channel upon creation. This parameter expects a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>dict</code></a> of overwrites with the target (either a <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> or a <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>) as the key and a <a href="#discord.PermissionOverwrite" title="discord.PermissionOverwrite"><code>PermissionOverwrite</code></a> as the value.

Note

Creating a channel of a specified position will not update the position of other channels to follow suit. A follow-up call to <a href="#discord.TextChannel.edit" title="discord.TextChannel.edit"><code>edit()</code></a> will be required to update the position of the channel in the channel list.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

Examples

Creating a basic channel:

```
channel = await guild.create_text_channel('cool-channel')

```

Creating a “secret” channel:

```
overwrites = {
    guild.default_role: discord.PermissionOverwrite(read_messages=False),
    guild.me: discord.PermissionOverwrite(read_messages=True)
}

channel = await guild.create_text_channel('secret', overwrites=overwrites)

```

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The channel’s name.
- **overwrites** (Dict\[Union\[<a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>], <a href="#discord.PermissionOverwrite" title="discord.PermissionOverwrite"><code>PermissionOverwrite</code></a>]) – A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>dict</code></a> of target (either a role or a member) to <a href="#discord.PermissionOverwrite" title="discord.PermissionOverwrite"><code>PermissionOverwrite</code></a> to apply upon creation of a channel. Useful for creating secret channels.
- **category** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.CategoryChannel" title="discord.CategoryChannel"><code>CategoryChannel</code></a>]) – The category to place the newly created channel under. The permissions will be automatically synced to category if no overwrites are provided.
- **position** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The position in the channel list. This is a number that starts at 0. e.g. the top channel is position 0.
- **topic** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The new channel’s topic.
- **slowmode\_delay** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – Specifies the slowmode rate limit for user in this channel, in seconds. The maximum value possible is <code>21600</code>.
- **nsfw** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – To mark the channel as NSFW or not.
- **news** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to create the text channel as a news channel.

  New in version 2.0.
- **default\_auto\_archive\_duration** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) –

  The default auto archive duration for threads created in the text channel (in minutes). Must be one of <code>60</code>, <code>1440</code>, <code>4320</code>, or <code>10080</code>.

  New in version 2.0.
- **default\_thread\_slowmode\_delay** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) –

  The default slowmode delay in seconds for threads created in the text channel.

  New in version 2.3.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for creating this channel. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to create this channel.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Creating the channel failed.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – The permission overwrite information is not in proper form.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The channel that was just created.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.TextChannel" title="discord.TextChannel"><code>TextChannel</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* create_voice_channel(*name*, ***, *reason=None*, *category=None*, *position=...*, *bitrate=...*, *user_limit=...*, *rtc_region=...*, *video_quality_mode=...*, *overwrites=...*, *nsfw=...*)<a href="#discord.Guild.create_voice_channel" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Similar to <a href="#discord.Guild.create_text_channel" title="discord.Guild.create_text_channel"><code>create_text_channel()</code></a> except makes a <a href="#discord.ForumChannel" title="discord.ForumChannel"><code>ForumChannel</code></a> instead.

The <code>overwrites</code> parameter can be used to create a ‘secret’ channel upon creation. This parameter expects a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>dict</code></a> of overwrites with the target (either a <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> or a <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>) as the key and a <a href="#discord.PermissionOverwrite" title="discord.PermissionOverwrite"><code>PermissionOverwrite</code></a> as the value.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The channel’s name.
- **overwrites** (Dict\[Union\[<a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>], <a href="#discord.PermissionOverwrite" title="discord.PermissionOverwrite"><code>PermissionOverwrite</code></a>]) – A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>dict</code></a> of target (either a role or a member) to <a href="#discord.PermissionOverwrite" title="discord.PermissionOverwrite"><code>PermissionOverwrite</code></a> to apply upon creation of a channel. Useful for creating secret channels.
- **topic** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The channel’s topic.
- **category** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.CategoryChannel" title="discord.CategoryChannel"><code>CategoryChannel</code></a>]) – The category to place the newly created channel under. The permissions will be automatically synced to category if no overwrites are provided.
- **position** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The position in the channel list. This is a number that starts at 0. e.g. the top channel is position 0.
- **nsfw** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – To mark the channel as NSFW or not.
- **slowmode\_delay** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – Specifies the slowmode rate limit for users in this channel, in seconds. The maximum possible value is <code>21600</code>.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for creating this channel. Shows up in the audit log.
- **default\_auto\_archive\_duration** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The default auto archive duration for threads created in the forum channel (in minutes). Must be one of <code>60</code>, <code>1440</code>, <code>4320</code>, or <code>10080</code>.
- **default\_thread\_slowmode\_delay** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) –

  The default slowmode delay in seconds for threads created in this forum.

  New in version 2.1.
- **default\_sort\_order** (<a href="#discord.ForumOrderType" title="discord.ForumOrderType"><code>ForumOrderType</code></a>) –

  The default sort order for posts in this forum channel.

  New in version 2.3.
- **default\_reaction\_emoji** (Union\[<a href="#discord.Emoji" title="discord.Emoji"><code>Emoji</code></a>, <a href="#discord.PartialEmoji" title="discord.PartialEmoji"><code>PartialEmoji</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) –

  The default reaction emoji for threads created in this forum to show in the add reaction button.

  New in version 2.3.
- **default\_layout** (<a href="#discord.ForumLayoutType" title="discord.ForumLayoutType"><code>ForumLayoutType</code></a>) –

  The default layout for posts in this forum. This cannot be set if <code>media</code> is set to <code>True</code>.

  New in version 2.3.
- **available\_tags** (Sequence\[<a href="#discord.ForumTag" title="discord.ForumTag"><code>ForumTag</code></a>]) –

  The available tags for this forum channel.

  New in version 2.1.
- **media** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to create a media forum channel.

  New in version 2.6.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to create this channel.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Creating the channel failed.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – The permission overwrite information is not in proper form.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The channel that was just created.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.ForumChannel" title="discord.ForumChannel"><code>ForumChannel</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* leave()<a href="#discord.Guild.leave" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Leaves the guild.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Leaving the guild failed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* delete()<a href="#discord.Guild.delete" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Deletes the guild. You must be the guild owner to delete the guild.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Deleting the guild failed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to delete the guild.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* edit(***, *reason=...*, *name=...*, *description=...*, *icon=...*, *banner=...*, *splash=...*, *discovery_splash=...*, *community=...*, *afk_channel=...*, *owner=...*, *afk_timeout=...*, *default_notifications=...*, *verification_level=...*, *explicit_content_filter=...*, *vanity_code=...*, *system_channel=...*, *system_channel_flags=...*, *preferred_locale=...*, *rules_channel=...*, *public_updates_channel=...*, *premium_progress_bar_enabled=...*, *discoverable=...*, *invites_disabled=...*, *widget_enabled=...*, *widget_channel=...*, *mfa_level=...*, *raid_alerts_disabled=...*, *safety_alerts_channel=...*, *invites_disabled_until=...*, *dms_disabled_until=...*)<a href="#discord.Guild.edit" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Edits the guild.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_guild" title="discord.Permissions.manage_guild"><code>manage_guild</code></a> to edit the guild.

Changed in version 2.0: The newly updated guild is returned.

Changed in version 2.0: The <code>region</code> keyword parameter has been removed.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> or <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>ValueError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The new name of the guild.
- **description** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The new description of the guild. Could be <code>None</code> for no description. This is only available to guilds that contain <code>COMMUNITY</code> in <a href="#discord.Guild.features" title="discord.Guild.features"><code>Guild.features</code></a>.
- **icon** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bytes</code></a>) – A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-bytes-like-object" title="(in Python v3.14)">bytes-like object</a> representing the icon. Only PNG/JPEG is supported. GIF is only available to guilds that contain <code>ANIMATED_ICON</code> in <a href="#discord.Guild.features" title="discord.Guild.features"><code>Guild.features</code></a>. Could be <code>None</code> to denote removal of the icon.
- **banner** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bytes</code></a>) – A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-bytes-like-object" title="(in Python v3.14)">bytes-like object</a> representing the banner. Could be <code>None</code> to denote removal of the banner. This is only available to guilds that contain <code>BANNER</code> in <a href="#discord.Guild.features" title="discord.Guild.features"><code>Guild.features</code></a>.
- **splash** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bytes</code></a>) – A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-bytes-like-object" title="(in Python v3.14)">bytes-like object</a> representing the invite splash. Only PNG/JPEG supported. Could be <code>None</code> to denote removing the splash. This is only available to guilds that contain <code>INVITE_SPLASH</code> in <a href="#discord.Guild.features" title="discord.Guild.features"><code>Guild.features</code></a>.
- **discovery\_splash** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bytes</code></a>) –

  A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-bytes-like-object" title="(in Python v3.14)">bytes-like object</a> representing the discovery splash. Only PNG/JPEG supported. Could be <code>None</code> to denote removing the splash. This is only available to guilds that contain <code>DISCOVERABLE</code> in <a href="#discord.Guild.features" title="discord.Guild.features"><code>Guild.features</code></a>.

  New in version 2.0.
- **community** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether the guild should be a Community guild. If set to <code>True</code>, both <code>rules_channel</code> and <code>public_updates_channel</code> parameters are required.

  New in version 2.0.
- **afk\_channel** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.VoiceChannel" title="discord.VoiceChannel"><code>VoiceChannel</code></a>]) – The new channel that is the AFK channel. Could be <code>None</code> for no AFK channel.
- **afk\_timeout** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The number of seconds until someone is moved to the AFK channel.
- **owner** (<a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>) –

  The new owner of the guild to transfer ownership to. Note that you must be owner of the guild to do this.

  Deprecated since version 2.6: This parameter is deprecated and will be removed in a future version as bots can no longer own guilds.
- **verification\_level** (<a href="#discord.VerificationLevel" title="discord.VerificationLevel"><code>VerificationLevel</code></a>) – The new verification level for the guild.
- **default\_notifications** (<a href="#discord.NotificationLevel" title="discord.NotificationLevel"><code>NotificationLevel</code></a>) – The new default notification level for the guild.
- **explicit\_content\_filter** (<a href="#discord.ContentFilter" title="discord.ContentFilter"><code>ContentFilter</code></a>) – The new explicit content filter for the guild.
- **vanity\_code** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) –

  The new vanity code for the guild.

  Deprecated since version 2.6: This parameter is deprecated and will be removed in a future version as bots can no longer set this.
- **system\_channel** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.TextChannel" title="discord.TextChannel"><code>TextChannel</code></a>]) – The new channel that is used for the system channel. Could be <code>None</code> for no system channel.
- **system\_channel\_flags** (<a href="#discord.SystemChannelFlags" title="discord.SystemChannelFlags"><code>SystemChannelFlags</code></a>) – The new system channel settings to use with the new system channel.
- **preferred\_locale** (<a href="#discord.Locale" title="discord.Locale"><code>Locale</code></a>) –

  The new preferred locale for the guild. Used as the primary language in the guild.

  Changed in version 2.0: Now accepts an enum instead of <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>.
- **rules\_channel** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.TextChannel" title="discord.TextChannel"><code>TextChannel</code></a>]) –

  The new channel that is used for rules. This is only available to guilds that contain <code>COMMUNITY</code> in <a href="#discord.Guild.features" title="discord.Guild.features"><code>Guild.features</code></a>. Could be <code>None</code> for no rules channel.

  New in version 1.4.
- **public\_updates\_channel** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.TextChannel" title="discord.TextChannel"><code>TextChannel</code></a>]) –

  The new channel that is used for public updates from Discord. This is only available to guilds that contain <code>COMMUNITY</code> in <a href="#discord.Guild.features" title="discord.Guild.features"><code>Guild.features</code></a>. Could be <code>None</code> for no public updates channel.

  New in version 1.4.
- **premium\_progress\_bar\_enabled** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether the premium AKA server boost level progress bar should be enabled for the guild.

  New in version 2.0.
- **discoverable** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether server discovery is enabled for this guild.

  New in version 2.1.
- **invites\_disabled** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether joining via invites should be disabled for the guild.

  New in version 2.1.
- **widget\_enabled** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to enable the widget for the guild.

  New in version 2.3.
- **widget\_channel** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>]) –

  The new widget channel. <code>None</code> removes the widget channel.

  New in version 2.3.
- **mfa\_level** (<a href="#discord.MFALevel" title="discord.MFALevel"><code>MFALevel</code></a>) –

  The new guild’s Multi-Factor Authentication requirement level. Note that you must be owner of the guild to do this.

  New in version 2.3.

  Deprecated since version 2.6: This parameter is deprecated and will be removed in a future version as bots can no longer own guilds.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for editing this guild. Shows up on the audit log.
- **raid\_alerts\_disabled** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether the alerts for raid protection should be disabled for the guild.

  New in version 2.3.
- **safety\_alerts\_channel** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.TextChannel" title="discord.TextChannel"><code>TextChannel</code></a>]) –

  The new channel that is used for safety alerts. This is only available to guilds that contain <code>COMMUNITY</code> in <a href="#discord.Guild.features" title="discord.Guild.features"><code>Guild.features</code></a>. Could be <code>None</code> for no safety alerts channel.

  New in version 2.3.
- **invites\_disabled\_until** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]) –

  The time when invites should be enabled again, or <code>None</code> to disable the action. This must be a timezone-aware datetime object. Consider using <a href="#discord.utils.utcnow" title="discord.utils.utcnow"><code>utils.utcnow()</code></a>.

  New in version 2.4.
- **dms\_disabled\_until** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]) –

  The time when direct messages should be allowed again, or <code>None</code> to disable the action. This must be a timezone-aware datetime object. Consider using <a href="#discord.utils.utcnow" title="discord.utils.utcnow"><code>utils.utcnow()</code></a>.

  New in version 2.4.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to edit the guild.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Editing the guild failed.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – The image format passed in to <code>icon</code> is invalid. It must be PNG or JPG. This is also raised if you are not the owner of the guild and request an ownership transfer.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – The type passed to the <code>default_notifications</code>, <code>rules_channel</code>, <code>public_updates_channel</code>, <code>safety_alerts_channel</code> <code>verification_level</code>, <code>explicit_content_filter</code>, <code>system_channel_flags</code>, or <code>mfa_level</code> parameter was of the incorrect type.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The newly updated guild. Note that this has the same limitations as mentioned in <a href="#discord.Client.fetch_guild" title="discord.Client.fetch_guild"><code>Client.fetch_guild()</code></a> and may not have full data.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_channels()<a href="#discord.Guild.fetch_channels" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

New in version 1.2.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>

- <a href="#discord.InvalidData" title="discord.InvalidData">**InvalidData**</a> – An unknown channel type was received from Discord.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>

All channels in the guild.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>

Sequence\[<a href="#discord.abc.GuildChannel" title="discord.abc.GuildChannel"><code>abc.GuildChannel</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* active_threads()<a href="#discord.Guild.active_threads" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>

List\[<a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*async for ... in* fetch_members(***, *limit=1000*, *after=...*)<a href="#discord.Guild.fetch_members" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Retrieves an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterator" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterator</a> that enables receiving the guild’s members. In order to use this, <a href="#discord.Intents.members" title="discord.Intents.members"><code>Intents.members()</code></a> must be enabled.

Note

This method is an API call. For general usage, consider <a href="#discord.Guild.members" title="discord.Guild.members"><code>members</code></a> instead.

New in version 1.3.

All parameters are optional.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **limit** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) – The number of members to retrieve. Defaults to 1000. Pass <code>None</code> to fetch all members. Note that this is potentially slow.
- **after** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve members after this date or object. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.ClientException" title="discord.ClientException">**ClientException**</a> – The members intent is not enabled.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Getting the members failed.

</dd><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> – The member with the member data parsed.

</dd></dl>

Examples

Usage

```
async for member in guild.fetch_members(limit=150):
    print(member.name)

```

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_member(*member_id*, */*)<a href="#discord.Guild.fetch_member" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Retrieves a <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> from a guild ID, and a member ID.

Note

This method is an API call. If you have <a href="#discord.Intents.members" title="discord.Intents.members"><code>Intents.members</code></a> and member cache enabled, consider <a href="#discord.Guild.get_member" title="discord.Guild.get_member"><code>get_member()</code></a> instead.

Changed in version 2.0: <code>member_id</code> parameter is now positional-only.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**member\_id** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The member’s ID to fetch from.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have access to the guild.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Fetching the member failed.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The member could not be found.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The member from the member ID.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_ban(*user*)<a href="#discord.Guild.fetch_ban" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>

The <a href="#discord.BanEntry" title="discord.BanEntry"><code>BanEntry</code></a> object for the specified user.

<a href="#discord.BanEntry" title="discord.BanEntry"><code>BanEntry</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_channel(*channel_id*, */*)<a href="#discord.Guild.fetch_channel" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Retrieves a <a href="#discord.abc.GuildChannel" title="discord.abc.GuildChannel"><code>abc.GuildChannel</code></a> or <a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a> with the specified ID.

Note

This method is an API call. For general usage, consider <a href="#discord.Guild.get_channel_or_thread" title="discord.Guild.get_channel_or_thread"><code>get_channel_or_thread()</code></a> instead.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.InvalidData" title="discord.InvalidData">**InvalidData**</a> – An unknown channel type was received from Discord or the guild the channel belongs to is not the same as the one in this object points to.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Retrieving the channel failed.

The channel from the ID.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*async for ... in* bans(***, *limit=1000*, *before=...*, *after=...*)<a href="#discord.Guild.bans" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Retrieves an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterator" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterator</a> of the users that are banned from the guild as a <a href="#discord.BanEntry" title="discord.BanEntry"><code>BanEntry</code></a>.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.ban_members" title="discord.Permissions.ban_members"><code>ban_members</code></a> to get this information.

Changed in version 2.0: Due to a breaking change in Discord’s API, this now returns a paginated iterator instead of a list.

Examples

Usage

```
async for entry in guild.bans(limit=150):
    print(entry.user, entry.reason)

```

Flattening into a list

```
bans = [entry async for entry in guild.bans(limit=2000)]
# bans is now a list of BanEntry...

```

All parameters are optional.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **limit** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) – The number of bans to retrieve. If <code>None</code>, it retrieves every ban in the guild. Note, however, that this would make it a slow operation. Defaults to <code>1000</code>.
- **before** (<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>) – Retrieves bans before this user.
- **after** (<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>) – Retrieve bans after this user.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have proper permissions to get the information.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – An error occurred while fetching the information.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – Both <code>after</code> and <code>before</code> were provided, as Discord does not support this type of pagination.

</dd><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.BanEntry" title="discord.BanEntry"><code>BanEntry</code></a> – The ban entry of the banned user.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* prune_members(***, *days*, *compute_prune_count=True*, *roles=...*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Guild.prune_members" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Prunes the guild from its inactive members.

The inactive members are denoted if they have not logged on in <code>days</code> number of days and they have no roles.

You must have both <a href="#discord.Permissions.kick_members" title="discord.Permissions.kick_members"><code>kick_members</code></a> and <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_guild" title="discord.Permissions.manage_guild"><code>manage_guild</code></a> to do this.

To check how many members you would prune without actually pruning, see the <a href="#discord.Guild.estimate_pruned_members" title="discord.Guild.estimate_pruned_members"><code>estimate_pruned_members()</code></a> function.

To prune members that have specific roles see the <code>roles</code> parameter.

Changed in version 1.4: The <code>roles</code> keyword-only parameter was added.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **days** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The number of days before counting as inactive.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for doing this action. Shows up on the audit log.
- **compute\_prune\_count** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to compute the prune count. This defaults to <code>True</code> which makes it prone to timeouts in very large guilds. In order to prevent timeouts, you must set this to <code>False</code>. If this is set to <code>False</code>, then this function will always return <code>None</code>.
- **roles** (List\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>]) – A list of <a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a> that represent roles to include in the pruning process. If a member has a role that is not specified, they’ll be excluded.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to prune members.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – An error occurred while pruning members.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – An integer was not passed for <code>days</code>.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The number of members pruned. If <code>compute_prune_count</code> is <code>False</code> then this returns <code>None</code>.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* templates()<a href="#discord.Guild.templates" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Gets the list of templates from this guild.

New in version 1.7.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You don’t have permissions to get the templates.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The templates for this guild.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

List\[<a href="#discord.Template" title="discord.Template"><code>Template</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* webhooks()<a href="#discord.Guild.webhooks" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

<dd>

<dd>

The webhooks for this guild.

<dd>

List\[<a href="#discord.Webhook" title="discord.Webhook"><code>Webhook</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* estimate_pruned_members(***, *days*, *roles=...*)<a href="#discord.Guild.estimate_pruned_members" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Similar to <a href="#discord.Guild.prune_members" title="discord.Guild.prune_members"><code>prune_members()</code></a> except instead of actually pruning members, it returns how many members it would prune from the guild had it been called.

Changed in version 2.0: The returned value can be <code>None</code>.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **days** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The number of days before counting as inactive.
- **roles** (List\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>]) –

  A list of <a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a> that represent roles to include in the estimate. If a member has a role that is not specified, they’ll be excluded.

  New in version 1.7.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to prune members.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – An error occurred while fetching the prune members estimate.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – An integer was not passed for <code>days</code>.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The number of members estimated to be pruned.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* invites()<a href="#discord.Guild.invites" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

</dl><dl><dt>*await* create_sticker(***, *name*, *description=...*, *emoji*, *file*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Guild.create_sticker" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Creates a <a href="#discord.Sticker" title="discord.Sticker"><code>Sticker</code></a> for the guild.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_emojis_and_stickers" title="discord.Permissions.manage_emojis_and_stickers"><code>manage_emojis_and_stickers</code></a> to do this.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The sticker name. Must be between 2 and 30 characters.
- **description** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The sticker’s description. Can be an empty string or a string between 2 and 100 characters. Defaults to an empty string if not provided.
- **emoji** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The emoji tag associated with the sticker. This corresponds to the <code>tags</code> field in Discord’s API, which is used for emoji autocomplete and suggestion purposes. For correct rendering in Discord’s UI, this should ideally be a raw Unicode emoji or the string ID of a custom emoji. Any string up to 200 characters is accepted.
- **file** (<a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a>) – The file of the sticker to upload.
- **reason** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The reason for creating this sticker. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – An error occurred creating a sticker.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The created sticker.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.GuildSticker" title="discord.GuildSticker"><code>GuildSticker</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>

</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_scheduled_event(*scheduled_event_id*, */*, ***, *with_counts=True*)<a href="#discord.Guild.fetch_scheduled_event" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Retrieves a scheduled event from the guild.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **scheduled\_event\_id** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The scheduled event ID.
- **with\_counts** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to include the number of users that are subscribed to the event. Defaults to <code>True</code>.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The scheduled event was not found.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Retrieving the scheduled event failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The scheduled event.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.ScheduledEvent" title="discord.ScheduledEvent"><code>ScheduledEvent</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* create_scheduled_event(***, *name*, *start_time*, *entity_type=...*, *privacy_level=...*, *channel=...*, *location=...*, *end_time=...*, *description=...*, *image=...*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Guild.create_scheduled_event" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Creates a scheduled event for the guild.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_events" title="discord.Permissions.manage_events"><code>manage_events</code></a> to do this.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The name of the scheduled event.
- **description** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The description of the scheduled event.
- **channel** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>]) –

  The channel to send the scheduled event to. If the channel is a <a href="#discord.StageInstance" title="discord.StageInstance"><code>StageInstance</code></a> or <a href="#discord.VoiceChannel" title="discord.VoiceChannel"><code>VoiceChannel</code></a> then it automatically sets the entity type.

  Required if <code>entity_type</code> is either <a href="#discord.EntityType.voice" title="discord.EntityType.voice"><code>EntityType.voice</code></a> or <a href="#discord.EntityType.stage_instance" title="discord.EntityType.stage_instance"><code>EntityType.stage_instance</code></a>.
- **start\_time** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>) – The scheduled start time of the scheduled event. This must be a timezone-aware datetime object. Consider using <a href="#discord.utils.utcnow" title="discord.utils.utcnow"><code>utils.utcnow()</code></a>.
- **end\_time** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>) –

  The scheduled end time of the scheduled event. This must be a timezone-aware datetime object. Consider using <a href="#discord.utils.utcnow" title="discord.utils.utcnow"><code>utils.utcnow()</code></a>.

  Required if the entity type is <a href="#discord.EntityType.external" title="discord.EntityType.external"><code>EntityType.external</code></a>.
- **privacy\_level** (<a href="#discord.PrivacyLevel" title="discord.PrivacyLevel"><code>PrivacyLevel</code></a>) – The privacy level of the scheduled event.
- **entity\_type** (<a href="#discord.EntityType" title="discord.EntityType"><code>EntityType</code></a>) – The entity type of the scheduled event. If the channel is a <a href="#discord.StageInstance" title="discord.StageInstance"><code>StageInstance</code></a> or <a href="#discord.VoiceChannel" title="discord.VoiceChannel"><code>VoiceChannel</code></a> then this is automatically set to the appropriate entity type. If no channel is passed then the entity type is assumed to be <a href="#discord.EntityType.external" title="discord.EntityType.external"><code>EntityType.external</code></a>
- **image** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bytes</code></a>) – The image of the scheduled event.
- **location** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) –

  The location of the scheduled event.

  Required if the <code>entity_type</code> is <a href="#discord.EntityType.external" title="discord.EntityType.external"><code>EntityType.external</code></a>.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for creating this scheduled event. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – <code>image</code> was not a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-bytes-like-object" title="(in Python v3.14)">bytes-like object</a>, or <code>privacy_level</code> was not a <a href="#discord.PrivacyLevel" title="discord.PrivacyLevel"><code>PrivacyLevel</code></a>, or <code>entity_type</code> was not an <a href="#discord.EntityType" title="discord.EntityType"><code>EntityType</code></a>, <code>status</code> was not an <a href="#discord.EventStatus" title="discord.EventStatus"><code>EventStatus</code></a>, or an argument was provided that was incompatible with the provided <code>entity_type</code>.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – <code>start_time</code> or <code>end_time</code> was not a timezone-aware datetime object.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You are not allowed to create scheduled events.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Creating the scheduled event failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The created scheduled event.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.ScheduledEvent" title="discord.ScheduledEvent"><code>ScheduledEvent</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_emojis()<a href="#discord.Guild.fetch_emojis" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Retrieves all custom <a href="#discord.Emoji" title="discord.Emoji"><code>Emoji</code></a>s from the guild.

<a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – An error occurred fetching the emojis.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_emoji(*emoji_id*, */*)<a href="#discord.Guild.fetch_emoji" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Retrieves a custom <a href="#discord.Emoji" title="discord.Emoji"><code>Emoji</code></a> from the guild.

Note

This method is an API call. For general usage, consider iterating over <a href="#discord.Guild.emojis" title="discord.Guild.emojis"><code>emojis</code></a> instead.

Changed in version 2.0: <code>emoji_id</code> parameter is now positional-only.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**emoji\_id** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The emoji’s ID.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The emoji requested could not be found.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – An error occurred fetching the emoji.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The retrieved emoji.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Emoji" title="discord.Emoji"><code>Emoji</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* create_custom_emoji(***, *name*, *image*, *roles=...*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Guild.create_custom_emoji" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Creates a custom <a href="#discord.Emoji" title="discord.Emoji"><code>Emoji</code></a> for the guild.

There is currently a limit of 50 static and animated emojis respectively per guild, unless the guild has the <code>MORE_EMOJI</code> feature which extends the limit to 200.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_emojis" title="discord.Permissions.manage_emojis"><code>manage_emojis</code></a> to do this.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The emoji name. Must be at least 2 characters.
- **image** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bytes</code></a>) – The <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-bytes-like-object" title="(in Python v3.14)">bytes-like object</a> representing the image data to use. Only JPG, PNG and GIF images are supported.
- **roles** (List\[<a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>]) – A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#list" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>list</code></a> of <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>s that can use this emoji. Leave empty to make it available to everyone.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for creating this emoji. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You are not allowed to create emojis.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – An error occurred creating an emoji.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The created emoji.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Emoji" title="discord.Emoji"><code>Emoji</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* delete_emoji(*emoji*, */*, ***, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Guild.delete_emoji" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Deletes the custom <a href="#discord.Emoji" title="discord.Emoji"><code>Emoji</code></a> from the guild.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_emojis" title="discord.Permissions.manage_emojis"><code>manage_emojis</code></a> to do this.

Changed in version 2.0: <code>emoji</code> parameter is now positional-only.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **emoji** (<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>) – The emoji you are deleting.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for deleting this emoji. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You are not allowed to delete emojis.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – An error occurred deleting the emoji.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_roles()<a href="#discord.Guild.fetch_roles" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

<a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Retrieving the roles failed.

All roles in the guild.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

List\[<a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_role(*role_id*, */*)<a href="#discord.Guild.fetch_role" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Note

This method is an API call. For general usage, consider <a href="#discord.Guild.get_role" title="discord.Guild.get_role"><code>get_role</code></a> instead.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**role\_id** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The role’s ID.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>

- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The role requested could not be found.

The retrieved role.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* create_role(***, *name=...*, *permissions=...*, *color=...*, *colour=...*, *hoist=...*, *display_icon=...*, *mentionable=...*, *reason=None*, *secondary_color=...*, *tertiary_color=...*, *secondary_colour=...*, *tertiary_colour=...*)<a href="#discord.Guild.create_role" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Creates a <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a> for the guild.

All fields are optional.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_roles" title="discord.Permissions.manage_roles"><code>manage_roles</code></a> to do this.

Changed in version 1.6: Can now pass <code>int</code> to <code>colour</code> keyword-only parameter.

New in version 2.0: The <code>display_icon</code> keyword-only parameter was added.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

Changed in version 2.6: The <code>colour</code> and <code>color</code> parameters now set the role’s primary color.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The role name. Defaults to ‘new role’.
- **permissions** (<a href="#discord.Permissions" title="discord.Permissions"><code>Permissions</code></a>) – The permissions to have. Defaults to no permissions.
- **colour** (Union\[<a href="#discord.Colour" title="discord.Colour"><code>Colour</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) – The colour for the role. Defaults to <a href="#discord.Colour.default" title="discord.Colour.default"><code>Colour.default()</code></a>. This is aliased to <code>color</code> as well.
- **secondary\_colour** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.Colour" title="discord.Colour"><code>Colour</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]]) –

  The secondary colour for the role.

  New in version 2.6.
- **tertiary\_colour** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.Colour" title="discord.Colour"><code>Colour</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]]) –

  The tertiary colour for the role. Can only be used for the holographic role preset, which is <code>(11127295, 16759788, 16761760)</code>

  New in version 2.6.
- **hoist** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Indicates if the role should be shown separately in the member list. Defaults to <code>False</code>.
- **display\_icon** (Union\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bytes</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-bytes-like-object" title="(in Python v3.14)">bytes-like object</a> representing the icon or <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a> representing unicode emoji that should be used as a role icon. Only PNG/JPEG is supported. This is only available to guilds that contain <code>ROLE_ICONS</code> in <a href="#discord.Guild.features" title="discord.Guild.features"><code>features</code></a>.
- **mentionable** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Indicates if the role should be mentionable by others. Defaults to <code>False</code>.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for creating this role. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to create the role.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Creating the role failed.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – An invalid keyword argument was given.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The newly created role.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* edit_role_positions(*positions*, ***, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Guild.edit_role_positions" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Bulk edits a list of <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a> in the guild.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_roles" title="discord.Permissions.manage_roles"><code>manage_roles</code></a> to do this.

New in version 1.4.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

Example

```
positions = {
    bots_role: 1, # penultimate role
    tester_role: 2,
    admin_role: 6
}

await guild.edit_role_positions(positions=positions)

```

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **positions** – A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>dict</code></a> of <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a> to <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a> to change the positions of each given role.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for editing the role positions. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to move the roles.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Moving the roles failed.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – An invalid keyword argument was given.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

A list of all the roles in the guild.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

List\[<a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* role_member_counts()<a href="#discord.Guild.role_member_counts" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Retrieves a mapping of roles to the number of members that have it.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_roles" title="discord.Permissions.manage_roles"><code>manage_roles</code></a> to do this.

New in version 2.7.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to view the role member counts.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Retrieving the role member counts failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

A mapping of roles to the number of members that have it. If a role is not found in the cache, it will be represented as an <a href="#discord.Object" title="discord.Object"><code>Object</code></a> instead of a <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

Dict\[Union\[<a href="#discord.Object" title="discord.Object"><code>Object</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>], <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* welcome_screen()<a href="#discord.Guild.welcome_screen" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Returns the guild’s welcome screen.

The guild must have <code>COMMUNITY</code> in <a href="#discord.Guild.features" title="discord.Guild.features"><code>features</code></a>.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_guild" title="discord.Permissions.manage_guild"><code>manage_guild</code></a> to do this.as well.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>
