</dl><dl><dt>*await* ban(*user*, ***, *reason=None*, *delete_message_days=...*, *delete_message_seconds=...*)<a href="#discord.Guild.ban" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Bans a user from the guild.

The user must meet the <a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a> abc.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.ban_members" title="discord.Permissions.ban_members"><code>ban_members</code></a> to do this.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **user** (<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>) – The user to ban from the guild.
- **delete\_message\_days** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) –

  The number of days worth of messages to delete from the user in the guild. The minimum is 0 and the maximum is 7. Defaults to 1 day if neither <code>delete_message_days</code> nor <code>delete_message_seconds</code> are passed.

  Deprecated since version 2.1.
- **delete\_message\_seconds** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) –

  The number of seconds worth of messages to delete from the user in the guild. The minimum is 0 and the maximum is 604800 (7 days). Defaults to 1 day if neither <code>delete_message_days</code> nor <code>delete_message_seconds</code> are passed.

  New in version 2.1.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason the user got banned.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The requested user was not found.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to ban.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Banning failed.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – You specified both <code>delete_message_days</code> and <code>delete_message_seconds</code>.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* unban(*user*, ***, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Guild.unban" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Unbanning failed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* bulk_ban(*users*, ***, *reason=None*, *delete_message_seconds=86400*)<a href="#discord.Guild.bulk_ban" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.ban_members" title="discord.Permissions.ban_members"><code>ban_members</code></a> and <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_guild" title="discord.Permissions.manage_guild"><code>manage_guild</code></a> to do this.

New in version 2.4.

- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason the users got banned.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The result of the bulk ban operation.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.BulkBanResult" title="discord.BulkBanResult"><code>BulkBanResult</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*async for ... in* audit_logs(***, *limit=100*, *before=...*, *after=...*, *oldest_first=...*, *user=...*, *action=...*)<a href="#discord.Guild.audit_logs" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterator" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterator</a> that enables receiving the guild’s audit logs.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.view_audit_log" title="discord.Permissions.view_audit_log"><code>view_audit_log</code></a> to do this.

Examples

Getting the first 100 entries:

```
async for entry in guild.audit_logs(limit=100):
    print(f'{entry.user} did {entry.action} to {entry.target}')

```

Getting entries for a specific action:

```
async for entry in guild.audit_logs(action=discord.AuditLogAction.ban):
    print(f'{entry.user} banned {entry.target}')

```

Getting entries made by a specific user:

```
entries = [entry async for entry in guild.audit_logs(limit=None, user=guild.me)]
await channel.send(f'I made {len(entries)} moderation actions.')

```

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **limit** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) – The number of entries to retrieve. If <code>None</code> retrieve all entries.
- **before** (Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]) – Retrieve entries before this date or entry. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.
- **after** (Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]) – Retrieve entries after this date or entry. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.
- **oldest\_first** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – If set to <code>True</code>, return entries in oldest-&gt;newest order. Defaults to <code>True</code> if <code>after</code> is specified, otherwise <code>False</code>.
- **user** (<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>) – The moderator to filter entries from.
- **action** (<a href="#discord.AuditLogAction" title="discord.AuditLogAction"><code>AuditLogAction</code></a>) – The action to filter with.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You are not allowed to fetch audit logs
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – An error occurred while fetching the audit logs.

</dd><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.AuditLogEntry" title="discord.AuditLogEntry"><code>AuditLogEntry</code></a> – The audit log entry.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* widget()<a href="#discord.Guild.widget" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* edit_widget(***, *enabled=...*, *channel=...*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Guild.edit_widget" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **enabled** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to enable the widget for the guild.

- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for editing this widget. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* chunk(***, *cache=True*)<a href="#discord.Guild.chunk" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Requests all members that belong to this guild. In order to use this, <a href="#discord.Intents.members" title="discord.Intents.members"><code>Intents.members()</code></a> must be enabled.

This is a websocket operation and can be slow.

New in version 1.5.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**cache** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to cache the members as well.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.ClientException" title="discord.ClientException">**ClientException**</a> – The members intent is not enabled.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The list of members in the guild.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

List\[<a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* query_members(*query=None*, ***, *limit=5*, *user_ids=None*, *presences=False*, *cache=True*)<a href="#discord.Guild.query_members" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Request members of this guild whose username or nickname starts with the given query. This is a websocket operation.

New in version 1.3.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **query** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The string that the username or nickname should start with.
- **limit** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The maximum number of members to send back. This must be a number between 5 and 100.
- **presences** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to request for presences to be provided. This defaults to <code>False</code>.

  New in version 1.6.
- **cache** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to cache the members internally. This makes operations such as <a href="#discord.Guild.get_member" title="discord.Guild.get_member"><code>get_member()</code></a> work for those that matched.
- **user\_ids** (Optional\[List\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]]) –

  List of user IDs to search for. If the user ID is not in the guild then it won’t be returned.

  New in version 1.4.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-exceptions.html#asyncio.TimeoutError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**asyncio.TimeoutError**</a> – The query timed out waiting for the members.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – Invalid parameters were passed to the function
- <a href="#discord.ClientException" title="discord.ClientException">**ClientException**</a> – The presences intent is not enabled.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The list of members that have matched the query.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

List\[<a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* change_voice_state(***, *channel*, *self_mute=False*, *self_deaf=False*)<a href="#discord.Guild.change_voice_state" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

</dl><dl><dt>*await* create_automod_rule(***, *name*, *event_type*, *trigger*, *actions*, *enabled=False*, *exempt_roles=...*, *exempt_channels=...*, *reason=...*)<a href="#discord.Guild.create_automod_rule" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Create an automod rule.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_guild" title="discord.Permissions.manage_guild"><code>Permissions.manage_guild</code></a> to do this.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The name of the automod rule.
- **event\_type** (<a href="#discord.AutoModRuleEventType" title="discord.AutoModRuleEventType"><code>AutoModRuleEventType</code></a>) – The type of event that the automod rule will trigger on.
- **trigger** (<a href="#discord.AutoModTrigger" title="discord.AutoModTrigger"><code>AutoModTrigger</code></a>) – The trigger that will trigger the automod rule.
- **actions** (List\[<a href="#discord.AutoModRuleAction" title="discord.AutoModRuleAction"><code>AutoModRuleAction</code></a>]) – The actions that will be taken when the automod rule is triggered.

- **exempt\_roles** (Sequence\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>]) – A list of roles that will be exempt from the automod rule.
- **exempt\_channels** (Sequence\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>]) – A list of channels that will be exempt from the automod rule.
- **reason** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The reason for creating this automod rule. Shows up on the audit log.

</dl><dl><dt>*await* create_soundboard_sound(***, *name*, *sound*, *volume=1*, *emoji=None*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Guild.create_soundboard_sound" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Creates a <a href="#discord.SoundboardSound" title="discord.SoundboardSound"><code>SoundboardSound</code></a> for the guild. You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.create_expressions" title="discord.Permissions.create_expressions"><code>Permissions.create_expressions</code></a> to do this.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>

- **sound** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bytes</code></a>) – The <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-bytes-like-object" title="(in Python v3.14)">bytes-like object</a> representing the sound data. Only MP3 and OGG sound files that don’t exceed the duration of 5.2s are supported.
- **volume** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>float</code></a>) – The volume of the sound. Must be between 0 and 1. Defaults to <code>1</code>.

- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for creating the sound. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Creating the soundboard sound failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The newly created soundboard sound.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.SoundboardSound" title="discord.SoundboardSound"><code>SoundboardSound</code></a>

</dl><dl><dt>*await* start(***, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.ScheduledEvent.start" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Starts the scheduled event.

Shorthand for:

```
await event.edit(status=EventStatus.active)

```

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for starting the scheduled event.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – The scheduled event has already started or has ended.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to start the scheduled event.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – The scheduled event could not be started.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The scheduled event that was started.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.ScheduledEvent" title="discord.ScheduledEvent"><code>ScheduledEvent</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* end(***, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.ScheduledEvent.end" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Ends the scheduled event.

Shorthand for:

```
await event.edit(status=EventStatus.completed)

```

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for ending the scheduled event.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – The scheduled event is not active or has already ended.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to end the scheduled event.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – The scheduled event could not be ended.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The scheduled event that was ended.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.ScheduledEvent" title="discord.ScheduledEvent"><code>ScheduledEvent</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* cancel(***, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.ScheduledEvent.cancel" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Cancels the scheduled event.

Shorthand for:

```
await event.edit(status=EventStatus.cancelled)

```

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for cancelling the scheduled event.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – The scheduled event is already running.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to cancel the scheduled event.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – The scheduled event could not be cancelled.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The scheduled event that was cancelled.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.ScheduledEvent" title="discord.ScheduledEvent"><code>ScheduledEvent</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* edit(***, *name=...*, *description=...*, *channel=...*, *start_time=...*, *end_time=...*, *privacy_level=...*, *entity_type=...*, *status=...*, *image=...*, *location=...*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.ScheduledEvent.edit" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Edits the scheduled event.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_events" title="discord.Permissions.manage_events"><code>manage_events</code></a> to do this.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The name of the scheduled event.
- **description** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The description of the scheduled event.
- **channel** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>]) –

  The channel to put the scheduled event in. If the channel is a <a href="#discord.StageInstance" title="discord.StageInstance"><code>StageInstance</code></a> or <a href="#discord.VoiceChannel" title="discord.VoiceChannel"><code>VoiceChannel</code></a> then it automatically sets the entity type.

  Required if the entity type is either <a href="#discord.EntityType.voice" title="discord.EntityType.voice"><code>EntityType.voice</code></a> or <a href="#discord.EntityType.stage_instance" title="discord.EntityType.stage_instance"><code>EntityType.stage_instance</code></a>.
- **start\_time** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>) – The time that the scheduled event will start. This must be a timezone-aware datetime object. Consider using <a href="#discord.utils.utcnow" title="discord.utils.utcnow"><code>utils.utcnow()</code></a>.
- **end\_time** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]) –

  The time that the scheduled event will end. This must be a timezone-aware datetime object. Consider using <a href="#discord.utils.utcnow" title="discord.utils.utcnow"><code>utils.utcnow()</code></a>.

  If the entity type is either <a href="#discord.EntityType.voice" title="discord.EntityType.voice"><code>EntityType.voice</code></a> or <a href="#discord.EntityType.stage_instance" title="discord.EntityType.stage_instance"><code>EntityType.stage_instance</code></a>, the end\_time can be cleared by passing <code>None</code>.

  Required if the entity type is <a href="#discord.EntityType.external" title="discord.EntityType.external"><code>EntityType.external</code></a>.
- **privacy\_level** (<a href="#discord.PrivacyLevel" title="discord.PrivacyLevel"><code>PrivacyLevel</code></a>) – The privacy level of the scheduled event.
- **entity\_type** (<a href="#discord.EntityType" title="discord.EntityType"><code>EntityType</code></a>) – The new entity type. If the channel is a <a href="#discord.StageInstance" title="discord.StageInstance"><code>StageInstance</code></a> or <a href="#discord.VoiceChannel" title="discord.VoiceChannel"><code>VoiceChannel</code></a> then this is automatically set to the appropriate entity type.
- **status** (<a href="#discord.EventStatus" title="discord.EventStatus"><code>EventStatus</code></a>) – The new status of the scheduled event.
- **image** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bytes</code></a>]) – The new image of the scheduled event or <code>None</code> to remove the image.
- **location** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) –

  The new location of the scheduled event.

  Required if the entity type is <a href="#discord.EntityType.external" title="discord.EntityType.external"><code>EntityType.external</code></a>.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for editing the scheduled event. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – <code>image</code> was not a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-bytes-like-object" title="(in Python v3.14)">bytes-like object</a>, or <code>privacy_level</code> was not a <a href="#discord.PrivacyLevel" title="discord.PrivacyLevel"><code>PrivacyLevel</code></a>, or <code>entity_type</code> was not an <a href="#discord.EntityType" title="discord.EntityType"><code>EntityType</code></a>, <code>status</code> was not an <a href="#discord.EventStatus" title="discord.EventStatus"><code>EventStatus</code></a>, or an argument was provided that was incompatible with the scheduled event’s entity type.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – <code>start_time</code> or <code>end_time</code> was not a timezone-aware datetime object.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to edit the scheduled event.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Editing the scheduled event failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The edited scheduled event.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.ScheduledEvent" title="discord.ScheduledEvent"><code>ScheduledEvent</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* delete(***, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.ScheduledEvent.delete" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Deletes the scheduled event.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_events" title="discord.Permissions.manage_events"><code>manage_events</code></a> to do this.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for deleting the scheduled event. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to delete the scheduled event.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Deleting the scheduled event failed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*async for ... in* users(***, *limit=None*, *before=None*, *after=None*, *oldest_first=...*)<a href="#discord.ScheduledEvent.users" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Retrieves all <a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a> that are subscribed to this event.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.members" title="discord.Intents.members"><code>Intents.members</code></a> to get information about members other than yourself.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Retrieving the members failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

All subscribed users of this event.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

List\[<a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl>

Optional\[<a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>] The role which the integration uses for subscribers.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*await* edit(***, *expire_behaviour=...*, *expire_grace_period=...*, *enable_emoticons=...*)<a href="#discord.StreamIntegration.edit" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Edits the integration.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_guild" title="discord.Permissions.manage_guild"><code>manage_guild</code></a> to do this.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **expire\_behaviour** (<a href="#discord.ExpireBehaviour" title="discord.ExpireBehaviour"><code>ExpireBehaviour</code></a>) – The behaviour when an integration subscription lapses. Aliased to <code>expire_behavior</code> as well.
- **expire\_grace\_period** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The period (in days) where the integration will ignore lapsed subscriptions.
- **enable\_emoticons** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Where emoticons should be synced for this integration (currently twitch only).

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permission to edit the integration.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Editing the guild failed.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – <code>expire_behaviour</code> did not receive a <a href="#discord.ExpireBehaviour" title="discord.ExpireBehaviour"><code>ExpireBehaviour</code></a>.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* sync()<a href="#discord.StreamIntegration.sync" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Syncs the integration.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_guild" title="discord.Permissions.manage_guild"><code>manage_guild</code></a> to do this.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permission to sync the integration.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Syncing the integration failed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl>

<dl><dt>*class*discord.Member<a href="#discord.Member" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Represents a Discord member to a <a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a>.

This implements a lot of the functionality of <a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a>.

<dl><dt>x == y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two members are equal. Note that this works with <a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a> instances too.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x != y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two members are not equal. Note that this works with <a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a> instances too.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>hash(x)</dt>
<dd>

Returns the member’s hash.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>str(x)</dt>
<dd>

Returns the member’s handle (e.g. <code>name</code> or <code>name#discriminator</code>).

</dd></dl>

<dl><dt>joined_at<a href="#discord.Member.joined_at" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

An aware datetime object that specifies the date and time in UTC that the member joined the guild. If the member left and rejoined the guild, this will be the latest date. This can be <code>None</code>, such as when the member is a guest.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>activities<a href="#discord.Member.activities" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The activities that the user is currently doing.

Note

Due to a Discord API limitation, a user’s Spotify activity may not appear if they are listening to a song with a title longer than 128 characters. See <a href="https://github.com/Rapptz/discord.py/issues/1738">GH-1738</a> for more information.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Tuple\[Union\[<a href="#discord.BaseActivity" title="discord.BaseActivity"><code>BaseActivity</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Spotify" title="discord.Spotify"><code>Spotify</code></a>]]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>guild<a href="#discord.Member.guild" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The guild that the member belongs to.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>nick<a href="#discord.Member.nick" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The guild specific nickname of the user. Takes precedence over the global name.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>pending<a href="#discord.Member.pending" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Whether the member is pending member verification.

New in version 1.6.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>premium_since<a href="#discord.Member.premium_since" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

An aware datetime object that specifies the date and time in UTC when the member used their “Nitro boost” on the guild, if available. This could be <code>None</code>.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>timed_out_until<a href="#discord.Member.timed_out_until" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

An aware datetime object that specifies the date and time in UTC that the member’s time out will expire. This will be set to <code>None</code> or a time in the past if the user is not timed out.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>client_status<a href="#discord.Member.client_status" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

<dl><dt>Type</dt>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*async with* typing()<a href="#discord.Member.typing" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns an asynchronous context manager that allows you to send a typing indicator to the destination for an indefinite period of time, or 10 seconds if the context manager is called using <code>await</code>.

Example Usage:

```
async with channel.typing():
    # simulate something heavy
    await asyncio.sleep(20)

await channel.send('Done!')

```

Example Usage:

```
await channel.typing()
# Do some computational magic for about 10 seconds
await channel.send('Done!')

```

Changed in version 2.0: This no longer works with the <code>with</code> syntax, <code>async with</code> must be used instead.

Changed in version 2.0: Added functionality to <code>await</code> the context manager to send a typing indicator for 10 seconds.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*property*name<a href="#discord.Member.name" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*activity<a href="#discord.Member.activity" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns the primary activity the user is currently doing. Could be <code>None</code> if no activity is being done.

Note

Due to a Discord API limitation, this may be <code>None</code> if the user is listening to a song on Spotify with a title longer than 128 characters. See <a href="https://github.com/Rapptz/discord.py/issues/1738">GH-1738</a> for more information.

Note

A user may have multiple activities, these can be accessed under <a href="#discord.Member.activities" title="discord.Member.activities"><code>activities</code></a>.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>

Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.BaseActivity" title="discord.BaseActivity"><code>BaseActivity</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Spotify" title="discord.Spotify"><code>Spotify</code></a>]]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>mentioned_in(*message*)<a href="#discord.Member.mentioned_in" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

**message** (<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>) – The message to check if you’re mentioned in.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*top_role<a href="#discord.Member.top_role" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns the member’s highest role.

This is useful for figuring where a member stands in the role hierarchy chain.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*guild_permissions<a href="#discord.Member.guild_permissions" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns the member’s guild permissions.

This only takes into consideration the guild permissions and not most of the implied permissions or any of the channel permission overwrites. For 100% accurate permission calculation, please use <a href="#discord.abc.GuildChannel.permissions_for" title="discord.abc.GuildChannel.permissions_for"><code>abc.GuildChannel.permissions_for()</code></a>.

This does take into consideration guild ownership, the administrator implication, and whether the member is timed out.

Changed in version 2.0: Member timeouts are taken into consideration.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Permissions" title="discord.Permissions"><code>Permissions</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*resolved_permissions<a href="#discord.Member.resolved_permissions" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns the member’s resolved permissions from an interaction.

This is only available in interaction contexts and represents the resolved permissions of the member in the channel the interaction was executed in. This is more or less equivalent to calling <a href="#discord.abc.GuildChannel.permissions_for" title="discord.abc.GuildChannel.permissions_for"><code>abc.GuildChannel.permissions_for()</code></a> but stored and returned as an attribute by the Discord API rather than computed.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="#discord.Permissions" title="discord.Permissions"><code>Permissions</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*voice<a href="#discord.Member.voice" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

Returns the member’s current voice state.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>

Optional\[<a href="#discord.VoiceState" title="discord.VoiceState"><code>VoiceState</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*flags<a href="#discord.Member.flags" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.MemberFlags" title="discord.MemberFlags"><code>MemberFlags</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* ban(***, *delete_message_days=...*, *delete_message_seconds=...*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Member.ban" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Bans this member. Equivalent to <a href="#discord.Guild.ban" title="discord.Guild.ban"><code>Guild.ban()</code></a>.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*await* unban(***, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Member.unban" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Unbans this member. Equivalent to <a href="#discord.Guild.unban" title="discord.Guild.unban"><code>Guild.unban()</code></a>.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*await* kick(***, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Member.kick" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Kicks this member. Equivalent to <a href="#discord.Guild.kick" title="discord.Guild.kick"><code>Guild.kick()</code></a>.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*await* edit(***, *nick=...*, *mute=...*, *deafen=...*, *suppress=...*, *roles=...*, *voice_channel=...*, *timed_out_until=...*, *bypass_verification=...*, *avatar=...*, *banner=...*, *bio=...*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Member.edit" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Edits the member’s data.

Note

To upload an avatar or banner, a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-bytes-like-object" title="(in Python v3.14)">bytes-like object</a> must be passed in that represents the image being uploaded. If this is done through a file then the file must be opened via <code>open('some_filename', 'rb')</code> and the <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-bytes-like-object" title="(in Python v3.14)">bytes-like object</a> is given through the use of <code>fp.read()</code>.

Depending on the parameter passed, this requires different permissions listed below:

| Parameter | Permission |
| --- | --- |
| nick | <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_nicknames" title="discord.Permissions.manage_nicknames"><code>Permissions.manage_nicknames</code></a> |
| mute | <a href="#discord.Permissions.mute_members" title="discord.Permissions.mute_members"><code>Permissions.mute_members</code></a> |
| deafen | <a href="#discord.Permissions.deafen_members" title="discord.Permissions.deafen_members"><code>Permissions.deafen_members</code></a> |
| roles | <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_roles" title="discord.Permissions.manage_roles"><code>Permissions.manage_roles</code></a> |
| voice\_channel | <a href="#discord.Permissions.move_members" title="discord.Permissions.move_members"><code>Permissions.move_members</code></a> |
| timed\_out\_until | <a href="#discord.Permissions.moderate_members" title="discord.Permissions.moderate_members"><code>Permissions.moderate_members</code></a> |
| bypass\_verification | <a href="#discord.Permissions.moderate_members" title="discord.Permissions.moderate_members"><code>Permissions.moderate_members</code></a> |

All parameters are optional.

Changed in version 1.1: Can now pass <code>None</code> to <code>voice_channel</code> to kick a member from voice.

Changed in version 2.0: The newly updated member is now optionally returned, if applicable.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **nick** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The member’s new nickname. Use <code>None</code> to remove the nickname.
- **mute** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Indicates if the member should be guild muted or un-muted.
- **deafen** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Indicates if the member should be guild deafened or un-deafened.
- **suppress** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Indicates if the member should be suppressed in stage channels.

  New in version 1.7.
- **roles** (List\[<a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>]) – The member’s new list of roles. This *replaces* the roles.
- **voice\_channel** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.VoiceChannel" title="discord.VoiceChannel"><code>VoiceChannel</code></a>, <a href="#discord.StageChannel" title="discord.StageChannel"><code>StageChannel</code></a>]]) – The voice channel to move the member to. Pass <code>None</code> to kick them from voice.
- **timed\_out\_until** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]) –

  The date the member’s timeout should expire, or <code>None</code> to remove the timeout. This must be a timezone-aware datetime object. Consider using <a href="#discord.utils.utcnow" title="discord.utils.utcnow"><code>utils.utcnow()</code></a>.

  New in version 2.0.
- **bypass\_verification** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Indicates if the member should be allowed to bypass the guild verification requirements.

  New in version 2.2.
- **avatar** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bytes</code></a>]) –

  A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-bytes-like-object" title="(in Python v3.14)">bytes-like object</a> representing the image to upload. Could be <code>None</code> to denote no avatar. Only image formats supported for uploading are JPEG, PNG, GIF, and WEBP. This can only be set when editing the bot’s own member.

  New in version 2.7.
- **banner** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bytes</code></a>]) –

  A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-bytes-like-object" title="(in Python v3.14)">bytes-like object</a> representing the image to upload. Could be <code>None</code> to denote no banner. Only image formats supported for uploading are JPEG, PNG, GIF and WEBP.. This can only be set when editing the bot’s own member.

  New in version 2.7.
- **bio** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) –

  The new bio for the member. Use <code>None</code> to remove the bio. This can only be set when editing the bot’s own member.

  New in version 2.7.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for editing this member. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to do the action requested.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – The operation failed.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – The datetime object passed to <code>timed_out_until</code> was not timezone-aware.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – You tried to edit the bio, avatar or banner of a member that is not the bot’s own member. Or the wrong image format passed for <code>avatar</code> or <code>banner</code>.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The newly updated member, if applicable. This is not returned if certain fields are passed, such as <code>suppress</code>.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* request_to_speak()<a href="#discord.Member.request_to_speak" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Request to speak in the connected channel.

Only applies to stage channels.

Note

Requesting members that are not the client is equivalent to <a href="#discord.Member.edit" title="discord.Member.edit"><code>edit</code></a> providing <code>suppress</code> as <code>False</code>.

New in version 1.7.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.ClientException" title="discord.ClientException">**ClientException**</a> – You are not connected to a voice channel.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to do the action requested.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – The operation failed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* move_to(*channel*, ***, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Member.move_to" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Moves a member to a new voice channel (they must be connected first).

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.move_members" title="discord.Permissions.move_members"><code>move_members</code></a> to do this.

This raises the same exceptions as <a href="#discord.Member.edit" title="discord.Member.edit"><code>edit()</code></a>.

Changed in version 1.1: Can now pass <code>None</code> to kick a member from voice.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **channel** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.VoiceChannel" title="discord.VoiceChannel"><code>VoiceChannel</code></a>, <a href="#discord.StageChannel" title="discord.StageChannel"><code>StageChannel</code></a>]]) – The new voice channel to move the member to. Pass <code>None</code> to kick them from voice.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for doing this action. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* timeout(*until*, */*, ***, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Member.timeout" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Applies a time out to a member until the specified date time or for the given <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.timedelta" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.timedelta</code></a>.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.moderate_members" title="discord.Permissions.moderate_members"><code>moderate_members</code></a> to do this.

This raises the same exceptions as <a href="#discord.Member.edit" title="discord.Member.edit"><code>edit()</code></a>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **until** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.timedelta" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.timedelta</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – If this is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.timedelta" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.timedelta</code></a> then it represents the amount of time the member should be timed out for. If this is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a> then it’s when the member’s timeout should expire. If <code>None</code> is passed then the timeout is removed. Note that the API only allows for timeouts up to 28 days.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for doing this action. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – The <code>until</code> parameter was the wrong type or the datetime was not timezone-aware.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* add_roles(**roles*, *reason=None*, *atomic=True*)<a href="#discord.Member.add_roles" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Gives the member a number of <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>s.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_roles" title="discord.Permissions.manage_roles"><code>manage_roles</code></a> to use this, and the added <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>s must appear lower in the list of roles than the highest role of the client.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **\*roles** (<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>) – An argument list of <a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a> representing a <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a> to give to the member.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for adding these roles. Shows up on the audit log.
- **atomic** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to atomically add roles. This will ensure that multiple operations will always be applied regardless of the current state of the cache.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to add these roles.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Adding roles failed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* remove_roles(**roles*, *reason=None*, *atomic=True*)<a href="#discord.Member.remove_roles" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Removes <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>s from this member.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_roles" title="discord.Permissions.manage_roles"><code>manage_roles</code></a> to use this, and the removed <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>s must appear lower in the list of roles than the highest role of the client.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **\*roles** (<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>) – An argument list of <a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a> representing a <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a> to remove from the member.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for removing these roles. Shows up on the audit log.
- **atomic** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to atomically remove roles. This will ensure that multiple operations will always be applied regardless of the current state of the cache.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to remove these roles.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Removing the roles failed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_voice()<a href="#discord.Member.fetch_voice" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Retrieves the current voice state from this member.

New in version 2.5.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The member is not in a voice channel.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to get a voice state.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Retrieving the voice state failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The current voice state of the member.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.VoiceState" title="discord.VoiceState"><code>VoiceState</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_message(*id*, */*)<a href="#discord.Member.fetch_message" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Retrieves a single <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> from the destination.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**id** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The message ID to look for.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The specified message was not found.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the permissions required to get a message.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Retrieving the message failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>

The message asked for.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>get_role(*role_id*, */*)<a href="#discord.Member.get_role" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns a role with the given ID from roles which the member has.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**role\_id** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The ID to search for.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The role or <code>None</code> if not found in the member’s roles.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*async for ... in* history(***, *limit=100*, *before=None*, *after=None*, *around=None*, *oldest_first=None*)<a href="#discord.Member.history" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterator" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterator</a> that enables receiving the destination’s message history.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.read_message_history" title="discord.Permissions.read_message_history"><code>read_message_history</code></a> to do this.

Examples

Usage

```
counter = 0
async for message in channel.history(limit=200):
    if message.author == client.user:
        counter += 1

```

Flattening into a list:

```
messages = [message async for message in channel.history(limit=123)]
# messages is now a list of Message...

```

All parameters are optional.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **limit** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) – The number of messages to retrieve. If <code>None</code>, retrieves every message in the channel. Note, however, that this would make it a slow operation.
- **before** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve messages before this date or message. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.
- **after** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve messages after this date or message. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.
- **around** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve messages around this date or message. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time. When using this argument, the maximum limit is 101. Note that if the limit is an even number then this will return at most limit + 1 messages.
- **oldest\_first** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>]) – If set to <code>True</code>, return messages in oldest-&gt;newest order. Defaults to <code>True</code> if <code>after</code> is specified, otherwise <code>False</code>.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to get channel message history.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – The request to get message history failed.

</dd><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> – The message with the message data parsed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>pins(***, *limit=50*, *before=None*, *oldest_first=False*)<a href="#discord.Member.pins" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Retrieves an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterator" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterator</a> of the pinned messages in the channel.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.view_channel" title="discord.Permissions.view_channel"><code>view_channel</code></a> and <a href="#discord.Permissions.read_message_history" title="discord.Permissions.read_message_history"><code>read_message_history</code></a> in order to use this.

Changed in version 2.6: Due to a change in Discord’s API, this now returns a paginated iterator instead of a list.

For backwards compatibility, you can still retrieve a list of pinned messages by using <code>await</code> on the returned object. This is however deprecated.

Note

Due to a limitation with the Discord API, the <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> object returned by this method does not contain complete <a href="#discord.Message.reactions" title="discord.Message.reactions"><code>Message.reactions</code></a> data.

Examples

Usage

```
counter = 0
async for message in channel.pins(limit=250):
    counter += 1

```

Flattening into a list:

```
messages = [message async for message in channel.pins(limit=50)]
# messages is now a list of Message...

```

All parameters are optional.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **limit** (*Optional**\[*<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)">*int*</a>*]*) –

  The number of pinned messages to retrieve. If <code>None</code>, it retrieves every pinned message in the channel. Note, however, that this would make it a slow operation. Defaults to <code>50</code>.

  New in version 2.6.
- **before** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>, <a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>]]) –

  Retrieve pinned messages before this time or snowflake. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.

  New in version 2.6.
- **oldest\_first** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  If set to <code>True</code>, return messages in oldest pin-&gt;newest pin order. Defaults to <code>False</code>.

  New in version 2.6.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the permission to retrieve pinned messages.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Retrieving the pinned messages failed.

</dd><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> – The pinned message with <a href="#discord.Message.pinned_at" title="discord.Message.pinned_at"><code>Message.pinned_at</code></a> set.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* send(*content=None*, ***, *tts=False*, *embed=None*, *embeds=None*, *file=None*, *files=None*, *stickers=None*, *delete_after=None*, *nonce=None*, *allowed_mentions=None*, *reference=None*, *mention_author=None*, *view=None*, *suppress_embeds=False*, *silent=False*, *poll=None*)<a href="#discord.Member.send" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Sends a message to the destination with the content given.

The content must be a type that can convert to a string through <code>str(content)</code>. If the content is set to <code>None</code> (the default), then the <code>embed</code> parameter must be provided.

To upload a single file, the <code>file</code> parameter should be used with a single <a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a> object. To upload multiple files, the <code>files</code> parameter should be used with a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#list" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>list</code></a> of <a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a> objects. **Specifying both parameters will lead to an exception**.

To upload a single embed, the <code>embed</code> parameter should be used with a single <a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a> object. To upload multiple embeds, the <code>embeds</code> parameter should be used with a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#list" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>list</code></a> of <a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a> objects. **Specifying both parameters will lead to an exception**.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> or <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>ValueError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **content** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The content of the message to send.
- **tts** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Indicates if the message should be sent using text-to-speech.
- **embed** (<a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a>) – The rich embed for the content.
- **embeds** (List\[<a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a>]) –

  A list of embeds to upload. Must be a maximum of 10.

  New in version 2.0.
- **file** (<a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a>) – The file to upload.
- **files** (List\[<a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a>]) – A list of files to upload. Must be a maximum of 10.
- **nonce** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The nonce to use for sending this message. If the message was successfully sent, then the message will have a nonce with this value.
- **delete\_after** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>float</code></a>) – If provided, the number of seconds to wait in the background before deleting the message we just sent. If the deletion fails, then it is silently ignored.
- **allowed\_mentions** (<a href="#discord.AllowedMentions" title="discord.AllowedMentions"><code>AllowedMentions</code></a>) –

  Controls the mentions being processed in this message. If this is passed, then the object is merged with <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a>. The merging behaviour only overrides attributes that have been explicitly passed to the object, otherwise it uses the attributes set in <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a>. If no object is passed at all then the defaults given by <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a> are used instead.

  New in version 1.4.
- **reference** (Union\[<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>, <a href="#discord.MessageReference" title="discord.MessageReference"><code>MessageReference</code></a>, <a href="#discord.PartialMessage" title="discord.PartialMessage"><code>PartialMessage</code></a>]) –

  A reference to the <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> to which you are referencing, this can be created using <a href="#discord.Message.to_reference" title="discord.Message.to_reference"><code>to_reference()</code></a> or passed directly as a <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>. In the event of a replying reference, you can control whether this mentions the author of the referenced message using the <a href="#discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user" title="discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user"><code>replied_user</code></a> attribute of <code>allowed_mentions</code> or by setting <code>mention_author</code>.

  New in version 1.6.
- **mention\_author** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>]) –

  If set, overrides the <a href="#discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user" title="discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user"><code>replied_user</code></a> attribute of <code>allowed_mentions</code>.

  New in version 1.6.
- **view** (Union\[<a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.ui.View" title="discord.ui.View"><code>discord.ui.View</code></a>, <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.ui.LayoutView" title="discord.ui.LayoutView"><code>discord.ui.LayoutView</code></a>]) –

  A Discord UI View to add to the message.

  New in version 2.0.
- **stickers** (Sequence\[Union\[<a href="#discord.GuildSticker" title="discord.GuildSticker"><code>GuildSticker</code></a>, <a href="#discord.StickerItem" title="discord.StickerItem"><code>StickerItem</code></a>]]) –

  A list of stickers to upload. Must be a maximum of 3.

  New in version 2.0.
- **suppress\_embeds** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to suppress embeds for the message. This sends the message without any embeds if set to <code>True</code>.

  New in version 2.0.
- **silent** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to suppress push and desktop notifications for the message. This will increment the mention counter in the UI, but will not actually send a notification.

  New in version 2.2.
- **poll** (<a href="#discord.Poll" title="discord.Poll"><code>Poll</code></a>) –

  The poll to send with this message.

  New in version 2.4.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Sending the message failed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to send the message.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – You sent a message with the same nonce as one that has been explicitly deleted shortly earlier.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – The <code>files</code> or <code>embeds</code> list is not of the appropriate size.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – You specified both <code>file</code> and <code>files</code>, or you specified both <code>embed</code> and <code>embeds</code>, or the <code>reference</code> object is not a <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>, <a href="#discord.MessageReference" title="discord.MessageReference"><code>MessageReference</code></a> or <a href="#discord.PartialMessage" title="discord.PartialMessage"><code>PartialMessage</code></a>.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The message that was sent.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>is_timed_out()<a href="#discord.Member.is_timed_out" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns whether this member is timed out.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

<code>True</code> if the member is timed out. <code>False</code> otherwise.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl>

**reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) –

This does not apply if <a href="#discord.Emoji.is_application_owned" title="discord.Emoji.is_application_owned"><code>is_application_owned()</code></a> is <code>True</code>.

</dd></dl></dd>

<dl><dt>*class*discord.PartialEmoji<a href="#discord.PartialEmoji" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Represents a “partial” emoji.

This model will be given in two scenarios:

- “Raw” data events such as <a href="#discord.on_raw_reaction_add" title="discord.on_raw_reaction_add"><code>on_raw_reaction_add()</code></a>
- Custom emoji that the bot cannot see from e.g. <a href="#discord.Message.reactions" title="discord.Message.reactions"><code>Message.reactions</code></a>

<dl><dt>x == y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two emoji are the same.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x != y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two emoji are not the same.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>hash(x)</dt>
<dd>

Return the emoji’s hash.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>str(x)</dt>
<dd>

Returns the emoji rendered for discord.

</dd></dl>

<dl><dt>name<a href="#discord.PartialEmoji.name" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The custom emoji name, if applicable, or the unicode codepoint of the non-custom emoji. This can be <code>None</code> if the emoji got deleted (e.g. removing a reaction with a deleted emoji).

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>animated<a href="#discord.PartialEmoji.animated" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Whether the emoji is animated or not.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>id<a href="#discord.PartialEmoji.id" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The ID of the custom emoji, if applicable.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*classmethod* from_str(*value*, ***, *client=...*)<a href="#discord.PartialEmoji.from_str" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Converts a Discord string representation of an emoji to a <a href="#discord.PartialEmoji" title="discord.PartialEmoji"><code>PartialEmoji</code></a>.

The formats accepted are:

- <code>a:name:id</code>
- <code>&lt;a:name:id&gt;</code>
- <code>name:id</code>
- <code>&lt;:name:id&gt;</code>

If the format does not match then it is assumed to be a unicode emoji.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **value** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The string representation of an emoji.
- **client** (<a href="#discord.Client" title="discord.Client"><code>Client</code></a>) –

  The client to initialise this emoji with. This allows it to attach the client’s internal state.

  New in version 2.7.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The partial emoji from this string.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.PartialEmoji" title="discord.PartialEmoji"><code>PartialEmoji</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>is_custom_emoji()<a href="#discord.PartialEmoji.is_custom_emoji" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>: Checks if this is a custom non-Unicode emoji.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>is_unicode_emoji()<a href="#discord.PartialEmoji.is_unicode_emoji" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>: Checks if this is a Unicode emoji.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*property*created_at<a href="#discord.PartialEmoji.created_at" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns the emoji’s creation time in UTC, or None if Unicode emoji.

New in version 1.6.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*url<a href="#discord.PartialEmoji.url" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

<dl><dt>*class*discord.Role<a href="#discord.Role" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x != y</dt>

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x &lt; y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if a role is lower than another in the hierarchy.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x &gt;= y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if a role is higher or equal to another in the hierarchy.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x &lt;= y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if a role is lower or equal to another in the hierarchy.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>hash(x)</dt>
<dd>

Return the role’s hash.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>str(x)</dt>
<dd>

</dd></dl>

<dd>

The position of the role. This number is usually positive. The bottom role has a position of 0.

Warning

Multiple roles can have the same position number. As a consequence of this, comparing via role position is prone to subtle bugs if checking for role hierarchy. The recommended and correct way to compare for roles in the hierarchy is using the comparison operators on the role objects themselves.
