</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* edit(***, *name=...*, *permissions=...*, *colour=...*, *color=...*, *hoist=...*, *display_icon=...*, *mentionable=...*, *position=...*, *reason=...*, *secondary_color=...*, *tertiary_color=...*, *secondary_colour=...*, *tertiary_colour=...*)<a href="#discord.Role.edit" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Edits the role.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_roles" title="discord.Permissions.manage_roles"><code>manage_roles</code></a> to do this.

All fields are optional.

Changed in version 1.4: Can now pass <code>int</code> to <code>colour</code> keyword-only parameter.

Changed in version 2.0: Edits are no longer in-place, the newly edited role is returned instead.

New in version 2.0: The <code>display_icon</code> keyword-only parameter was added.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>ValueError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

Changed in version 2.6: The <code>colour</code> and <code>color</code> parameters now set the role’s primary color.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The new role name to change to.
- **permissions** (<a href="#discord.Permissions" title="discord.Permissions"><code>Permissions</code></a>) – The new permissions to change to.
- **colour** (Union\[<a href="#discord.Colour" title="discord.Colour"><code>Colour</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) – The new colour to change to. (aliased to color as well)
- **secondary\_colour** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.Colour" title="discord.Colour"><code>Colour</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]]) –

  The new secondary colour for the role.

  New in version 2.6.
- **tertiary\_colour** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.Colour" title="discord.Colour"><code>Colour</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]]) –

  The new tertiary colour for the role. Can only be used for the holographic role preset, which is <code>(11127295, 16759788, 16761760)</code>

  New in version 2.6.
- **hoist** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Indicates if the role should be shown separately in the member list.
- **display\_icon** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bytes</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]]) – A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-bytes-like-object" title="(in Python v3.14)">bytes-like object</a> representing the icon or <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a> representing unicode emoji that should be used as a role icon. Could be <code>None</code> to denote removal of the icon. Only PNG/JPEG is supported. This is only available to guilds that contain <code>ROLE_ICONS</code> in <a href="#discord.Guild.features" title="discord.Guild.features"><code>Guild.features</code></a>.
- **mentionable** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Indicates if the role should be mentionable by others.
- **position** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The new role’s position. This must be below your top role’s position or it will fail.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for editing this role. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to change the role.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Editing the role failed.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – An invalid position was given or the default role was asked to be moved.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The newly edited role.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* move(***, *beginning=...*, *end=...*, *above=...*, *below=...*, *offset=0*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Role.move" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

A rich interface to help move a role relative to other roles.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_roles" title="discord.Permissions.manage_roles"><code>manage_roles</code></a> to do this, and you cannot move roles above the client’s top role in the guild.

New in version 2.5.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **beginning** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to move this at the beginning of the role list, above the default role. This is mutually exclusive with *end*, *above*, and *below*.
- **end** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to move this at the end of the role list. This is mutually exclusive with *beginning*, *above*, and *below*.
- **above** (<a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>) – The role that should be above our current role. This mutually exclusive with *beginning*, *end*, and *below*.
- **below** (<a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>) – The role that should be below our current role. This mutually exclusive with *beginning*, *end*, and *above*.
- **offset** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The number of roles to offset the move by. For example, an offset of <code>2</code> with <code>beginning=True</code> would move it 2 above the beginning. A positive number moves it above while a negative number moves it below. Note that this number is relative and computed after the <code>beginning</code>, <code>end</code>, <code>before</code>, and <code>after</code> parameters.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for editing this role. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You cannot move the role there, or lack permissions to do so.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Moving the role failed.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – A bad mix of arguments were passed.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – An invalid role was passed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

A list of all the roles in the guild.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

List\[<a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* delete(***, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Role.delete" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Deletes the role.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_roles" title="discord.Permissions.manage_roles"><code>manage_roles</code></a> to do this.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for deleting this role. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to delete the role.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Deleting the role failed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl>

<dl><dt>*class*discord.RoleTags<a href="#discord.RoleTags" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Represents tags on a role.

A role tag is a piece of extra information attached to a managed role that gives it context for the reason the role is managed.

While this can be accessed, a useful interface is also provided in the <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a> and <a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a> classes as well.

New in version 1.6.

<dl><dt>*class*discord.PartialMessageable<a href="#discord.PartialMessageable" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Represents a partial messageable to aid with working messageable channels when only a channel ID is present.

The only way to construct this class is through <a href="#discord.Client.get_partial_messageable" title="discord.Client.get_partial_messageable"><code>Client.get_partial_messageable()</code></a>.

Note that this class is trimmed down and has no rich attributes.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>x == y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two partial messageables are equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x != y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two partial messageables are not equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>hash(x)</dt>
<dd>

Returns the partial messageable’s hash.

</dd></dl>

</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_message(*id*, */*)<a href="#discord.PartialMessageable.fetch_message" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Retrieves a single <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> from the destination.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**id** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The message ID to look for.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The specified message was not found.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the permissions required to get a message.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Retrieving the message failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The message asked for.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*async for ... in* history(***, *limit=100*, *before=None*, *after=None*, *around=None*, *oldest_first=None*)<a href="#discord.PartialMessageable.history" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterator" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterator</a> that enables receiving the destination’s message history.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.read_message_history" title="discord.Permissions.read_message_history"><code>read_message_history</code></a> to do this.

Examples

Usage

```
counter = 0
async for message in channel.history(limit=200):
    if message.author == client.user:
        counter += 1

```

Flattening into a list:

```
messages = [message async for message in channel.history(limit=123)]
# messages is now a list of Message...

```

All parameters are optional.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **limit** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) – The number of messages to retrieve. If <code>None</code>, retrieves every message in the channel. Note, however, that this would make it a slow operation.
- **before** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve messages before this date or message. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.
- **after** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve messages after this date or message. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.
- **around** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve messages around this date or message. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time. When using this argument, the maximum limit is 101. Note that if the limit is an even number then this will return at most limit + 1 messages.
- **oldest\_first** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>]) – If set to <code>True</code>, return messages in oldest-&gt;newest order. Defaults to <code>True</code> if <code>after</code> is specified, otherwise <code>False</code>.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to get channel message history.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – The request to get message history failed.

</dd><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> – The message with the message data parsed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>pins(***, *limit=50*, *before=None*, *oldest_first=False*)<a href="#discord.PartialMessageable.pins" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Retrieves an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterator" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterator</a> of the pinned messages in the channel.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.view_channel" title="discord.Permissions.view_channel"><code>view_channel</code></a> and <a href="#discord.Permissions.read_message_history" title="discord.Permissions.read_message_history"><code>read_message_history</code></a> in order to use this.

Changed in version 2.6: Due to a change in Discord’s API, this now returns a paginated iterator instead of a list.

For backwards compatibility, you can still retrieve a list of pinned messages by using <code>await</code> on the returned object. This is however deprecated.

Note

Due to a limitation with the Discord API, the <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> object returned by this method does not contain complete <a href="#discord.Message.reactions" title="discord.Message.reactions"><code>Message.reactions</code></a> data.

Examples

Usage

```
counter = 0
async for message in channel.pins(limit=250):
    counter += 1

```

Flattening into a list:

```
messages = [message async for message in channel.pins(limit=50)]
# messages is now a list of Message...

```

All parameters are optional.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **limit** (*Optional**\[*<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)">*int*</a>*]*) –

  The number of pinned messages to retrieve. If <code>None</code>, it retrieves every pinned message in the channel. Note, however, that this would make it a slow operation. Defaults to <code>50</code>.

  New in version 2.6.
- **before** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>, <a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>]]) –

  Retrieve pinned messages before this time or snowflake. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.

  New in version 2.6.
- **oldest\_first** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  If set to <code>True</code>, return messages in oldest pin-&gt;newest pin order. Defaults to <code>False</code>.

  New in version 2.6.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the permission to retrieve pinned messages.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Retrieving the pinned messages failed.

</dd><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> – The pinned message with <a href="#discord.Message.pinned_at" title="discord.Message.pinned_at"><code>Message.pinned_at</code></a> set.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* send(*content=None*, ***, *tts=False*, *embed=None*, *embeds=None*, *file=None*, *files=None*, *stickers=None*, *delete_after=None*, *nonce=None*, *allowed_mentions=None*, *reference=None*, *mention_author=None*, *view=None*, *suppress_embeds=False*, *silent=False*, *poll=None*)<a href="#discord.PartialMessageable.send" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Sends a message to the destination with the content given.

The content must be a type that can convert to a string through <code>str(content)</code>. If the content is set to <code>None</code> (the default), then the <code>embed</code> parameter must be provided.

To upload a single file, the <code>file</code> parameter should be used with a single <a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a> object. To upload multiple files, the <code>files</code> parameter should be used with a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#list" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>list</code></a> of <a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a> objects. **Specifying both parameters will lead to an exception**.

To upload a single embed, the <code>embed</code> parameter should be used with a single <a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a> object. To upload multiple embeds, the <code>embeds</code> parameter should be used with a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#list" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>list</code></a> of <a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a> objects. **Specifying both parameters will lead to an exception**.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> or <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>ValueError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **content** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The content of the message to send.
- **tts** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Indicates if the message should be sent using text-to-speech.
- **embed** (<a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a>) – The rich embed for the content.
- **embeds** (List\[<a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a>]) –

  A list of embeds to upload. Must be a maximum of 10.

  New in version 2.0.
- **file** (<a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a>) – The file to upload.
- **files** (List\[<a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a>]) – A list of files to upload. Must be a maximum of 10.
- **nonce** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The nonce to use for sending this message. If the message was successfully sent, then the message will have a nonce with this value.
- **delete\_after** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>float</code></a>) – If provided, the number of seconds to wait in the background before deleting the message we just sent. If the deletion fails, then it is silently ignored.
- **allowed\_mentions** (<a href="#discord.AllowedMentions" title="discord.AllowedMentions"><code>AllowedMentions</code></a>) –

  Controls the mentions being processed in this message. If this is passed, then the object is merged with <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a>. The merging behaviour only overrides attributes that have been explicitly passed to the object, otherwise it uses the attributes set in <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a>. If no object is passed at all then the defaults given by <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a> are used instead.

  New in version 1.4.
- **reference** (Union\[<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>, <a href="#discord.MessageReference" title="discord.MessageReference"><code>MessageReference</code></a>, <a href="#discord.PartialMessage" title="discord.PartialMessage"><code>PartialMessage</code></a>]) –

  A reference to the <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> to which you are referencing, this can be created using <a href="#discord.Message.to_reference" title="discord.Message.to_reference"><code>to_reference()</code></a> or passed directly as a <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>. In the event of a replying reference, you can control whether this mentions the author of the referenced message using the <a href="#discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user" title="discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user"><code>replied_user</code></a> attribute of <code>allowed_mentions</code> or by setting <code>mention_author</code>.

  New in version 1.6.
- **mention\_author** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>]) –

  If set, overrides the <a href="#discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user" title="discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user"><code>replied_user</code></a> attribute of <code>allowed_mentions</code>.

  New in version 1.6.
- **view** (Union\[<a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.ui.View" title="discord.ui.View"><code>discord.ui.View</code></a>, <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.ui.LayoutView" title="discord.ui.LayoutView"><code>discord.ui.LayoutView</code></a>]) –

  A Discord UI View to add to the message.

  New in version 2.0.
- **stickers** (Sequence\[Union\[<a href="#discord.GuildSticker" title="discord.GuildSticker"><code>GuildSticker</code></a>, <a href="#discord.StickerItem" title="discord.StickerItem"><code>StickerItem</code></a>]]) –

  A list of stickers to upload. Must be a maximum of 3.

  New in version 2.0.
- **suppress\_embeds** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to suppress embeds for the message. This sends the message without any embeds if set to <code>True</code>.

  New in version 2.0.
- **silent** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to suppress push and desktop notifications for the message. This will increment the mention counter in the UI, but will not actually send a notification.

  New in version 2.2.
- **poll** (<a href="#discord.Poll" title="discord.Poll"><code>Poll</code></a>) –

  The poll to send with this message.

  New in version 2.4.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Sending the message failed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to send the message.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – You sent a message with the same nonce as one that has been explicitly deleted shortly earlier.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – The <code>files</code> or <code>embeds</code> list is not of the appropriate size.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – You specified both <code>file</code> and <code>files</code>, or you specified both <code>embed</code> and <code>embeds</code>, or the <code>reference</code> object is not a <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>, <a href="#discord.MessageReference" title="discord.MessageReference"><code>MessageReference</code></a> or <a href="#discord.PartialMessage" title="discord.PartialMessage"><code>PartialMessage</code></a>.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The message that was sent.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>typing()<a href="#discord.PartialMessageable.typing" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns an asynchronous context manager that allows you to send a typing indicator to the destination for an indefinite period of time, or 10 seconds if the context manager is called using <code>await</code>.

Example Usage:

```
async with channel.typing():
    # simulate something heavy
    await asyncio.sleep(20)

await channel.send('Done!')

```

Example Usage:

```
await channel.typing()
# Do some computational magic for about 10 seconds
await channel.send('Done!')

```

Changed in version 2.0: This no longer works with the <code>with</code> syntax, <code>async with</code> must be used instead.

Changed in version 2.0: Added functionality to <code>await</code> the context manager to send a typing indicator for 10 seconds.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*property*guild<a href="#discord.PartialMessageable.guild" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

<dl><dt>*class*discord.TextChannel<a href="#discord.TextChannel" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Represents a Discord guild text channel.

<dl><dt>x == y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two channels are equal.

</dl><dl><dt>*async with* typing()<a href="#discord.TextChannel.typing" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns an asynchronous context manager that allows you to send a typing indicator to the destination for an indefinite period of time, or 10 seconds if the context manager is called using <code>await</code>.

Example Usage:

```
async with channel.typing():
    # simulate something heavy
    await asyncio.sleep(20)

await channel.send('Done!')

```

Example Usage:

```
await channel.typing()
# Do some computational magic for about 10 seconds
await channel.send('Done!')

```

Changed in version 2.0: This no longer works with the <code>with</code> syntax, <code>async with</code> must be used instead.

Changed in version 2.0: Added functionality to <code>await</code> the context manager to send a typing indicator for 10 seconds.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*property*type<a href="#discord.TextChannel.type" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

<dl><dt>Type</dt>

<a href="#discord.ChannelType" title="discord.ChannelType"><code>ChannelType</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>permissions_for(*obj*, */*)<a href="#discord.TextChannel.permissions_for" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Handles permission resolution for the <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> or <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>.

This function takes into consideration the following cases:

- Guild owner
- Guild roles
- Channel overrides
- Member overrides
- Implicit permissions
- Member timeout
- User installed app

If a <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a> is passed, then it checks the permissions someone with that role would have, which is essentially:

- The default role permissions
- The permissions of the role used as a parameter
- The default role permission overwrites
- The permission overwrites of the role used as a parameter

Changed in version 2.0: The object passed in can now be a role object.

Changed in version 2.0: <code>obj</code> parameter is now positional-only.

Changed in version 2.4: User installed apps are now taken into account. The permissions returned for a user installed app mirrors the permissions Discord returns in <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.Interaction.app_permissions" title="discord.Interaction.app_permissions"><code>app_permissions</code></a>, though it is recommended to use that attribute instead.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**obj** (Union\[<a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>]) – The object to resolve permissions for. This could be either a member or a role. If it’s a role then member overwrites are not computed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The resolved permissions for the member or role.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Permissions" title="discord.Permissions"><code>Permissions</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*members<a href="#discord.TextChannel.members" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns all members that can see this channel.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

List\[<a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*threads<a href="#discord.TextChannel.threads" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns all the threads that you can see.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

List\[<a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*property*last_message<a href="#discord.TextChannel.last_message" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Retrieves the last message from this channel in cache.

The message might not be valid or point to an existing message.

Reliable Fetching

For a slightly more reliable method of fetching the last message, consider using either <a href="#discord.TextChannel.history" title="discord.TextChannel.history"><code>history()</code></a> or <a href="#discord.TextChannel.fetch_message" title="discord.TextChannel.fetch_message"><code>fetch_message()</code></a> with the <a href="#discord.TextChannel.last_message_id" title="discord.TextChannel.last_message_id"><code>last_message_id</code></a> attribute.

<dl><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The last message in this channel or <code>None</code> if not found.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* edit(***, *reason=None*, ***options*)<a href="#discord.TextChannel.edit" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Edits the channel.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_channels" title="discord.Permissions.manage_channels"><code>manage_channels</code></a> to do this.

Changed in version 1.3: The <code>overwrites</code> keyword-only parameter was added.

Changed in version 1.4: The <code>type</code> keyword-only parameter was added.

Changed in version 2.0: Edits are no longer in-place, the newly edited channel is returned instead.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> or <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>ValueError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The new channel name.
- **topic** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The new channel’s topic.
- **position** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The new channel’s position.
- **nsfw** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – To mark the channel as NSFW or not.
- **sync\_permissions** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to sync permissions with the channel’s new or pre-existing category. Defaults to <code>False</code>.
- **category** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.CategoryChannel" title="discord.CategoryChannel"><code>CategoryChannel</code></a>]) – The new category for this channel. Can be <code>None</code> to remove the category.
- **slowmode\_delay** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – Specifies the slowmode rate limit for user in this channel, in seconds. A value of <code>0</code> disables slowmode. The maximum value possible is <code>21600</code>.
- **type** (<a href="#discord.ChannelType" title="discord.ChannelType"><code>ChannelType</code></a>) – Change the type of this text channel. Currently, only conversion between <a href="#discord.ChannelType.text" title="discord.ChannelType.text"><code>ChannelType.text</code></a> and <a href="#discord.ChannelType.news" title="discord.ChannelType.news"><code>ChannelType.news</code></a> is supported. This is only available to guilds that contain <code>NEWS</code> in <a href="#discord.Guild.features" title="discord.Guild.features"><code>Guild.features</code></a>.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for editing this channel. Shows up on the audit log.
- **overwrites** (<code>Mapping</code>) – A <code>Mapping</code> of target (either a role or a member) to <a href="#discord.PermissionOverwrite" title="discord.PermissionOverwrite"><code>PermissionOverwrite</code></a> to apply to the channel.
- **default\_auto\_archive\_duration** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) –

  The new default auto archive duration in minutes for threads created in this channel. Must be one of <code>60</code>, <code>1440</code>, <code>4320</code>, or <code>10080</code>.

  New in version 2.0.
- **default\_thread\_slowmode\_delay** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) –

  The new default slowmode delay in seconds for threads created in this channel.

  New in version 2.3.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – The new <code>position</code> is less than 0 or greater than the number of channels.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – The permission overwrite information is not in proper form.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to edit the channel.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Editing the channel failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The newly edited text channel. If the edit was only positional then <code>None</code> is returned instead.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="#discord.TextChannel" title="discord.TextChannel"><code>TextChannel</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* clone(***, *name=None*, *category=None*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.TextChannel.clone" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Clones this channel. This creates a channel with the same properties as this channel.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_channels" title="discord.Permissions.manage_channels"><code>manage_channels</code></a> to do this.

New in version 1.1.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The name of the new channel. If not provided, defaults to this channel name.
- **category** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.CategoryChannel" title="discord.CategoryChannel"><code>CategoryChannel</code></a>]) –

  The category the new channel belongs to. This parameter is ignored if cloning a category channel.

  New in version 2.5.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for cloning this channel. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to create this channel.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Creating the channel failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The channel that was created.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.abc.GuildChannel" title="discord.abc.GuildChannel"><code>abc.GuildChannel</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* delete_messages(*messages*, ***, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.TextChannel.delete_messages" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Deletes a list of messages. This is similar to <a href="#discord.Message.delete" title="discord.Message.delete"><code>Message.delete()</code></a> except it bulk deletes multiple messages.

As a special case, if the number of messages is 0, then nothing is done. If the number of messages is 1 then single message delete is done. If it’s more than two, then bulk delete is used.

You cannot bulk delete more than 100 messages or messages that are older than 14 days old.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_messages" title="discord.Permissions.manage_messages"><code>manage_messages</code></a> to do this.

Changed in version 2.0: <code>messages</code> parameter is now positional-only.

The <code>reason</code> keyword-only parameter was added.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **messages** (Iterable\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>]) – An iterable of messages denoting which ones to bulk delete.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for deleting the messages. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.ClientException" title="discord.ClientException">**ClientException**</a> – The number of messages to delete was more than 100.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have proper permissions to delete the messages.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – If single delete, then the message was already deleted.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Deleting the messages failed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* purge(***, *limit=100*, *check=...*, *before=None*, *after=None*, *around=None*, *oldest_first=None*, *bulk=True*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.TextChannel.purge" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Purges a list of messages that meet the criteria given by the predicate <code>check</code>. If a <code>check</code> is not provided then all messages are deleted without discrimination.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_messages" title="discord.Permissions.manage_messages"><code>manage_messages</code></a> to delete messages even if they are your own. Having <a href="#discord.Permissions.read_message_history" title="discord.Permissions.read_message_history"><code>read_message_history</code></a> is also needed to retrieve message history.

Changed in version 2.0: The <code>reason</code> keyword-only parameter was added.

Examples

Deleting bot’s messages

```
def is_me(m):
    return m.author == client.user

deleted = await channel.purge(limit=100, check=is_me)
await channel.send(f'Deleted {len(deleted)} message(s)')

```

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **limit** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) – The number of messages to search through. This is not the number of messages that will be deleted, though it can be.
- **check** (Callable\[\[<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>], <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>]) – The function used to check if a message should be deleted. It must take a <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> as its sole parameter.
- **before** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Same as <code>before</code> in <a href="#discord.TextChannel.history" title="discord.TextChannel.history"><code>history()</code></a>.
- **after** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Same as <code>after</code> in <a href="#discord.TextChannel.history" title="discord.TextChannel.history"><code>history()</code></a>.
- **around** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Same as <code>around</code> in <a href="#discord.TextChannel.history" title="discord.TextChannel.history"><code>history()</code></a>.
- **oldest\_first** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>]) – Same as <code>oldest_first</code> in <a href="#discord.TextChannel.history" title="discord.TextChannel.history"><code>history()</code></a>.
- **bulk** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – If <code>True</code>, use bulk delete. Setting this to <code>False</code> is useful for mass-deleting a bot’s own messages without <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_messages" title="discord.Permissions.manage_messages"><code>Permissions.manage_messages</code></a>. When <code>True</code>, will fall back to single delete if messages are older than two weeks.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for purging the messages. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have proper permissions to do the actions required.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Purging the messages failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The list of messages that were deleted.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

List\[<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* webhooks()<a href="#discord.TextChannel.webhooks" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Gets the list of webhooks from this channel.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_webhooks" title="discord.Permissions.manage_webhooks"><code>manage_webhooks</code></a> to do this.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You don’t have permissions to get the webhooks.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The webhooks for this channel.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

List\[<a href="#discord.Webhook" title="discord.Webhook"><code>Webhook</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* create_webhook(***, *name*, *avatar=None*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.TextChannel.create_webhook" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Creates a webhook for this channel.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_webhooks" title="discord.Permissions.manage_webhooks"><code>manage_webhooks</code></a> to do this.

Changed in version 1.1: Added the <code>reason</code> keyword-only parameter.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The webhook’s name.
- **avatar** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bytes</code></a>]) – A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-bytes-like-object" title="(in Python v3.14)">bytes-like object</a> representing the webhook’s default avatar. This operates similarly to <a href="#discord.ClientUser.edit" title="discord.ClientUser.edit"><code>edit()</code></a>.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for creating this webhook. Shows up in the audit logs.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Creating the webhook failed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to create a webhook.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The created webhook.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Webhook" title="discord.Webhook"><code>Webhook</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* follow(***, *destination*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.TextChannel.follow" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Follows a channel using a webhook.

Only news channels can be followed.

Note

The webhook returned will not provide a token to do webhook actions, as Discord does not provide it.

New in version 1.3.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **destination** (<a href="#discord.TextChannel" title="discord.TextChannel"><code>TextChannel</code></a>) – The channel you would like to follow from.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) –

  The reason for following the channel. Shows up on the destination guild’s audit log.

  New in version 1.4.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Following the channel failed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the permissions to create a webhook.
- <a href="#discord.ClientException" title="discord.ClientException">**ClientException**</a> – The channel is not a news channel.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – The destination channel is not a text channel.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The created webhook.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Webhook" title="discord.Webhook"><code>Webhook</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>get_partial_message(*message_id*, */*)<a href="#discord.TextChannel.get_partial_message" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Creates a <a href="#discord.PartialMessage" title="discord.PartialMessage"><code>PartialMessage</code></a> from the message ID.

This is useful if you want to work with a message and only have its ID without doing an unnecessary API call.

Changed in version 2.0: <code>message_id</code> parameter is now positional-only.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**message\_id** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The message ID to create a partial message for.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The partial message.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.PartialMessage" title="discord.PartialMessage"><code>PartialMessage</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>get_thread(*thread_id*, */*)<a href="#discord.TextChannel.get_thread" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns a thread with the given ID.

Note

This does not always retrieve archived threads, as they are not retained in the internal cache. Use <a href="#discord.Guild.fetch_channel" title="discord.Guild.fetch_channel"><code>Guild.fetch_channel()</code></a> instead.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**thread\_id** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The ID to search for.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The returned thread or <code>None</code> if not found.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* create_thread(***, *name*, *message=None*, *auto_archive_duration=...*, *type=None*, *reason=None*, *invitable=True*, *slowmode_delay=None*)<a href="#discord.TextChannel.create_thread" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Creates a thread in this text channel.

To create a public thread, you must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.create_public_threads" title="discord.Permissions.create_public_threads"><code>create_public_threads</code></a>. For a private thread, <a href="#discord.Permissions.create_private_threads" title="discord.Permissions.create_private_threads"><code>create_private_threads</code></a> is needed instead.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The name of the thread.
- **message** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>]) – A snowflake representing the message to create the thread with. If <code>None</code> is passed then a private thread is created. Defaults to <code>None</code>.
- **auto\_archive\_duration** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) –

  The duration in minutes before a thread is automatically hidden from the channel list. If not provided, the channel’s default auto archive duration is used.

  Must be one of <code>60</code>, <code>1440</code>, <code>4320</code>, or <code>10080</code>, if provided.
- **type** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.ChannelType" title="discord.ChannelType"><code>ChannelType</code></a>]) – The type of thread to create. If a <code>message</code> is passed then this parameter is ignored, as a thread created with a message is always a public thread. By default this creates a private thread if this is <code>None</code>.
- **reason** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The reason for creating a new thread. Shows up on the audit log.
- **invitable** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether non-moderators can add users to the thread. Only applicable to private threads. Defaults to <code>True</code>.
- **slowmode\_delay** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) – Specifies the slowmode rate limit for user in this channel, in seconds. The maximum value possible is <code>21600</code>. By default no slowmode rate limit if this is <code>None</code>.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to create a thread.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Starting the thread failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The created thread

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*async for ... in* archived_threads(***, *private=False*, *joined=False*, *limit=100*, *before=None*)<a href="#discord.TextChannel.archived_threads" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterator" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterator</a> that iterates over all archived threads in this text channel, in order of decreasing ID for joined threads, and decreasing <a href="#discord.Thread.archive_timestamp" title="discord.Thread.archive_timestamp"><code>Thread.archive_timestamp</code></a> otherwise.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.read_message_history" title="discord.Permissions.read_message_history"><code>read_message_history</code></a> to do this. If iterating over private threads then <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_threads" title="discord.Permissions.manage_threads"><code>manage_threads</code></a> is also required.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **limit** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>]) – The number of threads to retrieve. If <code>None</code>, retrieves every archived thread in the channel. Note, however, that this would make it a slow operation.
- **before** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve archived channels before the given date or ID.
- **private** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to retrieve private archived threads.
- **joined** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to retrieve private archived threads that you’ve joined. You cannot set <code>joined</code> to <code>True</code> and <code>private</code> to <code>False</code>.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to get archived threads.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – The request to get the archived threads failed.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – <code>joined</code> was set to <code>True</code> and <code>private</code> was set to <code>False</code>. You cannot retrieve public archived threads that you have joined.

</dd><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a> – The archived threads.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*category<a href="#discord.TextChannel.category" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

The category this channel belongs to.

If there is no category then this is <code>None</code>.

<dd>

Optional\[<a href="#discord.CategoryChannel" title="discord.CategoryChannel"><code>CategoryChannel</code></a>]

List\[<a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* create_invite(***, *reason=None*, *max_age=0*, *max_uses=0*, *temporary=False*, *unique=True*, *target_type=None*, *target_user=None*, *target_application_id=None*, *guest=False*)<a href="#discord.TextChannel.create_invite" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Creates an instant invite from a text or voice channel.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.create_instant_invite" title="discord.Permissions.create_instant_invite"><code>create_instant_invite</code></a> to do this.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **max\_age** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – How long the invite should last in seconds. If it’s 0 then the invite doesn’t expire. Defaults to <code>0</code>.
- **max\_uses** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – How many uses the invite could be used for. If it’s 0 then there are unlimited uses. Defaults to <code>0</code>.
- **temporary** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Denotes that the invite grants temporary membership (i.e. they get kicked after they disconnect). Defaults to <code>False</code>.
- **unique** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Indicates if a unique invite URL should be created. Defaults to True. If this is set to <code>False</code> then it will return a previously created invite.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for creating this invite. Shows up on the audit log.
- **target\_type** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.InviteTarget" title="discord.InviteTarget"><code>InviteTarget</code></a>]) –

  The type of target for the voice channel invite, if any.

  New in version 2.0.
- **target\_user** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a>]) –

  The user whose stream to display for this invite, required if <code>target_type</code> is <a href="#discord.InviteTarget.stream" title="discord.InviteTarget.stream"><code>InviteTarget.stream</code></a>. The user must be streaming in the channel.

  New in version 2.0.
- **target\_application\_id:** –

  Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]: The id of the embedded application for the invite, required if <code>target_type</code> is <a href="#discord.InviteTarget.embedded_application" title="discord.InviteTarget.embedded_application"><code>InviteTarget.embedded_application</code></a>.

  New in version 2.0.
- **guest** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether the invite is a guest invite.

  New in version 2.6.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Invite creation failed.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The channel that was passed is a category or an invalid channel.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The invite that was created.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Invite" title="discord.Invite"><code>Invite</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*created_at<a href="#discord.TextChannel.created_at" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* delete(***, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.TextChannel.delete" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

**reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for deleting this channel. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_message(*id*, */*)<a href="#discord.TextChannel.fetch_message" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Retrieves a single <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> from the destination.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**id** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The message ID to look for.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The specified message was not found.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the permissions required to get a message.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Retrieving the message failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The message asked for.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*async for ... in* history(***, *limit=100*, *before=None*, *after=None*, *around=None*, *oldest_first=None*)<a href="#discord.TextChannel.history" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterator" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterator</a> that enables receiving the destination’s message history.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.read_message_history" title="discord.Permissions.read_message_history"><code>read_message_history</code></a> to do this.

Examples

Usage

```
counter = 0
async for message in channel.history(limit=200):
    if message.author == client.user:
        counter += 1

```

Flattening into a list:

```
messages = [message async for message in channel.history(limit=123)]
# messages is now a list of Message...

```

All parameters are optional.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **limit** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) – The number of messages to retrieve. If <code>None</code>, retrieves every message in the channel. Note, however, that this would make it a slow operation.
- **before** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve messages before this date or message. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.
- **after** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve messages after this date or message. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.
- **around** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve messages around this date or message. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time. When using this argument, the maximum limit is 101. Note that if the limit is an even number then this will return at most limit + 1 messages.
- **oldest\_first** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>]) – If set to <code>True</code>, return messages in oldest-&gt;newest order. Defaults to <code>True</code> if <code>after</code> is specified, otherwise <code>False</code>.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to get channel message history.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – The request to get message history failed.

</dd><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> – The message with the message data parsed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* invites()<a href="#discord.TextChannel.invites" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – An error occurred while fetching the information.

The string that allows you to mention the channel.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* move(***kwargs*)<a href="#discord.TextChannel.move" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

A rich interface to help move a channel relative to other channels.

If exact position movement is required, <code>edit</code> should be used instead.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_channels" title="discord.Permissions.manage_channels"><code>manage_channels</code></a> to do this.

Note

Voice channels will always be sorted below text channels. This is a Discord limitation.

New in version 1.7.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> or <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>ValueError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **beginning** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to move the channel to the beginning of the channel list (or category if given). This is mutually exclusive with <code>end</code>, <code>before</code>, and <code>after</code>.
- **end** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to move the channel to the end of the channel list (or category if given). This is mutually exclusive with <code>beginning</code>, <code>before</code>, and <code>after</code>.
- **before** (<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>) – Whether to move the channel before the given channel. This is mutually exclusive with <code>beginning</code>, <code>end</code>, and <code>after</code>.
- **after** (<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>) – Whether to move the channel after the given channel. This is mutually exclusive with <code>beginning</code>, <code>end</code>, and <code>before</code>.
- **offset** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The number of channels to offset the move by. For example, an offset of <code>2</code> with <code>beginning=True</code> would move it 2 after the beginning. A positive number moves it below while a negative number moves it above. Note that this number is relative and computed after the <code>beginning</code>, <code>end</code>, <code>before</code>, and <code>after</code> parameters.
- **category** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>]) – The category to move this channel under. If <code>None</code> is given then it moves it out of the category. This parameter is ignored if moving a category channel.
- **sync\_permissions** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to sync the permissions with the category (if given).
- **reason** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The reason for the move.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – An invalid position was given.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – A bad mix of arguments were passed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to move the channel.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Moving the channel failed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*overwrites<a href="#discord.TextChannel.overwrites" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns all of the channel’s overwrites.

This is returned as a dictionary where the key contains the target which can be either a <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a> or a <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> and the value is the overwrite as a <a href="#discord.PermissionOverwrite" title="discord.PermissionOverwrite"><code>PermissionOverwrite</code></a>.

Changed in version 2.0: Overwrites can now be type-aware <a href="#discord.Object" title="discord.Object"><code>Object</code></a> in case of cache lookup failure

<dl><dt>Returns</dt>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>overwrites_for(*obj*)<a href="#discord.TextChannel.overwrites_for" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

</dl><dl><dt>*property*permissions_synced<a href="#discord.TextChannel.permissions_synced" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
