</dl><dl><dt>pins(***, *limit=50*, *before=None*, *oldest_first=False*)<a href="#discord.TextChannel.pins" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Retrieves an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterator" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterator</a> of the pinned messages in the channel.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.view_channel" title="discord.Permissions.view_channel"><code>view_channel</code></a> and <a href="#discord.Permissions.read_message_history" title="discord.Permissions.read_message_history"><code>read_message_history</code></a> in order to use this.

Changed in version 2.6: Due to a change in Discord’s API, this now returns a paginated iterator instead of a list.

For backwards compatibility, you can still retrieve a list of pinned messages by using <code>await</code> on the returned object. This is however deprecated.

Note

Due to a limitation with the Discord API, the <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> object returned by this method does not contain complete <a href="#discord.Message.reactions" title="discord.Message.reactions"><code>Message.reactions</code></a> data.

Examples

Usage

```
counter = 0
async for message in channel.pins(limit=250):
    counter += 1

```

Flattening into a list:

```
messages = [message async for message in channel.pins(limit=50)]
# messages is now a list of Message...

```

All parameters are optional.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **limit** (*Optional**\[*<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)">*int*</a>*]*) –

  The number of pinned messages to retrieve. If <code>None</code>, it retrieves every pinned message in the channel. Note, however, that this would make it a slow operation. Defaults to <code>50</code>.

  New in version 2.6.
- **before** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>, <a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>]]) –

  Retrieve pinned messages before this time or snowflake. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.

  New in version 2.6.
- **oldest\_first** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  If set to <code>True</code>, return messages in oldest pin-&gt;newest pin order. Defaults to <code>False</code>.

  New in version 2.6.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the permission to retrieve pinned messages.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Retrieving the pinned messages failed.

</dd><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> – The pinned message with <a href="#discord.Message.pinned_at" title="discord.Message.pinned_at"><code>Message.pinned_at</code></a> set.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* send(*content=None*, ***, *tts=False*, *embed=None*, *embeds=None*, *file=None*, *files=None*, *stickers=None*, *delete_after=None*, *nonce=None*, *allowed_mentions=None*, *reference=None*, *mention_author=None*, *view=None*, *suppress_embeds=False*, *silent=False*, *poll=None*)<a href="#discord.TextChannel.send" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Sends a message to the destination with the content given.

The content must be a type that can convert to a string through <code>str(content)</code>. If the content is set to <code>None</code> (the default), then the <code>embed</code> parameter must be provided.

To upload a single file, the <code>file</code> parameter should be used with a single <a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a> object. To upload multiple files, the <code>files</code> parameter should be used with a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#list" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>list</code></a> of <a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a> objects. **Specifying both parameters will lead to an exception**.

To upload a single embed, the <code>embed</code> parameter should be used with a single <a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a> object. To upload multiple embeds, the <code>embeds</code> parameter should be used with a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#list" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>list</code></a> of <a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a> objects. **Specifying both parameters will lead to an exception**.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> or <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>ValueError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **content** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The content of the message to send.
- **tts** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Indicates if the message should be sent using text-to-speech.
- **embed** (<a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a>) – The rich embed for the content.
- **embeds** (List\[<a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a>]) –

  A list of embeds to upload. Must be a maximum of 10.

  New in version 2.0.
- **file** (<a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a>) – The file to upload.
- **files** (List\[<a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a>]) – A list of files to upload. Must be a maximum of 10.
- **nonce** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The nonce to use for sending this message. If the message was successfully sent, then the message will have a nonce with this value.
- **delete\_after** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>float</code></a>) – If provided, the number of seconds to wait in the background before deleting the message we just sent. If the deletion fails, then it is silently ignored.
- **allowed\_mentions** (<a href="#discord.AllowedMentions" title="discord.AllowedMentions"><code>AllowedMentions</code></a>) –

  Controls the mentions being processed in this message. If this is passed, then the object is merged with <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a>. The merging behaviour only overrides attributes that have been explicitly passed to the object, otherwise it uses the attributes set in <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a>. If no object is passed at all then the defaults given by <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a> are used instead.

  New in version 1.4.
- **reference** (Union\[<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>, <a href="#discord.MessageReference" title="discord.MessageReference"><code>MessageReference</code></a>, <a href="#discord.PartialMessage" title="discord.PartialMessage"><code>PartialMessage</code></a>]) –

  A reference to the <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> to which you are referencing, this can be created using <a href="#discord.Message.to_reference" title="discord.Message.to_reference"><code>to_reference()</code></a> or passed directly as a <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>. In the event of a replying reference, you can control whether this mentions the author of the referenced message using the <a href="#discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user" title="discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user"><code>replied_user</code></a> attribute of <code>allowed_mentions</code> or by setting <code>mention_author</code>.

  New in version 1.6.
- **mention\_author** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>]) –

  If set, overrides the <a href="#discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user" title="discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user"><code>replied_user</code></a> attribute of <code>allowed_mentions</code>.

  New in version 1.6.
- **view** (Union\[<a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.ui.View" title="discord.ui.View"><code>discord.ui.View</code></a>, <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.ui.LayoutView" title="discord.ui.LayoutView"><code>discord.ui.LayoutView</code></a>]) –

  A Discord UI View to add to the message.

  New in version 2.0.
- **stickers** (Sequence\[Union\[<a href="#discord.GuildSticker" title="discord.GuildSticker"><code>GuildSticker</code></a>, <a href="#discord.StickerItem" title="discord.StickerItem"><code>StickerItem</code></a>]]) –

  A list of stickers to upload. Must be a maximum of 3.

  New in version 2.0.
- **suppress\_embeds** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to suppress embeds for the message. This sends the message without any embeds if set to <code>True</code>.

  New in version 2.0.
- **silent** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to suppress push and desktop notifications for the message. This will increment the mention counter in the UI, but will not actually send a notification.

  New in version 2.2.
- **poll** (<a href="#discord.Poll" title="discord.Poll"><code>Poll</code></a>) –

  The poll to send with this message.

  New in version 2.4.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Sending the message failed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to send the message.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – You sent a message with the same nonce as one that has been explicitly deleted shortly earlier.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – The <code>files</code> or <code>embeds</code> list is not of the appropriate size.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – You specified both <code>file</code> and <code>files</code>, or you specified both <code>embed</code> and <code>embeds</code>, or the <code>reference</code> object is not a <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>, <a href="#discord.MessageReference" title="discord.MessageReference"><code>MessageReference</code></a> or <a href="#discord.PartialMessage" title="discord.PartialMessage"><code>PartialMessage</code></a>.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The message that was sent.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* set_permissions(*target*, ***, *overwrite=see - below*, *reason=None*, ***permissions*)<a href="#discord.TextChannel.set_permissions" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Sets the channel specific permission overwrites for a target in the channel.

The <code>target</code> parameter should either be a <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> or a <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a> that belongs to guild.

The <code>overwrite</code> parameter, if given, must either be <code>None</code> or <a href="#discord.PermissionOverwrite" title="discord.PermissionOverwrite"><code>PermissionOverwrite</code></a>. For convenience, you can pass in keyword arguments denoting <a href="#discord.Permissions" title="discord.Permissions"><code>Permissions</code></a> attributes. If this is done, then you cannot mix the keyword arguments with the <code>overwrite</code> parameter.

If the <code>overwrite</code> parameter is <code>None</code>, then the permission overwrites are deleted.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_roles" title="discord.Permissions.manage_roles"><code>manage_roles</code></a> to do this.

Note

This method *replaces* the old overwrites with the ones given.

Examples

Setting allow and deny:

```
await message.channel.set_permissions(message.author, read_messages=True,
                                                      send_messages=False)

```

Deleting overwrites

```
await channel.set_permissions(member, overwrite=None)

```

Using <a href="#discord.PermissionOverwrite" title="discord.PermissionOverwrite"><code>PermissionOverwrite</code></a>

```
overwrite = discord.PermissionOverwrite()
overwrite.send_messages = False
overwrite.read_messages = True
await channel.set_permissions(member, overwrite=overwrite)

```

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **target** (Union\[<a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>]) – The member or role to overwrite permissions for.
- **overwrite** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.PermissionOverwrite" title="discord.PermissionOverwrite"><code>PermissionOverwrite</code></a>]) – The permissions to allow and deny to the target, or <code>None</code> to delete the overwrite.
- **\*\*permissions** – A keyword argument list of permissions to set for ease of use. Cannot be mixed with <code>overwrite</code>.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for doing this action. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to edit channel specific permissions.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Editing channel specific permissions failed.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The role or member being edited is not part of the guild.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – The <code>overwrite</code> parameter was invalid or the target type was not <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a> or <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – The <code>overwrite</code> parameter and <code>positions</code> parameters were both unset.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl>

</dl><dl><dt>*property*members<a href="#discord.ForumChannel.members" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

<dl><dt>Type</dt>

List\[<a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>permissions_for(*obj*, */*)<a href="#discord.ForumChannel.permissions_for" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Handles permission resolution for the <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> or <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>.

This function takes into consideration the following cases:

- Guild owner
- Guild roles
- Channel overrides
- Member overrides
- Implicit permissions
- Member timeout
- User installed app

If a <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a> is passed, then it checks the permissions someone with that role would have, which is essentially:

- The default role permissions
- The permissions of the role used as a parameter
- The default role permission overwrites
- The permission overwrites of the role used as a parameter

Changed in version 2.0: The object passed in can now be a role object.

Changed in version 2.0: <code>obj</code> parameter is now positional-only.

Changed in version 2.4: User installed apps are now taken into account. The permissions returned for a user installed app mirrors the permissions Discord returns in <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.Interaction.app_permissions" title="discord.Interaction.app_permissions"><code>app_permissions</code></a>, though it is recommended to use that attribute instead.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**obj** (Union\[<a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>]) – The object to resolve permissions for. This could be either a member or a role. If it’s a role then member overwrites are not computed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The resolved permissions for the member or role.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Permissions" title="discord.Permissions"><code>Permissions</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>get_thread(*thread_id*, */*)<a href="#discord.ForumChannel.get_thread" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns a thread with the given ID.

Note

This does not always retrieve archived threads, as they are not retained in the internal cache. Use <a href="#discord.Guild.fetch_channel" title="discord.Guild.fetch_channel"><code>Guild.fetch_channel()</code></a> instead.

New in version 2.2.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**thread\_id** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The ID to search for.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The returned thread or <code>None</code> if not found.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*threads<a href="#discord.ForumChannel.threads" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

</dd></dl></dd>

The tag with the given ID, or <code>None</code> if not found.

Optional\[<a href="#discord.ForumTag" title="discord.ForumTag"><code>ForumTag</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>is_nsfw()<a href="#discord.ForumChannel.is_nsfw" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

New in version 2.4.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*await* clone(***, *name=None*, *category=None*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.ForumChannel.clone" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Clones this channel. This creates a channel with the same properties as this channel.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_channels" title="discord.Permissions.manage_channels"><code>manage_channels</code></a> to do this.

New in version 1.1.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The name of the new channel. If not provided, defaults to this channel name.
- **category** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.CategoryChannel" title="discord.CategoryChannel"><code>CategoryChannel</code></a>]) –

  The category the new channel belongs to. This parameter is ignored if cloning a category channel.

  New in version 2.5.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for cloning this channel. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to create this channel.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Creating the channel failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The channel that was created.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.abc.GuildChannel" title="discord.abc.GuildChannel"><code>abc.GuildChannel</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* edit(***, *reason=None*, ***options*)<a href="#discord.ForumChannel.edit" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Edits the forum.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_channels" title="discord.Permissions.manage_channels"><code>manage_channels</code></a> to do this.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The new forum name.
- **topic** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The new forum’s topic.
- **position** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The new forum’s position.
- **nsfw** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – To mark the forum as NSFW or not.
- **sync\_permissions** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to sync permissions with the forum’s new or pre-existing category. Defaults to <code>False</code>.
- **category** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.CategoryChannel" title="discord.CategoryChannel"><code>CategoryChannel</code></a>]) – The new category for this forum. Can be <code>None</code> to remove the category.
- **slowmode\_delay** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – Specifies the slowmode rate limit for user in this forum, in seconds. A value of <code>0</code> disables slowmode. The maximum value possible is <code>21600</code>.
- **type** (<a href="#discord.ChannelType" title="discord.ChannelType"><code>ChannelType</code></a>) – Change the type of this text forum. Currently, only conversion between <a href="#discord.ChannelType.text" title="discord.ChannelType.text"><code>ChannelType.text</code></a> and <a href="#discord.ChannelType.news" title="discord.ChannelType.news"><code>ChannelType.news</code></a> is supported. This is only available to guilds that contain <code>NEWS</code> in <a href="#discord.Guild.features" title="discord.Guild.features"><code>Guild.features</code></a>.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for editing this forum. Shows up on the audit log.
- **overwrites** (<code>Mapping</code>) – A <code>Mapping</code> of target (either a role or a member) to <a href="#discord.PermissionOverwrite" title="discord.PermissionOverwrite"><code>PermissionOverwrite</code></a> to apply to the forum.
- **default\_auto\_archive\_duration** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The new default auto archive duration in minutes for threads created in this channel. Must be one of <code>60</code>, <code>1440</code>, <code>4320</code>, or <code>10080</code>.
- **available\_tags** (Sequence\[<a href="#discord.ForumTag" title="discord.ForumTag"><code>ForumTag</code></a>]) –

  The new available tags for this forum.

  New in version 2.1.
- **default\_thread\_slowmode\_delay** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) –

  The new default slowmode delay for threads in this channel.

  New in version 2.1.
- **default\_reaction\_emoji** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.Emoji" title="discord.Emoji"><code>Emoji</code></a>, <a href="#discord.PartialEmoji" title="discord.PartialEmoji"><code>PartialEmoji</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]]) –

  The new default reaction emoji for threads in this channel.

  New in version 2.1.
- **default\_layout** (<a href="#discord.ForumLayoutType" title="discord.ForumLayoutType"><code>ForumLayoutType</code></a>) –

  The new default layout for posts in this forum.

  New in version 2.2.
- **default\_sort\_order** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.ForumOrderType" title="discord.ForumOrderType"><code>ForumOrderType</code></a>]) –

  The new default sort order for posts in this forum.

  New in version 2.3.
- **require\_tag** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to require a tag for threads in this channel or not.

  New in version 2.1.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – The new <code>position</code> is less than 0 or greater than the number of channels.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – The permission overwrite information is not in proper form or a type is not the expected type.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to edit the forum.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Editing the forum failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The newly edited forum channel. If the edit was only positional then <code>None</code> is returned instead.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="#discord.ForumChannel" title="discord.ForumChannel"><code>ForumChannel</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* create_tag(***, *name*, *emoji=None*, *moderated=False*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.ForumChannel.create_tag" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Creates a new tag in this forum.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_channels" title="discord.Permissions.manage_channels"><code>manage_channels</code></a> to do this.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The name of the tag. Can only be up to 20 characters.
- **emoji** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>, <a href="#discord.PartialEmoji" title="discord.PartialEmoji"><code>PartialEmoji</code></a>]]) – The emoji to use for the tag.
- **moderated** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether the tag can only be applied by moderators.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for creating this tag. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to create a tag in this forum.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Creating the tag failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The newly created tag.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.ForumTag" title="discord.ForumTag"><code>ForumTag</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* create_thread(***, *name*, *auto_archive_duration=...*, *slowmode_delay=None*, *content=None*, *tts=False*, *embed=...*, *embeds=...*, *file=...*, *files=...*, *stickers=...*, *allowed_mentions=...*, *mention_author=...*, *applied_tags=...*, *view=...*, *suppress_embeds=False*, *silent=False*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.ForumChannel.create_thread" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Creates a thread in this forum.

This thread is a public thread with the initial message given. Currently in order to start a thread in this forum, the user needs <a href="#discord.Permissions.send_messages" title="discord.Permissions.send_messages"><code>send_messages</code></a>.

You must send at least one of <code>content</code>, <code>embed</code>, <code>embeds</code>, <code>file</code>, <code>files</code>, or <code>view</code> to create a thread in a forum, since forum channels must have a starter message.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The name of the thread.
- **auto\_archive\_duration** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) –

  The duration in minutes before a thread is automatically hidden from the channel list. If not provided, the channel’s default auto archive duration is used.

  Must be one of <code>60</code>, <code>1440</code>, <code>4320</code>, or <code>10080</code>, if provided.
- **slowmode\_delay** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) – Specifies the slowmode rate limit for user in this channel, in seconds. The maximum value possible is <code>21600</code>. By default no slowmode rate limit if this is <code>None</code>.
- **content** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The content of the message to send with the thread.
- **tts** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Indicates if the message should be sent using text-to-speech.
- **embed** (<a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a>) – The rich embed for the content.
- **embeds** (List\[<a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a>]) – A list of embeds to upload. Must be a maximum of 10.
- **file** (<a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a>) – The file to upload.
- **files** (List\[<a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a>]) – A list of files to upload. Must be a maximum of 10.
- **allowed\_mentions** (<a href="#discord.AllowedMentions" title="discord.AllowedMentions"><code>AllowedMentions</code></a>) – Controls the mentions being processed in this message. If this is passed, then the object is merged with <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a>. The merging behaviour only overrides attributes that have been explicitly passed to the object, otherwise it uses the attributes set in <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a>. If no object is passed at all then the defaults given by <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a> are used instead.
- **mention\_author** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – If set, overrides the <a href="#discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user" title="discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user"><code>replied_user</code></a> attribute of <code>allowed_mentions</code>.
- **applied\_tags** (List\[<a href="#discord.ForumTag" title="discord.ForumTag"><code>discord.ForumTag</code></a>]) – A list of tags to apply to the thread.
- **view** (Union\[<a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.ui.View" title="discord.ui.View"><code>discord.ui.View</code></a>, <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.ui.LayoutView" title="discord.ui.LayoutView"><code>discord.ui.LayoutView</code></a>]) – A Discord UI View to add to the message.
- **stickers** (Sequence\[Union\[<a href="#discord.GuildSticker" title="discord.GuildSticker"><code>GuildSticker</code></a>, <a href="#discord.StickerItem" title="discord.StickerItem"><code>StickerItem</code></a>]]) – A list of stickers to upload. Must be a maximum of 3.
- **suppress\_embeds** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to suppress embeds for the message. This sends the message without any embeds if set to <code>True</code>.
- **silent** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to suppress push and desktop notifications for the message. This will increment the mention counter in the UI, but will not actually send a notification.

  New in version 2.7.
- **reason** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The reason for creating a new thread. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to create a thread.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Starting the thread failed.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – The <code>files</code> or <code>embeds</code> list is not of the appropriate size.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – You specified both <code>file</code> and <code>files</code>, or you specified both <code>embed</code> and <code>embeds</code>.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The created thread with the created message. This is also accessible as a namedtuple with <code>thread</code> and <code>message</code> fields.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

Tuple\[<a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>

</dl><dl><dt>*async for ... in* archived_threads(***, *limit=100*, *before=None*)<a href="#discord.ForumChannel.archived_threads" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

Returns an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterator" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterator</a> that iterates over all archived threads in this forum in order of decreasing <a href="#discord.Thread.archive_timestamp" title="discord.Thread.archive_timestamp"><code>Thread.archive_timestamp</code></a>.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.read_message_history" title="discord.Permissions.read_message_history"><code>read_message_history</code></a> to do this.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>

If <code>None</code>, retrieves every archived thread in the channel. Note, however, that this would make it a slow operation.
- **before** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve archived channels before the given date or ID.

</dd><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a> – The archived threads.

</dd></dl></dd>

</dl><dl><dt>*await* create_invite(***, *reason=None*, *max_age=0*, *max_uses=0*, *temporary=False*, *unique=True*, *target_type=None*, *target_user=None*, *target_application_id=None*, *guest=False*)<a href="#discord.ForumChannel.create_invite" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Creates an instant invite from a text or voice channel.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.create_instant_invite" title="discord.Permissions.create_instant_invite"><code>create_instant_invite</code></a> to do this.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **max\_age** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – How long the invite should last in seconds. If it’s 0 then the invite doesn’t expire. Defaults to <code>0</code>.
- **max\_uses** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – How many uses the invite could be used for. If it’s 0 then there are unlimited uses. Defaults to <code>0</code>.
- **temporary** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Denotes that the invite grants temporary membership (i.e. they get kicked after they disconnect). Defaults to <code>False</code>.
- **unique** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Indicates if a unique invite URL should be created. Defaults to True. If this is set to <code>False</code> then it will return a previously created invite.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for creating this invite. Shows up on the audit log.
- **target\_type** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.InviteTarget" title="discord.InviteTarget"><code>InviteTarget</code></a>]) –

  The type of target for the voice channel invite, if any.

  New in version 2.0.
- **target\_user** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a>]) –

  The user whose stream to display for this invite, required if <code>target_type</code> is <a href="#discord.InviteTarget.stream" title="discord.InviteTarget.stream"><code>InviteTarget.stream</code></a>. The user must be streaming in the channel.

  New in version 2.0.
- **target\_application\_id:** –

  Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]: The id of the embedded application for the invite, required if <code>target_type</code> is <a href="#discord.InviteTarget.embedded_application" title="discord.InviteTarget.embedded_application"><code>InviteTarget.embedded_application</code></a>.

  New in version 2.0.
- **guest** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether the invite is a guest invite.

  New in version 2.6.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Invite creation failed.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The channel that was passed is a category or an invalid channel.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The invite that was created.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Invite" title="discord.Invite"><code>Invite</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* move(***kwargs*)<a href="#discord.ForumChannel.move" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

A rich interface to help move a channel relative to other channels.

If exact position movement is required, <code>edit</code> should be used instead.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_channels" title="discord.Permissions.manage_channels"><code>manage_channels</code></a> to do this.

Note

Voice channels will always be sorted below text channels. This is a Discord limitation.

New in version 1.7.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> or <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>ValueError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **beginning** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to move the channel to the beginning of the channel list (or category if given). This is mutually exclusive with <code>end</code>, <code>before</code>, and <code>after</code>.
- **end** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to move the channel to the end of the channel list (or category if given). This is mutually exclusive with <code>beginning</code>, <code>before</code>, and <code>after</code>.
- **before** (<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>) – Whether to move the channel before the given channel. This is mutually exclusive with <code>beginning</code>, <code>end</code>, and <code>after</code>.
- **after** (<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>) – Whether to move the channel after the given channel. This is mutually exclusive with <code>beginning</code>, <code>end</code>, and <code>before</code>.
- **offset** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The number of channels to offset the move by. For example, an offset of <code>2</code> with <code>beginning=True</code> would move it 2 after the beginning. A positive number moves it below while a negative number moves it above. Note that this number is relative and computed after the <code>beginning</code>, <code>end</code>, <code>before</code>, and <code>after</code> parameters.
- **category** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>]) – The category to move this channel under. If <code>None</code> is given then it moves it out of the category. This parameter is ignored if moving a category channel.
- **sync\_permissions** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to sync the permissions with the category (if given).
- **reason** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The reason for the move.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – An invalid position was given.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – A bad mix of arguments were passed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to move the channel.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Moving the channel failed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*overwrites<a href="#discord.ForumChannel.overwrites" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns all of the channel’s overwrites.

This is returned as a dictionary where the key contains the target which can be either a <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a> or a <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> and the value is the overwrite as a <a href="#discord.PermissionOverwrite" title="discord.PermissionOverwrite"><code>PermissionOverwrite</code></a>.

Changed in version 2.0: Overwrites can now be type-aware <a href="#discord.Object" title="discord.Object"><code>Object</code></a> in case of cache lookup failure

<dl><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The channel’s permission overwrites.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

Dict\[Union\[<a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Object" title="discord.Object"><code>Object</code></a>], <a href="#discord.PermissionOverwrite" title="discord.PermissionOverwrite"><code>PermissionOverwrite</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>overwrites_for(*obj*)<a href="#discord.ForumChannel.overwrites_for" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns the channel-specific overwrites for a member or a role.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**obj** (Union\[<a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>, <a href="#discord.abc.User" title="discord.abc.User"><code>User</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Object" title="discord.Object"><code>Object</code></a>]) – The role or user denoting whose overwrite to get.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The permission overwrites for this object.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.PermissionOverwrite" title="discord.PermissionOverwrite"><code>PermissionOverwrite</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*permissions_synced<a href="#discord.ForumChannel.permissions_synced" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Whether or not the permissions for this channel are synced with the category it belongs to.

If there is no category then this is <code>False</code>.

New in version 1.3.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* set_permissions(*target*, ***, *overwrite=see - below*, *reason=None*, ***permissions*)<a href="#discord.ForumChannel.set_permissions" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Sets the channel specific permission overwrites for a target in the channel.

The <code>target</code> parameter should either be a <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> or a <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a> that belongs to guild.

The <code>overwrite</code> parameter, if given, must either be <code>None</code> or <a href="#discord.PermissionOverwrite" title="discord.PermissionOverwrite"><code>PermissionOverwrite</code></a>. For convenience, you can pass in keyword arguments denoting <a href="#discord.Permissions" title="discord.Permissions"><code>Permissions</code></a> attributes. If this is done, then you cannot mix the keyword arguments with the <code>overwrite</code> parameter.

If the <code>overwrite</code> parameter is <code>None</code>, then the permission overwrites are deleted.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_roles" title="discord.Permissions.manage_roles"><code>manage_roles</code></a> to do this.

Note

This method *replaces* the old overwrites with the ones given.

Examples

Setting allow and deny:

```
await message.channel.set_permissions(message.author, read_messages=True,
                                                      send_messages=False)

```

Deleting overwrites

```
await channel.set_permissions(member, overwrite=None)

```

Using <a href="#discord.PermissionOverwrite" title="discord.PermissionOverwrite"><code>PermissionOverwrite</code></a>

```
overwrite = discord.PermissionOverwrite()
overwrite.send_messages = False
overwrite.read_messages = True
await channel.set_permissions(member, overwrite=overwrite)

```

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **target** (Union\[<a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>]) – The member or role to overwrite permissions for.
- **overwrite** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.PermissionOverwrite" title="discord.PermissionOverwrite"><code>PermissionOverwrite</code></a>]) – The permissions to allow and deny to the target, or <code>None</code> to delete the overwrite.
- **\*\*permissions** – A keyword argument list of permissions to set for ease of use. Cannot be mixed with <code>overwrite</code>.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for doing this action. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to edit channel specific permissions.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Editing channel specific permissions failed.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The role or member being edited is not part of the guild.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – The <code>overwrite</code> parameter was invalid or the target type was not <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a> or <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – The <code>overwrite</code> parameter and <code>positions</code> parameters were both unset.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl>

</dl><dl><dt>*async with* typing()<a href="#discord.Thread.typing" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns an asynchronous context manager that allows you to send a typing indicator to the destination for an indefinite period of time, or 10 seconds if the context manager is called using <code>await</code>.

Example Usage:

```
async with channel.typing():
    # simulate something heavy
    await asyncio.sleep(20)

await channel.send('Done!')

```

Example Usage:

```
await channel.typing()
# Do some computational magic for about 10 seconds
await channel.send('Done!')

```

Changed in version 2.0: This no longer works with the <code>with</code> syntax, <code>async with</code> must be used instead.

Changed in version 2.0: Added functionality to <code>await</code> the context manager to send a typing indicator for 10 seconds.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>is_news()<a href="#discord.Thread.is_news" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>: Whether the thread is a news thread.

A news thread is a thread that has a parent that is a news channel, i.e. <a href="#discord.TextChannel.is_news" title="discord.TextChannel.is_news"><code>TextChannel.is_news()</code></a> is <code>True</code>.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>is_nsfw()<a href="#discord.Thread.is_nsfw" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>: Whether the thread is NSFW or not.

An NSFW thread is a thread that has a parent that is an NSFW channel, i.e. <a href="#discord.TextChannel.is_nsfw" title="discord.TextChannel.is_nsfw"><code>TextChannel.is_nsfw()</code></a> is <code>True</code>.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>permissions_for(*obj*, */*)<a href="#discord.Thread.permissions_for" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Handles permission resolution for the <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> or <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>.

Since threads do not have their own permissions, they mostly inherit them from the parent channel with some implicit permissions changed.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**obj** (Union\[<a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Role" title="discord.Role"><code>Role</code></a>]) – The object to resolve permissions for. This could be either a member or a role. If it’s a role then member overwrites are not computed.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.ClientException" title="discord.ClientException">**ClientException**</a> – The parent channel was not cached and returned <code>None</code>

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The resolved permissions for the member or role.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Permissions" title="discord.Permissions"><code>Permissions</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* delete_messages(*messages*, */*, ***, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Thread.delete_messages" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Deletes a list of messages. This is similar to <a href="#discord.Message.delete" title="discord.Message.delete"><code>Message.delete()</code></a> except it bulk deletes multiple messages.

As a special case, if the number of messages is 0, then nothing is done. If the number of messages is 1 then single message delete is done. If it’s more than two, then bulk delete is used.

You cannot bulk delete more than 100 messages or messages that are older than 14 days old.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_messages" title="discord.Permissions.manage_messages"><code>manage_messages</code></a> to do this.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **messages** (Iterable\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>]) – An iterable of messages denoting which ones to bulk delete.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for deleting the messages. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.ClientException" title="discord.ClientException">**ClientException**</a> – The number of messages to delete was more than 100.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have proper permissions to delete the messages or you’re not using a bot account.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – If single delete, then the message was already deleted.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Deleting the messages failed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* purge(***, *limit=100*, *check=...*, *before=None*, *after=None*, *around=None*, *oldest_first=None*, *bulk=True*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Thread.purge" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Purges a list of messages that meet the criteria given by the predicate <code>check</code>. If a <code>check</code> is not provided then all messages are deleted without discrimination.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_messages" title="discord.Permissions.manage_messages"><code>manage_messages</code></a> to delete messages even if they are your own. Having <a href="#discord.Permissions.read_message_history" title="discord.Permissions.read_message_history"><code>read_message_history</code></a> is also needed to retrieve message history.

Examples

Deleting bot’s messages

```
def is_me(m):
    return m.author == client.user

deleted = await thread.purge(limit=100, check=is_me)
await thread.send(f'Deleted {len(deleted)} message(s)')

```

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **limit** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) – The number of messages to search through. This is not the number of messages that will be deleted, though it can be.
- **check** (Callable\[\[<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>], <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>]) – The function used to check if a message should be deleted. It must take a <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> as its sole parameter.
- **before** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Same as <code>before</code> in <a href="#discord.Thread.history" title="discord.Thread.history"><code>history()</code></a>.
- **after** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Same as <code>after</code> in <a href="#discord.Thread.history" title="discord.Thread.history"><code>history()</code></a>.
- **around** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Same as <code>around</code> in <a href="#discord.Thread.history" title="discord.Thread.history"><code>history()</code></a>.
- **oldest\_first** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>]) – Same as <code>oldest_first</code> in <a href="#discord.Thread.history" title="discord.Thread.history"><code>history()</code></a>.
- **bulk** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – If <code>True</code>, use bulk delete. Setting this to <code>False</code> is useful for mass-deleting a bot’s own messages without <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_messages" title="discord.Permissions.manage_messages"><code>Permissions.manage_messages</code></a>. When <code>True</code>, will fall back to single delete if messages are older than two weeks.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for purging the messages. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have proper permissions to do the actions required.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Purging the messages failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The list of messages that were deleted.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

List\[<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* edit(***, *name=...*, *archived=...*, *locked=...*, *invitable=...*, *pinned=...*, *slowmode_delay=...*, *auto_archive_duration=...*, *applied_tags=...*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Thread.edit" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Edits the thread.

Editing the thread requires <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_threads" title="discord.Permissions.manage_threads"><code>Permissions.manage_threads</code></a>. The thread creator can also edit <code>name</code>, <code>archived</code> or <code>auto_archive_duration</code>. Note that if the thread is locked then only those with <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_threads" title="discord.Permissions.manage_threads"><code>Permissions.manage_threads</code></a> can unarchive a thread.

The thread must be unarchived to be edited.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The new name of the thread.
- **archived** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to archive the thread or not.
- **locked** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to lock the thread or not.
- **pinned** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to pin the thread or not. This only works if the thread is part of a forum.
- **invitable** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether non-moderators can add other non-moderators to this thread. Only available for private threads.
- **auto\_archive\_duration** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The new duration in minutes before a thread is automatically hidden from the channel list. Must be one of <code>60</code>, <code>1440</code>, <code>4320</code>, or <code>10080</code>.
- **slowmode\_delay** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – Specifies the slowmode rate limit for user in this thread, in seconds. A value of <code>0</code> disables slowmode. The maximum value possible is <code>21600</code>.
- **applied\_tags** (Sequence\[<a href="#discord.ForumTag" title="discord.ForumTag"><code>ForumTag</code></a>]) –

  The new tags to apply to the thread. There can only be up to 5 tags applied to a thread.

  New in version 2.1.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for editing this thread. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to edit the thread.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Editing the thread failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The newly edited thread.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* add_tags(**tags*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Thread.add_tags" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Adds the given forum tags to a thread.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_threads" title="discord.Permissions.manage_threads"><code>manage_threads</code></a> to use this or the thread must be owned by you.

Tags that have <a href="#discord.ForumTag.moderated" title="discord.ForumTag.moderated"><code>ForumTag.moderated</code></a> set to <code>True</code> require <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_threads" title="discord.Permissions.manage_threads"><code>manage_threads</code></a> to be added.

The maximum number of tags that can be added to a thread is 5.

The parent channel must be a <a href="#discord.ForumChannel" title="discord.ForumChannel"><code>ForumChannel</code></a>.

New in version 2.1.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **\*tags** (<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>) – An argument list of <a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a> representing a <a href="#discord.ForumTag" title="discord.ForumTag"><code>ForumTag</code></a> to add to the thread.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for adding these tags.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to add these tags.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Adding tags failed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* remove_tags(**tags*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Thread.remove_tags" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Remove the given forum tags to a thread.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_threads" title="discord.Permissions.manage_threads"><code>manage_threads</code></a> to use this or the thread must be owned by you.

The parent channel must be a <a href="#discord.ForumChannel" title="discord.ForumChannel"><code>ForumChannel</code></a>.

New in version 2.1.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **\*tags** (<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>) – An argument list of <a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a> representing a <a href="#discord.ForumTag" title="discord.ForumTag"><code>ForumTag</code></a> to remove to the thread.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for removing these tags.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to remove these tags.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Removing tags failed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* join()<a href="#discord.Thread.join" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

If the thread is private and <a href="#discord.Thread.invitable" title="discord.Thread.invitable"><code>invitable</code></a> is <code>False</code> then <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_messages" title="discord.Permissions.manage_messages"><code>manage_messages</code></a> is required to add a user to the thread.

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Removing the user from the thread failed.

</dd></dl></dd>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* delete(***, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.Thread.delete" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_message(*id*, */*)<a href="#discord.Thread.fetch_message" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
