Retrieves a single <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> from the destination.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**id** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The message ID to look for.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The specified message was not found.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the permissions required to get a message.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Retrieving the message failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The message asked for.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*async for ... in* history(***, *limit=100*, *before=None*, *after=None*, *around=None*, *oldest_first=None*)<a href="#discord.DMChannel.history" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterator" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterator</a> that enables receiving the destination’s message history.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.read_message_history" title="discord.Permissions.read_message_history"><code>read_message_history</code></a> to do this.

Examples

Usage

```
counter = 0
async for message in channel.history(limit=200):
    if message.author == client.user:
        counter += 1

```

Flattening into a list:

```
messages = [message async for message in channel.history(limit=123)]
# messages is now a list of Message...

```

All parameters are optional.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **limit** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) – The number of messages to retrieve. If <code>None</code>, retrieves every message in the channel. Note, however, that this would make it a slow operation.
- **before** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve messages before this date or message. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.
- **after** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve messages after this date or message. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.
- **around** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve messages around this date or message. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time. When using this argument, the maximum limit is 101. Note that if the limit is an even number then this will return at most limit + 1 messages.
- **oldest\_first** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>]) – If set to <code>True</code>, return messages in oldest-&gt;newest order. Defaults to <code>True</code> if <code>after</code> is specified, otherwise <code>False</code>.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to get channel message history.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – The request to get message history failed.

</dd><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> – The message with the message data parsed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>pins(***, *limit=50*, *before=None*, *oldest_first=False*)<a href="#discord.DMChannel.pins" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Retrieves an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterator" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterator</a> of the pinned messages in the channel.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.view_channel" title="discord.Permissions.view_channel"><code>view_channel</code></a> and <a href="#discord.Permissions.read_message_history" title="discord.Permissions.read_message_history"><code>read_message_history</code></a> in order to use this.

Changed in version 2.6: Due to a change in Discord’s API, this now returns a paginated iterator instead of a list.

For backwards compatibility, you can still retrieve a list of pinned messages by using <code>await</code> on the returned object. This is however deprecated.

Note

Due to a limitation with the Discord API, the <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> object returned by this method does not contain complete <a href="#discord.Message.reactions" title="discord.Message.reactions"><code>Message.reactions</code></a> data.

Examples

Usage

```
counter = 0
async for message in channel.pins(limit=250):
    counter += 1

```

Flattening into a list:

```
messages = [message async for message in channel.pins(limit=50)]
# messages is now a list of Message...

```

All parameters are optional.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **limit** (*Optional**\[*<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)">*int*</a>*]*) –

  The number of pinned messages to retrieve. If <code>None</code>, it retrieves every pinned message in the channel. Note, however, that this would make it a slow operation. Defaults to <code>50</code>.

  New in version 2.6.
- **before** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>, <a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>]]) –

  Retrieve pinned messages before this time or snowflake. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.

  New in version 2.6.
- **oldest\_first** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  If set to <code>True</code>, return messages in oldest pin-&gt;newest pin order. Defaults to <code>False</code>.

  New in version 2.6.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the permission to retrieve pinned messages.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Retrieving the pinned messages failed.

</dd><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> – The pinned message with <a href="#discord.Message.pinned_at" title="discord.Message.pinned_at"><code>Message.pinned_at</code></a> set.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* send(*content=None*, ***, *tts=False*, *embed=None*, *embeds=None*, *file=None*, *files=None*, *stickers=None*, *delete_after=None*, *nonce=None*, *allowed_mentions=None*, *reference=None*, *mention_author=None*, *view=None*, *suppress_embeds=False*, *silent=False*, *poll=None*)<a href="#discord.DMChannel.send" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Sends a message to the destination with the content given.

The content must be a type that can convert to a string through <code>str(content)</code>. If the content is set to <code>None</code> (the default), then the <code>embed</code> parameter must be provided.

To upload a single file, the <code>file</code> parameter should be used with a single <a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a> object. To upload multiple files, the <code>files</code> parameter should be used with a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#list" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>list</code></a> of <a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a> objects. **Specifying both parameters will lead to an exception**.

To upload a single embed, the <code>embed</code> parameter should be used with a single <a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a> object. To upload multiple embeds, the <code>embeds</code> parameter should be used with a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#list" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>list</code></a> of <a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a> objects. **Specifying both parameters will lead to an exception**.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> or <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>ValueError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **content** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The content of the message to send.
- **tts** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Indicates if the message should be sent using text-to-speech.
- **embed** (<a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a>) – The rich embed for the content.
- **embeds** (List\[<a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a>]) –

  A list of embeds to upload. Must be a maximum of 10.

  New in version 2.0.
- **file** (<a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a>) – The file to upload.
- **files** (List\[<a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a>]) – A list of files to upload. Must be a maximum of 10.
- **nonce** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The nonce to use for sending this message. If the message was successfully sent, then the message will have a nonce with this value.
- **delete\_after** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>float</code></a>) – If provided, the number of seconds to wait in the background before deleting the message we just sent. If the deletion fails, then it is silently ignored.
- **allowed\_mentions** (<a href="#discord.AllowedMentions" title="discord.AllowedMentions"><code>AllowedMentions</code></a>) –

  Controls the mentions being processed in this message. If this is passed, then the object is merged with <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a>. The merging behaviour only overrides attributes that have been explicitly passed to the object, otherwise it uses the attributes set in <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a>. If no object is passed at all then the defaults given by <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a> are used instead.

  New in version 1.4.
- **reference** (Union\[<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>, <a href="#discord.MessageReference" title="discord.MessageReference"><code>MessageReference</code></a>, <a href="#discord.PartialMessage" title="discord.PartialMessage"><code>PartialMessage</code></a>]) –

  A reference to the <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> to which you are referencing, this can be created using <a href="#discord.Message.to_reference" title="discord.Message.to_reference"><code>to_reference()</code></a> or passed directly as a <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>. In the event of a replying reference, you can control whether this mentions the author of the referenced message using the <a href="#discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user" title="discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user"><code>replied_user</code></a> attribute of <code>allowed_mentions</code> or by setting <code>mention_author</code>.

  New in version 1.6.
- **mention\_author** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>]) –

  If set, overrides the <a href="#discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user" title="discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user"><code>replied_user</code></a> attribute of <code>allowed_mentions</code>.

  New in version 1.6.
- **view** (Union\[<a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.ui.View" title="discord.ui.View"><code>discord.ui.View</code></a>, <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.ui.LayoutView" title="discord.ui.LayoutView"><code>discord.ui.LayoutView</code></a>]) –

  A Discord UI View to add to the message.

  New in version 2.0.
- **stickers** (Sequence\[Union\[<a href="#discord.GuildSticker" title="discord.GuildSticker"><code>GuildSticker</code></a>, <a href="#discord.StickerItem" title="discord.StickerItem"><code>StickerItem</code></a>]]) –

  A list of stickers to upload. Must be a maximum of 3.

  New in version 2.0.
- **suppress\_embeds** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to suppress embeds for the message. This sends the message without any embeds if set to <code>True</code>.

  New in version 2.0.
- **silent** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to suppress push and desktop notifications for the message. This will increment the mention counter in the UI, but will not actually send a notification.

  New in version 2.2.
- **poll** (<a href="#discord.Poll" title="discord.Poll"><code>Poll</code></a>) –

  The poll to send with this message.

  New in version 2.4.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Sending the message failed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to send the message.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – You sent a message with the same nonce as one that has been explicitly deleted shortly earlier.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – The <code>files</code> or <code>embeds</code> list is not of the appropriate size.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – You specified both <code>file</code> and <code>files</code>, or you specified both <code>embed</code> and <code>embeds</code>, or the <code>reference</code> object is not a <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>, <a href="#discord.MessageReference" title="discord.MessageReference"><code>MessageReference</code></a> or <a href="#discord.PartialMessage" title="discord.PartialMessage"><code>PartialMessage</code></a>.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The message that was sent.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>

</dl><dl><dt>*async with* typing()<a href="#discord.GroupChannel.typing" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns an asynchronous context manager that allows you to send a typing indicator to the destination for an indefinite period of time, or 10 seconds if the context manager is called using <code>await</code>.

Example Usage:

```
async with channel.typing():
    # simulate something heavy
    await asyncio.sleep(20)

await channel.send('Done!')

```

Example Usage:

```
await channel.typing()
# Do some computational magic for about 10 seconds
await channel.send('Done!')

```

Changed in version 2.0: This no longer works with the <code>with</code> syntax, <code>async with</code> must be used instead.

Changed in version 2.0: Added functionality to <code>await</code> the context manager to send a typing indicator for 10 seconds.

</dl><dl><dt>*async for ... in* history(***, *limit=100*, *before=None*, *after=None*, *around=None*, *oldest_first=None*)<a href="#discord.GroupChannel.history" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterator" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterator</a> that enables receiving the destination’s message history.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.read_message_history" title="discord.Permissions.read_message_history"><code>read_message_history</code></a> to do this.

Examples

Usage

```
counter = 0
async for message in channel.history(limit=200):
    if message.author == client.user:
        counter += 1

```

Flattening into a list:

```
messages = [message async for message in channel.history(limit=123)]
# messages is now a list of Message...

```

All parameters are optional.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **limit** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) – The number of messages to retrieve. If <code>None</code>, retrieves every message in the channel. Note, however, that this would make it a slow operation.
- **before** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve messages before this date or message. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.
- **after** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve messages after this date or message. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.
- **around** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve messages around this date or message. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time. When using this argument, the maximum limit is 101. Note that if the limit is an even number then this will return at most limit + 1 messages.
- **oldest\_first** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>]) – If set to <code>True</code>, return messages in oldest-&gt;newest order. Defaults to <code>True</code> if <code>after</code> is specified, otherwise <code>False</code>.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to get channel message history.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – The request to get message history failed.

</dd><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> – The message with the message data parsed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*jump_url<a href="#discord.GroupChannel.jump_url" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

<dl><dt>Type</dt>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>pins(***, *limit=50*, *before=None*, *oldest_first=False*)<a href="#discord.GroupChannel.pins" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Retrieves an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterator" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterator</a> of the pinned messages in the channel.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.view_channel" title="discord.Permissions.view_channel"><code>view_channel</code></a> and <a href="#discord.Permissions.read_message_history" title="discord.Permissions.read_message_history"><code>read_message_history</code></a> in order to use this.

Changed in version 2.6: Due to a change in Discord’s API, this now returns a paginated iterator instead of a list.

For backwards compatibility, you can still retrieve a list of pinned messages by using <code>await</code> on the returned object. This is however deprecated.

Note

Due to a limitation with the Discord API, the <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> object returned by this method does not contain complete <a href="#discord.Message.reactions" title="discord.Message.reactions"><code>Message.reactions</code></a> data.

Examples

Usage

```
counter = 0
async for message in channel.pins(limit=250):
    counter += 1

```

Flattening into a list:

```
messages = [message async for message in channel.pins(limit=50)]
# messages is now a list of Message...

```

All parameters are optional.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **limit** (*Optional**\[*<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)">*int*</a>*]*) –

  The number of pinned messages to retrieve. If <code>None</code>, it retrieves every pinned message in the channel. Note, however, that this would make it a slow operation. Defaults to <code>50</code>.

  New in version 2.6.
- **before** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>, <a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>]]) –

  Retrieve pinned messages before this time or snowflake. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.

  New in version 2.6.
- **oldest\_first** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  If set to <code>True</code>, return messages in oldest pin-&gt;newest pin order. Defaults to <code>False</code>.

  New in version 2.6.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the permission to retrieve pinned messages.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Retrieving the pinned messages failed.

</dd><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> – The pinned message with <a href="#discord.Message.pinned_at" title="discord.Message.pinned_at"><code>Message.pinned_at</code></a> set.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* send(*content=None*, ***, *tts=False*, *embed=None*, *embeds=None*, *file=None*, *files=None*, *stickers=None*, *delete_after=None*, *nonce=None*, *allowed_mentions=None*, *reference=None*, *mention_author=None*, *view=None*, *suppress_embeds=False*, *silent=False*, *poll=None*)<a href="#discord.GroupChannel.send" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Sends a message to the destination with the content given.

The content must be a type that can convert to a string through <code>str(content)</code>. If the content is set to <code>None</code> (the default), then the <code>embed</code> parameter must be provided.

To upload a single file, the <code>file</code> parameter should be used with a single <a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a> object. To upload multiple files, the <code>files</code> parameter should be used with a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#list" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>list</code></a> of <a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a> objects. **Specifying both parameters will lead to an exception**.

To upload a single embed, the <code>embed</code> parameter should be used with a single <a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a> object. To upload multiple embeds, the <code>embeds</code> parameter should be used with a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#list" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>list</code></a> of <a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a> objects. **Specifying both parameters will lead to an exception**.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> or <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>ValueError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **content** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The content of the message to send.
- **tts** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Indicates if the message should be sent using text-to-speech.
- **embed** (<a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a>) – The rich embed for the content.
- **embeds** (List\[<a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a>]) –

  A list of embeds to upload. Must be a maximum of 10.

  New in version 2.0.
- **file** (<a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a>) – The file to upload.
- **files** (List\[<a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a>]) – A list of files to upload. Must be a maximum of 10.
- **nonce** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The nonce to use for sending this message. If the message was successfully sent, then the message will have a nonce with this value.
- **delete\_after** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>float</code></a>) – If provided, the number of seconds to wait in the background before deleting the message we just sent. If the deletion fails, then it is silently ignored.
- **allowed\_mentions** (<a href="#discord.AllowedMentions" title="discord.AllowedMentions"><code>AllowedMentions</code></a>) –

  Controls the mentions being processed in this message. If this is passed, then the object is merged with <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a>. The merging behaviour only overrides attributes that have been explicitly passed to the object, otherwise it uses the attributes set in <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a>. If no object is passed at all then the defaults given by <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a> are used instead.

  New in version 1.4.
- **reference** (Union\[<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>, <a href="#discord.MessageReference" title="discord.MessageReference"><code>MessageReference</code></a>, <a href="#discord.PartialMessage" title="discord.PartialMessage"><code>PartialMessage</code></a>]) –

  A reference to the <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a> to which you are referencing, this can be created using <a href="#discord.Message.to_reference" title="discord.Message.to_reference"><code>to_reference()</code></a> or passed directly as a <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>. In the event of a replying reference, you can control whether this mentions the author of the referenced message using the <a href="#discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user" title="discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user"><code>replied_user</code></a> attribute of <code>allowed_mentions</code> or by setting <code>mention_author</code>.

  New in version 1.6.
- **mention\_author** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>]) –

  If set, overrides the <a href="#discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user" title="discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user"><code>replied_user</code></a> attribute of <code>allowed_mentions</code>.

  New in version 1.6.
- **view** (Union\[<a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.ui.View" title="discord.ui.View"><code>discord.ui.View</code></a>, <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.ui.LayoutView" title="discord.ui.LayoutView"><code>discord.ui.LayoutView</code></a>]) –

  A Discord UI View to add to the message.

  New in version 2.0.
- **stickers** (Sequence\[Union\[<a href="#discord.GuildSticker" title="discord.GuildSticker"><code>GuildSticker</code></a>, <a href="#discord.StickerItem" title="discord.StickerItem"><code>StickerItem</code></a>]]) –

  A list of stickers to upload. Must be a maximum of 3.

  New in version 2.0.
- **suppress\_embeds** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to suppress embeds for the message. This sends the message without any embeds if set to <code>True</code>.

  New in version 2.0.
- **silent** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) –

  Whether to suppress push and desktop notifications for the message. This will increment the mention counter in the UI, but will not actually send a notification.

  New in version 2.2.
- **poll** (<a href="#discord.Poll" title="discord.Poll"><code>Poll</code></a>) –

  The poll to send with this message.

  New in version 2.4.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Sending the message failed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to send the message.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – You sent a message with the same nonce as one that has been explicitly deleted shortly earlier.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – The <code>files</code> or <code>embeds</code> list is not of the appropriate size.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – You specified both <code>file</code> and <code>files</code>, or you specified both <code>embed</code> and <code>embeds</code>, or the <code>reference</code> object is not a <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>, <a href="#discord.MessageReference" title="discord.MessageReference"><code>MessageReference</code></a> or <a href="#discord.PartialMessage" title="discord.PartialMessage"><code>PartialMessage</code></a>.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The message that was sent.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>permissions_for(*obj*, */*)<a href="#discord.GroupChannel.permissions_for" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Handles permission resolution for a <a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a>.

This function is there for compatibility with other channel types.

Actual direct messages do not really have the concept of permissions.

This returns all the Text related permissions set to <code>True</code> except:

- <a href="#discord.Permissions.send_tts_messages" title="discord.Permissions.send_tts_messages"><code>send_tts_messages</code></a>: You cannot send TTS messages in a DM.
- <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_messages" title="discord.Permissions.manage_messages"><code>manage_messages</code></a>: You cannot delete others messages in a DM.
- <a href="#discord.Permissions.create_private_threads" title="discord.Permissions.create_private_threads"><code>create_private_threads</code></a>: There are no threads in a DM.
- <a href="#discord.Permissions.create_public_threads" title="discord.Permissions.create_public_threads"><code>create_public_threads</code></a>: There are no threads in a DM.
- <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_threads" title="discord.Permissions.manage_threads"><code>manage_threads</code></a>: There are no threads in a DM.
- <a href="#discord.Permissions.send_messages_in_threads" title="discord.Permissions.send_messages_in_threads"><code>send_messages_in_threads</code></a>: There are no threads in a DM.

This also checks the kick\_members permission if the user is the owner.

Changed in version 2.0: <code>obj</code> parameter is now positional-only.

Changed in version 2.1: Thread related permissions are now set to <code>False</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**obj** (<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>) – The user to check permissions for.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The resolved permissions for the user.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Permissions" title="discord.Permissions"><code>Permissions</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* leave()<a href="#discord.GroupChannel.leave" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Leave the group.

If you are the only one in the group, this deletes it as well.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Leaving the group failed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl>

<dl><dt>*class*discord.Invite<a href="#discord.Invite" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Represents a Discord <a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a> or <a href="#discord.abc.GuildChannel" title="discord.abc.GuildChannel"><code>abc.GuildChannel</code></a> invite.

Depending on the way this object was created, some of the attributes can have a value of <code>None</code>.

<dl><dt>x == y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two invites are equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x != y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two invites are not equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>hash(x)</dt>
<dd>

Returns the invite hash.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>str(x)</dt>
<dd>

Returns the invite URL.

</dd></dl>

The following table illustrates what methods will obtain the attributes:

| Attribute | Method |
| --- | --- |
| <a href="#discord.Invite.max_age" title="discord.Invite.max_age"><code>max_age</code></a> | <a href="#discord.abc.GuildChannel.invites" title="discord.abc.GuildChannel.invites"><code>abc.GuildChannel.invites()</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Guild.invites" title="discord.Guild.invites"><code>Guild.invites()</code></a> |
| <a href="#discord.Invite.max_uses" title="discord.Invite.max_uses"><code>max_uses</code></a> | <a href="#discord.abc.GuildChannel.invites" title="discord.abc.GuildChannel.invites"><code>abc.GuildChannel.invites()</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Guild.invites" title="discord.Guild.invites"><code>Guild.invites()</code></a> |
| <a href="#discord.Invite.created_at" title="discord.Invite.created_at"><code>created_at</code></a> | <a href="#discord.abc.GuildChannel.invites" title="discord.abc.GuildChannel.invites"><code>abc.GuildChannel.invites()</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Guild.invites" title="discord.Guild.invites"><code>Guild.invites()</code></a> |
| <a href="#discord.Invite.temporary" title="discord.Invite.temporary"><code>temporary</code></a> | <a href="#discord.abc.GuildChannel.invites" title="discord.abc.GuildChannel.invites"><code>abc.GuildChannel.invites()</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Guild.invites" title="discord.Guild.invites"><code>Guild.invites()</code></a> |
| <a href="#discord.Invite.uses" title="discord.Invite.uses"><code>uses</code></a> | <a href="#discord.abc.GuildChannel.invites" title="discord.abc.GuildChannel.invites"><code>abc.GuildChannel.invites()</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Guild.invites" title="discord.Guild.invites"><code>Guild.invites()</code></a> |
| <a href="#discord.Invite.approximate_member_count" title="discord.Invite.approximate_member_count"><code>approximate_member_count</code></a> | <a href="#discord.Client.fetch_invite" title="discord.Client.fetch_invite"><code>Client.fetch_invite()</code></a> with <code>with_counts</code> enabled |
| <a href="#discord.Invite.approximate_presence_count" title="discord.Invite.approximate_presence_count"><code>approximate_presence_count</code></a> | <a href="#discord.Client.fetch_invite" title="discord.Client.fetch_invite"><code>Client.fetch_invite()</code></a> with <code>with_counts</code> enabled |

If it’s not in the table above then it is available by all methods.

</dl><dl><dt>*await* create_guild(*name*, *icon=...*)<a href="#discord.Template.create_guild" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Creates a <a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a> using the template.

Bot accounts in more than 10 guilds are not allowed to create guilds.

Changed in version 2.0: The <code>region</code> parameter has been removed.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>ValueError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

Deprecated since version 2.6: This function is deprecated and will be removed in a future version.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The name of the guild.
- **icon** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#bytes" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bytes</code></a>) – The <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-bytes-like-object" title="(in Python v3.14)">bytes-like object</a> representing the icon. See <a href="#discord.ClientUser.edit" title="discord.ClientUser.edit"><code>ClientUser.edit()</code></a> for more details on what is expected.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Guild creation failed.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – Invalid icon image format given. Must be PNG or JPG.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The guild created. This is not the same guild that is added to cache.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* sync()<a href="#discord.Template.sync" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_guild" title="discord.Permissions.manage_guild"><code>manage_guild</code></a> in the source guild to do this.

<dl><dt>*class*discord.WelcomeScreen<a href="#discord.WelcomeScreen" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Represents a <a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a> welcome screen.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>description<a href="#discord.WelcomeScreen.description" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The description shown on the welcome screen.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>welcome_channels<a href="#discord.WelcomeScreen.welcome_channels" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The channels shown on the welcome screen.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

List\[<a href="#discord.WelcomeChannel" title="discord.WelcomeChannel"><code>WelcomeChannel</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*enabled<a href="#discord.WelcomeScreen.enabled" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Whether the welcome screen is displayed.

This is equivalent to checking if <code>WELCOME_SCREEN_ENABLED</code> is present in <a href="#discord.Guild.features" title="discord.Guild.features"><code>Guild.features</code></a>.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* edit(***, *description=...*, *welcome_channels=...*, *enabled=...*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.WelcomeScreen.edit" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Edit the welcome screen.

Welcome channels can only accept custom emojis if <a href="#discord.Guild.premium_tier" title="discord.Guild.premium_tier"><code>Guild.premium_tier</code></a> is level 2 or above.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_guild" title="discord.Permissions.manage_guild"><code>manage_guild</code></a> in the guild to do this.

Usage:

```
rules_channel = guild.get_channel(12345678)
announcements_channel = guild.get_channel(87654321)

custom_emoji = utils.get(guild.emojis, name='loudspeaker')

await welcome_screen.edit(
    description='This is a very cool community server!',
    welcome_channels=[
        WelcomeChannel(channel=rules_channel, description='Read the rules!', emoji='👨‍🏫'),
        WelcomeChannel(channel=announcements_channel, description='Watch out for announcements!', emoji=custom_emoji),
    ]
)

```

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **description** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The welcome screen’s description.
- **welcome\_channels** (Optional\[List\[<a href="#discord.WelcomeChannel" title="discord.WelcomeChannel"><code>WelcomeChannel</code></a>]]) – The welcome channels, in their respective order.
- **enabled** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>]) – Whether the welcome screen should be displayed.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for editing the welcome screen. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Editing the welcome screen failed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You don’t have permissions to edit the welcome screen.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – This welcome screen does not exist.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl>

</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_invite(***, *with_counts=True*)<a href="#discord.Widget.fetch_invite" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Retrieves an <a href="#discord.Invite" title="discord.Invite"><code>Invite</code></a> from the widget’s invite URL. This is the same as <a href="#discord.Client.fetch_invite" title="discord.Client.fetch_invite"><code>Client.fetch_invite()</code></a>; the invite code is abstracted away.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**with\_counts** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether to include count information in the invite. This fills the <a href="#discord.Invite.approximate_member_count" title="discord.Invite.approximate_member_count"><code>Invite.approximate_member_count</code></a> and <a href="#discord.Invite.approximate_presence_count" title="discord.Invite.approximate_presence_count"><code>Invite.approximate_presence_count</code></a> fields.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

</dl><dl><dt>*await* edit(***, *name=...*, *description=...*, *emoji=...*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.GuildSticker.edit" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Edits a <a href="#discord.GuildSticker" title="discord.GuildSticker"><code>GuildSticker</code></a> for the guild.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The sticker’s new name. Must be at least 2 characters.
- **description** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The sticker’s new description. Can be <code>None</code>.
- **emoji** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The name of a unicode emoji that represents the sticker’s expression.
- **reason** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The reason for editing this sticker. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You are not allowed to edit stickers.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – An error occurred editing the sticker.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The newly modified sticker.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.GuildSticker" title="discord.GuildSticker"><code>GuildSticker</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* delete(***, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.GuildSticker.delete" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Deletes the custom <a href="#discord.Sticker" title="discord.Sticker"><code>Sticker</code></a> from the guild.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_emojis_and_stickers" title="discord.Permissions.manage_emojis_and_stickers"><code>manage_emojis_and_stickers</code></a> to do this.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for deleting this sticker. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You are not allowed to delete stickers.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – An error occurred deleting the sticker.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl>

</dl><dl><dt>*await* edit(***, *name=...*, *volume=...*, *emoji=...*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.SoundboardSound.edit" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Edits the soundboard sound.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_expressions" title="discord.Permissions.manage_expressions"><code>manage_expressions</code></a> to edit the sound. If the sound was created by the client, you must have either <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_expressions" title="discord.Permissions.manage_expressions"><code>manage_expressions</code></a> or <a href="#discord.Permissions.create_expressions" title="discord.Permissions.create_expressions"><code>create_expressions</code></a>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The new name of the sound. Must be between 2 and 32 characters.
- **volume** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>float</code></a>]) – The new volume of the sound. Must be between 0 and 1.
- **emoji** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.Emoji" title="discord.Emoji"><code>Emoji</code></a>, <a href="#discord.PartialEmoji" title="discord.PartialEmoji"><code>PartialEmoji</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]]) – The new emoji of the sound.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for editing this sound. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to edit the soundboard sound.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Editing the soundboard sound failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The newly updated soundboard sound.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.SoundboardSound" title="discord.SoundboardSound"><code>SoundboardSound</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* delete(***, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.SoundboardSound.delete" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Deletes the soundboard sound.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_expressions" title="discord.Permissions.manage_expressions"><code>manage_expressions</code></a> to delete the sound. If the sound was created by the client, you must have either <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_expressions" title="discord.Permissions.manage_expressions"><code>manage_expressions</code></a> or <a href="#discord.Permissions.create_expressions" title="discord.Permissions.create_expressions"><code>create_expressions</code></a>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for deleting this sound. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to delete the soundboard sound.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Deleting the soundboard sound failed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_subscription(*subscription_id*, */*)<a href="#discord.SKU.fetch_subscription" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Retrieves a <a href="#discord.Subscription" title="discord.Subscription"><code>Subscription</code></a> with the specified ID.

New in version 2.5.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**subscription\_id** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The subscription’s ID to fetch from.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – An subscription with this ID does not exist.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Fetching the subscription failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The subscription you requested.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Subscription" title="discord.Subscription"><code>Subscription</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*async for ... in* subscriptions(***, *limit=50*, *before=None*, *after=None*, *user*)<a href="#discord.SKU.subscriptions" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Retrieves an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterator" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterator</a> of the <a href="#discord.Subscription" title="discord.Subscription"><code>Subscription</code></a> that SKU has.

New in version 2.5.

Examples

Usage

```
async for subscription in sku.subscriptions(limit=100, user=user):
    print(subscription.user_id, subscription.current_period_end)

```

Flattening into a list

```
subscriptions = [subscription async for subscription in sku.subscriptions(limit=100, user=user)]
# subscriptions is now a list of Subscription...

```

All parameters are optional.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **limit** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) – The number of subscriptions to retrieve. If <code>None</code>, it retrieves every subscription for this SKU. Note, however, that this would make it a slow operation. Defaults to <code>100</code>.
- **before** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve subscriptions before this date or entitlement. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.
- **after** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]]) – Retrieve subscriptions after this date or entitlement. If a datetime is provided, it is recommended to use a UTC aware datetime. If the datetime is naive, it is assumed to be local time.
- **user** (<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>Snowflake</code></a>) – The user to filter by.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Fetching the subscriptions failed.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – Both <code>after</code> and <code>before</code> were provided, as Discord does not support this type of pagination.

</dd><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Subscription" title="discord.Subscription"><code>Subscription</code></a> – The subscription with the SKU.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl>

<dd>

Returns an approximate count of votes for this answer.

If the poll is finished, the count is exact.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*poll<a href="#discord.PollAnswer.poll" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns the parent poll of this answer.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Poll" title="discord.Poll"><code>Poll</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*victor<a href="#discord.PollAnswer.victor" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Whether the answer is the one that had the most votes when the poll ended.

New in version 2.5.

Note

If the poll has not ended, this will always return <code>False</code>.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*async for ... in* voters(***, *limit=None*, *after=None*)<a href="#discord.PollAnswer.voters" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-asynchronous-iterator" title="(in Python v3.14)">asynchronous iterator</a> representing the users that have voted on this answer.

The <code>after</code> parameter must represent a user and meet the <a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a> abc.

This can only be called when the parent poll was sent to a message.

Examples

Usage

```
async for voter in poll_answer.voters():
    print(f'{voter} has voted for {poll_answer}!')

```

Flattening into a list:

```
voters = [voter async for voter in poll_answer.voters()]
# voters is now a list of User

```

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **limit** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) – The maximum number of results to return. If not provided, returns all the users who voted on this poll answer.
- **after** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>]) – For pagination, voters are sorted by member.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Retrieving the users failed.

</dd><dt>Yields</dt>
<dd>

Union\[<a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a>] – The member (if retrievable) or the user that has voted on this poll answer. The case where it can be a <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> is in a guild message context. Sometimes it can be a <a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a> if the member has left the guild or if the member is not cached.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl>

## Data Classes ¶

Some classes are just there to be data containers, this lists them.

Unlike [models](#discord-api-models) you are allowed to create most of these yourself, even if they can also be used to hold attributes.

Nearly all classes here have [\_\_slots\_\_](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/datamodel.html#slots "(in Python v3.14)") defined which means that it is impossible to have dynamic attributes to the data classes.

The only exception to this rule is [`Object`](#discord.Object "discord.Object"), which is made with dynamic attributes in mind.

### Object ¶

Attributes

- [created\_at](#discord.Object.created_at)
- [id](#discord.Object.id)
- [type](#discord.Object.type)

<dl><dt>*class*discord.Object(*id*, ***, *type=...*)<a href="#discord.Object" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Represents a generic Discord object.

The purpose of this class is to allow you to create ‘miniature’ versions of data classes if you want to pass in just an ID. Most functions that take in a specific data class with an ID can also take in this class as a substitute instead. Note that even though this is the case, not all objects (if any) actually inherit from this class.

There are also some cases where some websocket events are received in <a href="https://github.com/Rapptz/discord.py/issues/21">strange order</a> and when such events happened you would receive this class rather than the actual data class. These cases are extremely rare.

<dl><dt>x == y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two objects are equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x != y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two objects are not equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>hash(x)</dt>
<dd>

Returns the object’s hash.

</dd></dl>

<dl><dt>id<a href="#discord.Object.id" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The ID of the object.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>type<a href="#discord.Object.type" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The discord.py model type of the object, if not specified, defaults to this class.

Note

In instances where there are multiple applicable types, use a shared base class. for example, both <a href="#discord.Member" title="discord.Member"><code>Member</code></a> and <a href="#discord.User" title="discord.User"><code>User</code></a> are subclasses of <a href="#discord.abc.User" title="discord.abc.User"><code>abc.User</code></a>.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Type\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*created_at<a href="#discord.Object.created_at" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns the snowflake’s creation time in UTC.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl>

<dl><dt>*class*discord.Embed(***, *colour=None*, *color=None*, *title=None*, *type='rich'*, *url=None*, *description=None*, *timestamp=None*)<a href="#discord.Embed" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Represents a Discord embed.

<dl><dt>len(x)</dt>
<dd>

Returns the total size of the embed. Useful for checking if it’s within the 6000 character limit.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>bool(b)</dt>
<dd>

Returns whether the embed has any data set.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x == y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two embeds are equal.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl>

For ease of use, all parameters that expect a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a> are implicitly casted to <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a> for you.

Changed in version 2.0: <code>Embed.Empty</code> has been removed in favour of <code>None</code>.

<dl><dt>title<a href="#discord.Embed.title" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The title of the embed. This can be set during initialisation. Can only be up to 256 characters.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>type<a href="#discord.Embed.type" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The type of embed. Usually “rich”. This can be set during initialisation. Possible strings for embed types can be found on discord’s <a href="https://discord.com/developers/docs/resources/message#embed-object-embed-types">api docs</a>

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>description<a href="#discord.Embed.description" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The description of the embed. This can be set during initialisation. Can only be up to 4096 characters.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>url<a href="#discord.Embed.url" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The URL of the embed. This can be set during initialisation.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>timestamp<a href="#discord.Embed.timestamp" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The timestamp of the embed content. This is an aware datetime. If a naive datetime is passed, it is converted to an aware datetime with the local timezone.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>colour<a href="#discord.Embed.colour" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The colour code of the embed. Aliased to <code>color</code> as well. This can be set during initialisation.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[Union\[<a href="#discord.Colour" title="discord.Colour"><code>Colour</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*classmethod* from_dict(*data*)<a href="#discord.Embed.from_dict" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Converts a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>dict</code></a> to a <a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a> provided it is in the format that Discord expects it to be in.

You can find out about this format in the <a href="https://discord.com/developers/docs/resources/message#embed-object">official Discord documentation</a>.

<dd>

The flags of this embed.

New in version 2.5.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.EmbedFlags" title="discord.EmbedFlags"><code>EmbedFlags</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*footer<a href="#discord.Embed.footer" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns an <code>EmbedProxy</code> denoting the footer contents.

See <a href="#discord.Embed.set_footer" title="discord.Embed.set_footer"><code>set_footer()</code></a> for possible values you can access.

If the attribute has no value then <code>None</code> is returned.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>set_footer(***, *text=None*, *icon_url=None*)<a href="#discord.Embed.set_footer" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Sets the footer for the embed content.

This function returns the class instance to allow for fluent-style chaining.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **text** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The footer text. Can only be up to 2048 characters.
- **icon\_url** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The URL of the footer icon. Only HTTP(S) is supported. Inline attachment URLs are also supported, see <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/faq.html#local-image">How do I use a local image file for an embed image?</a>.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>remove_footer()<a href="#discord.Embed.remove_footer" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Clears embed’s footer information.

This function returns the class instance to allow for fluent-style chaining.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*property*image<a href="#discord.Embed.image" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns an <code>EmbedProxy</code> denoting the image contents.

Possible attributes you can access are:

- <code>url</code> for the image URL.
- <code>proxy_url</code> for the proxied image URL.
- <code>width</code> for the image width.
- <code>height</code> for the image height.
- <code>flags</code> for the image’s attachment flags.

If the attribute has no value then <code>None</code> is returned.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>set_image(***, *url*)<a href="#discord.Embed.set_image" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Sets the image for the embed content.

This function returns the class instance to allow for fluent-style chaining.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**url** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The source URL for the image. Only HTTP(S) is supported. If <code>None</code> is passed, any existing image is removed. Inline attachment URLs are also supported, see <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/faq.html#local-image">How do I use a local image file for an embed image?</a>.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*thumbnail<a href="#discord.Embed.thumbnail" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns an <code>EmbedProxy</code> denoting the thumbnail contents.

Possible attributes you can access are:

- <code>url</code> for the thumbnail URL.
- <code>proxy_url</code> for the proxied thumbnail URL.
- <code>width</code> for the thumbnail width.
- <code>height</code> for the thumbnail height.
- <code>flags</code> for the thumbnail’s attachment flags.

If the attribute has no value then <code>None</code> is returned.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>set_thumbnail(***, *url*)<a href="#discord.Embed.set_thumbnail" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Sets the thumbnail for the embed content.

This function returns the class instance to allow for fluent-style chaining.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**url** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The source URL for the thumbnail. Only HTTP(S) is supported. If <code>None</code> is passed, any existing thumbnail is removed. Inline attachment URLs are also supported, see <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/faq.html#local-image">How do I use a local image file for an embed image?</a>.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*video<a href="#discord.Embed.video" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns an <code>EmbedProxy</code> denoting the video contents.

Possible attributes include:

- <code>url</code> for the video URL.
- <code>proxy_url</code> for the proxied video URL.
- <code>height</code> for the video height.
- <code>width</code> for the video width.
- <code>flags</code> for the video’s attachment flags.

If the attribute has no value then <code>None</code> is returned.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*property*provider<a href="#discord.Embed.provider" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns an <code>EmbedProxy</code> denoting the provider contents.

The only attributes that might be accessed are <code>name</code> and <code>url</code>.

If the attribute has no value then <code>None</code> is returned.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*property*author<a href="#discord.Embed.author" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns an <code>EmbedProxy</code> denoting the author contents.

See <a href="#discord.Embed.set_author" title="discord.Embed.set_author"><code>set_author()</code></a> for possible values you can access.

If the attribute has no value then <code>None</code> is returned.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>set_author(***, *name*, *url=None*, *icon_url=None*)<a href="#discord.Embed.set_author" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Sets the author for the embed content.

This function returns the class instance to allow for fluent-style chaining.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The name of the author. Can only be up to 256 characters.
- **url** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The URL for the author.
- **icon\_url** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The URL of the author icon. Only HTTP(S) is supported. Inline attachment URLs are also supported, see <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/faq.html#local-image">How do I use a local image file for an embed image?</a>.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>remove_author()<a href="#discord.Embed.remove_author" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Clears embed’s author information.

This function returns the class instance to allow for fluent-style chaining.

New in version 1.4.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*property*fields<a href="#discord.Embed.fields" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#list" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>list</code></a> of <code>EmbedProxy</code> denoting the field contents.

See <a href="#discord.Embed.add_field" title="discord.Embed.add_field"><code>add_field()</code></a> for possible values you can access.

If the attribute has no value then <code>None</code> is returned.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

List\[<code>EmbedProxy</code>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>add_field(***, *name*, *value*, *inline=True*)<a href="#discord.Embed.add_field" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Adds a field to the embed object.

This function returns the class instance to allow for fluent-style chaining. Can only be up to 25 fields.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The name of the field. Can only be up to 256 characters.
- **value** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The value of the field. Can only be up to 1024 characters.
- **inline** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether the field should be displayed inline.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>insert_field_at(*index*, ***, *name*, *value*, *inline=True*)<a href="#discord.Embed.insert_field_at" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Inserts a field before a specified index to the embed.

This function returns the class instance to allow for fluent-style chaining. Can only be up to 25 fields.

New in version 1.2.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **index** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The index of where to insert the field.
- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The name of the field. Can only be up to 256 characters.
- **value** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The value of the field. Can only be up to 1024 characters.
- **inline** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether the field should be displayed inline.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>clear_fields()<a href="#discord.Embed.clear_fields" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Removes all fields from this embed.

This function returns the class instance to allow for fluent-style chaining.

Changed in version 2.0: This function now returns the class instance.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>remove_field(*index*)<a href="#discord.Embed.remove_field" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Removes a field at a specified index.

If the index is invalid or out of bounds then the error is silently swallowed.

This function returns the class instance to allow for fluent-style chaining.

Note

When deleting a field by index, the index of the other fields shift to fill the gap just like a regular list.

Changed in version 2.0: This function now returns the class instance.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**index** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The index of the field to remove.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>set_field_at(*index*, ***, *name*, *value*, *inline=True*)<a href="#discord.Embed.set_field_at" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Modifies a field to the embed object.

The index must point to a valid pre-existing field. Can only be up to 25 fields.

This function returns the class instance to allow for fluent-style chaining.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **index** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) – The index of the field to modify.
- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The name of the field. Can only be up to 256 characters.
- **value** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The value of the field. Can only be up to 1024 characters.
- **inline** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether the field should be displayed inline.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#IndexError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**IndexError**</a> – An invalid index was provided.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>to_dict()<a href="#discord.Embed.to_dict" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Converts this embed object into a dict.

</dl>
