<dl><dt>*class*discord.AllowedMentions(***, *everyone=True*, *users=True*, *roles=True*, *replied_user=True*)<a href="#discord.AllowedMentions" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A class that represents what mentions are allowed in a message.

This class can be set during <a href="#discord.Client" title="discord.Client"><code>Client</code></a> initialisation to apply to every message sent. It can also be applied on a per message basis via <a href="#discord.abc.Messageable.send" title="discord.abc.Messageable.send"><code>abc.Messageable.send()</code></a> for more fine-grained control.

<dl><dt>everyone<a href="#discord.AllowedMentions.everyone" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Whether to allow everyone and here mentions. Defaults to <code>True</code>.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>users<a href="#discord.AllowedMentions.users" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Controls the users being mentioned. If <code>True</code> (the default) then users are mentioned based on the message content. If <code>False</code> then users are not mentioned at all. If a list of <a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a> is given then only the users provided will be mentioned, provided those users are in the message content.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Union\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>, Sequence\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>]]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>roles<a href="#discord.AllowedMentions.roles" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Controls the roles being mentioned. If <code>True</code> (the default) then roles are mentioned based on the message content. If <code>False</code> then roles are not mentioned at all. If a list of <a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a> is given then only the roles provided will be mentioned, provided those roles are in the message content.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Union\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>, Sequence\[<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>]]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>replied_user<a href="#discord.AllowedMentions.replied_user" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Whether to mention the author of the message being replied to. Defaults to <code>True</code>.

New in version 1.6.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*classmethod* all()<a href="#discord.AllowedMentions.all" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A factory method that returns a <a href="#discord.AllowedMentions" title="discord.AllowedMentions"><code>AllowedMentions</code></a> with all fields explicitly set to <code>True</code>

New in version 1.5.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*classmethod* none()<a href="#discord.AllowedMentions.none" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A factory method that returns a <a href="#discord.AllowedMentions" title="discord.AllowedMentions"><code>AllowedMentions</code></a> with all fields set to <code>False</code>

New in version 1.5.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl>

</dl><dl><dt>resolved<a href="#discord.MessageReference.resolved" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

The message that this reference resolved to. If this is <code>None</code> then the original message was not fetched either due to the Discord API not attempting to resolve it or it not being available at the time of creation. If the message was resolved at a prior point but has since been deleted then this will be of type <a href="#discord.DeletedReferencedMessage" title="discord.DeletedReferencedMessage"><code>DeletedReferencedMessage</code></a>.

New in version 1.6.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*classmethod* from_message(*message*, ***, *fail_if_not_exists=True*, *type=&lt;MessageReferenceType.default: 0&gt;*)<a href="#discord.MessageReference.from_message" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

- **type** (<a href="#discord.MessageReferenceType" title="discord.MessageReferenceType"><code>MessageReferenceType</code></a>) –

<dl><dt>*class*discord.PartialMessage(***, *channel*, *id*)<a href="#discord.PartialMessage" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Represents a partial message to aid with working messages when only a message and channel ID are present.

There are two ways to construct this class. The first one is through the constructor itself, and the second is via the following:

- <a href="#discord.TextChannel.get_partial_message" title="discord.TextChannel.get_partial_message"><code>TextChannel.get_partial_message()</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.VoiceChannel.get_partial_message" title="discord.VoiceChannel.get_partial_message"><code>VoiceChannel.get_partial_message()</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.StageChannel.get_partial_message" title="discord.StageChannel.get_partial_message"><code>StageChannel.get_partial_message()</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.Thread.get_partial_message" title="discord.Thread.get_partial_message"><code>Thread.get_partial_message()</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.DMChannel.get_partial_message" title="discord.DMChannel.get_partial_message"><code>DMChannel.get_partial_message()</code></a>

Note that this class is trimmed down and has no rich attributes.

New in version 1.6.

<dl><dt>x == y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two partial messages are equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x != y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two partial messages are not equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>hash(x)</dt>
<dd>

Returns the partial message’s hash.

</dd></dl>

<dl><dt>channel<a href="#discord.PartialMessage.channel" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The channel associated with this partial message.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Union\[<a href="#discord.PartialMessageable" title="discord.PartialMessageable"><code>PartialMessageable</code></a>, <a href="#discord.TextChannel" title="discord.TextChannel"><code>TextChannel</code></a>, <a href="#discord.StageChannel" title="discord.StageChannel"><code>StageChannel</code></a>, <a href="#discord.VoiceChannel" title="discord.VoiceChannel"><code>VoiceChannel</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a>, <a href="#discord.DMChannel" title="discord.DMChannel"><code>DMChannel</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>id<a href="#discord.PartialMessage.id" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The message ID.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>guild<a href="#discord.PartialMessage.guild" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

The guild that the partial message belongs to, if applicable.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>

Optional\[<a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*created_at<a href="#discord.PartialMessage.created_at" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

The partial message’s creation time in UTC.

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>

<dd>

Returns a URL that allows the client to jump to this message.

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*thread<a href="#discord.PartialMessage.thread" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

The public thread created from this message, if it exists.

Note

This does not retrieve archived threads, as they are not retained in the internal cache. Use <a href="#discord.PartialMessage.fetch_thread" title="discord.PartialMessage.fetch_thread"><code>fetch_thread()</code></a> instead.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch()<a href="#discord.PartialMessage.fetch" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Fetches the partial message to a full <a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The message was not found.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the permissions required to get a message.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Retrieving the message failed.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The full message.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* delete(***, *delay=None*)<a href="#discord.PartialMessage.delete" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Deletes the message.

Your own messages could be deleted without any proper permissions. However to delete other people’s messages, you must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_messages" title="discord.Permissions.manage_messages"><code>manage_messages</code></a>.

Changed in version 1.1: Added the new <code>delay</code> keyword-only parameter.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**delay** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>float</code></a>]) – If provided, the number of seconds to wait in the background before deleting the message. If the deletion fails then it is silently ignored.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have proper permissions to delete the message.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The message was deleted already
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Deleting the message failed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* edit(***, *content=...*, *embed=...*, *embeds=...*, *attachments=...*, *delete_after=None*, *allowed_mentions=...*, *view=...*)<a href="#discord.PartialMessage.edit" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Edits the message.

The content must be able to be transformed into a string via <code>str(content)</code>.

Changed in version 2.0: Edits are no longer in-place, the newly edited message is returned instead.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **content** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The new content to replace the message with. Could be <code>None</code> to remove the content.
- **embed** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a>]) – The new embed to replace the original with. Could be <code>None</code> to remove the embed.
- **embeds** (List\[<a href="#discord.Embed" title="discord.Embed"><code>Embed</code></a>]) –

  The new embeds to replace the original with. Must be a maximum of 10. To remove all embeds <code>[]</code> should be passed.

  New in version 2.0.
- **attachments** (List\[Union\[<a href="#discord.Attachment" title="discord.Attachment"><code>Attachment</code></a>, <a href="#discord.File" title="discord.File"><code>File</code></a>]]) –

  A list of attachments to keep in the message as well as new files to upload. If <code>[]</code> is passed then all attachments are removed.

  Note

  New files will always appear after current attachments.

  New in version 2.0.
- **delete\_after** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>float</code></a>]) – If provided, the number of seconds to wait in the background before deleting the message we just edited. If the deletion fails, then it is silently ignored.
- **allowed\_mentions** (Optional\[<a href="#discord.AllowedMentions" title="discord.AllowedMentions"><code>AllowedMentions</code></a>]) –

  Controls the mentions being processed in this message. If this is passed, then the object is merged with <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a>. The merging behaviour only overrides attributes that have been explicitly passed to the object, otherwise it uses the attributes set in <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a>. If no object is passed at all then the defaults given by <a href="#discord.Client.allowed_mentions" title="discord.Client.allowed_mentions"><code>allowed_mentions</code></a> are used instead.

  New in version 1.4.
- **view** (Optional\[Union\[<a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.ui.View" title="discord.ui.View"><code>View</code></a>, <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.ui.LayoutView" title="discord.ui.LayoutView"><code>LayoutView</code></a>]]) –

  The updated view to update this message with. If <code>None</code> is passed then the view is removed.

  Note

  If you want to update the message to have a <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.ui.LayoutView" title="discord.ui.LayoutView"><code>LayoutView</code></a>, you must explicitly set the <code>content</code>, <code>embed</code>, <code>embeds</code>, and <code>attachments</code> parameters to <code>None</code> if the previous message had any.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Editing the message failed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – Tried to suppress a message without permissions or edited a message’s content or embed that isn’t yours.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – This message does not exist.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – You specified both <code>embed</code> and <code>embeds</code>

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The newly edited message.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Message" title="discord.Message"><code>Message</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* publish()<a href="#discord.PartialMessage.publish" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Publishes this message to the channel’s followers.

The message must have been sent in a news channel. You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.send_messages" title="discord.Permissions.send_messages"><code>send_messages</code></a> to do this.

If the message is not your own then <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_messages" title="discord.Permissions.manage_messages"><code>manage_messages</code></a> is also needed.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to publish this message or the channel is not a news channel.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Publishing the message failed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* pin(***, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.PartialMessage.pin" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Pins the message.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.pin_messages" title="discord.Permissions.pin_messages"><code>pin_messages</code></a> to do this in a non-private channel context.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) –

The reason for pinning the message. Shows up on the audit log.

New in version 1.4.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to pin the message.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The message or channel was not found or deleted.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Pinning the message failed, probably due to the channel having more than 250 pinned messages.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* unpin(***, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.PartialMessage.unpin" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Unpins the message.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.pin_messages" title="discord.Permissions.pin_messages"><code>pin_messages</code></a> to do this in a non-private channel context.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) –

The reason for unpinning the message. Shows up on the audit log.

New in version 1.4.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to unpin the message.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The message or channel was not found or deleted.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Unpinning the message failed.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* add_reaction(*emoji*, */*)<a href="#discord.PartialMessage.add_reaction" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Adds a reaction to the message.

The emoji may be a unicode emoji or a custom guild <a href="#discord.Emoji" title="discord.Emoji"><code>Emoji</code></a>.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.read_message_history" title="discord.Permissions.read_message_history"><code>read_message_history</code></a> to do this. If nobody else has reacted to the message using this emoji, <a href="#discord.Permissions.add_reactions" title="discord.Permissions.add_reactions"><code>add_reactions</code></a> is required.

Changed in version 2.0: <code>emoji</code> parameter is now positional-only.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**emoji** (Union\[<a href="#discord.Emoji" title="discord.Emoji"><code>Emoji</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Reaction" title="discord.Reaction"><code>Reaction</code></a>, <a href="#discord.PartialEmoji" title="discord.PartialEmoji"><code>PartialEmoji</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The emoji to react with.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Adding the reaction failed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to react to the message.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The emoji you specified was not found.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – The emoji parameter is invalid.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* remove_reaction(*emoji*, *member*)<a href="#discord.PartialMessage.remove_reaction" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Remove a reaction by the member from the message.

The emoji may be a unicode emoji or a custom guild <a href="#discord.Emoji" title="discord.Emoji"><code>Emoji</code></a>.

If the reaction is not your own (i.e. <code>member</code> parameter is not you) then <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_messages" title="discord.Permissions.manage_messages"><code>manage_messages</code></a> is needed.

The <code>member</code> parameter must represent a member and meet the <a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a> abc.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **emoji** (Union\[<a href="#discord.Emoji" title="discord.Emoji"><code>Emoji</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Reaction" title="discord.Reaction"><code>Reaction</code></a>, <a href="#discord.PartialEmoji" title="discord.PartialEmoji"><code>PartialEmoji</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The emoji to remove.
- **member** (<a href="#discord.abc.Snowflake" title="discord.abc.Snowflake"><code>abc.Snowflake</code></a>) – The member for which to remove the reaction.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Removing the reaction failed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to remove the reaction.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The member or emoji you specified was not found.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – The emoji parameter is invalid.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* clear_reaction(*emoji*)<a href="#discord.PartialMessage.clear_reaction" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Clears a specific reaction from the message.

The emoji may be a unicode emoji or a custom guild <a href="#discord.Emoji" title="discord.Emoji"><code>Emoji</code></a>.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_messages" title="discord.Permissions.manage_messages"><code>manage_messages</code></a> to do this.

New in version 1.3.

Changed in version 2.0: This function will now raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>TypeError</code></a> instead of <code>InvalidArgument</code>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**emoji** (Union\[<a href="#discord.Emoji" title="discord.Emoji"><code>Emoji</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Reaction" title="discord.Reaction"><code>Reaction</code></a>, <a href="#discord.PartialEmoji" title="discord.PartialEmoji"><code>PartialEmoji</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The emoji to clear.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Clearing the reaction failed.
- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to clear the reaction.
- <a href="#discord.NotFound" title="discord.NotFound">**NotFound**</a> – The emoji you specified was not found.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#TypeError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**TypeError**</a> – The emoji parameter is invalid.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* clear_reactions()<a href="#discord.PartialMessage.clear_reactions" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Removes all the reactions from the message.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_messages" title="discord.Permissions.manage_messages"><code>manage_messages</code></a> to do this.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have the proper permissions to remove all the reactions.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* create_thread(***, *name*, *auto_archive_duration=...*, *slowmode_delay=None*, *reason=None*)<a href="#discord.PartialMessage.create_thread" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

This function is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#coroutine">*coroutine*</a>.

Creates a public thread from this message.

You must have <a href="#discord.Permissions.create_public_threads" title="discord.Permissions.create_public_threads"><code>create_public_threads</code></a> in order to create a public thread from a message.

The channel this message belongs in must be a <a href="#discord.TextChannel" title="discord.TextChannel"><code>TextChannel</code></a>.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **name** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>) – The name of the thread.
- **auto\_archive\_duration** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>) –

  The duration in minutes before a thread is automatically hidden from the channel list. If not provided, the channel’s default auto archive duration is used.

  Must be one of <code>60</code>, <code>1440</code>, <code>4320</code>, or <code>10080</code>, if provided.
- **slowmode\_delay** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]) – Specifies the slowmode rate limit for user in this channel, in seconds. The maximum value possible is <code>21600</code>. By default no slowmode rate limit if this is <code>None</code>.
- **reason** (Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The reason for creating a new thread. Shows up on the audit log.

</dd><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="discord.Forbidden">**Forbidden**</a> – You do not have permissions to create a thread.
- <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException">**HTTPException**</a> – Creating the thread failed.
- <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – This message does not have guild info attached.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The created thread.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*await* fetch_thread()<a href="#discord.PartialMessage.fetch_thread" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

<dl><dt>*class*discord.Intents(*value=0*, ***kwargs*)<a href="#discord.Intents" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Wraps up a Discord gateway intent flag.

Similar to <a href="#discord.Permissions" title="discord.Permissions"><code>Permissions</code></a>, the properties provided are two way. You can set and retrieve individual bits using the properties as if they were regular bools.

To construct an object you can pass keyword arguments denoting the flags to enable or disable.

This is used to disable certain gateway features that are unnecessary to run your bot. To make use of this, it is passed to the <code>intents</code> keyword argument of <a href="#discord.Client" title="discord.Client"><code>Client</code></a>.

New in version 1.5.

<dl><dt>x == y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two flags are equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x != y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two flags are not equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x | y, x |= y</dt>
<dd>

Returns an Intents instance with all enabled flags from both x and y.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x &amp; y, x &amp;= y</dt>
<dd>

Returns an Intents instance with only flags enabled on both x and y.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x ^ y, x ^= y</dt>
<dd>

Returns an Intents instance with only flags enabled on only one of x or y, not on both.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>~x</dt>
<dd>

Returns an Intents instance with all flags inverted from x.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>hash(x)</dt>
<dd>

Return the flag’s hash.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>iter(x)</dt>
<dd>

Returns an iterator of <code>(name, value)</code> pairs. This allows it to be, for example, constructed as a dict or a list of pairs.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>bool(b)</dt>
<dd>

Returns whether any intent is enabled.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl>

<dl><dt>value<a href="#discord.Intents.value" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The raw value. You should query flags via the properties rather than using this raw value.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*classmethod* all()<a href="#discord.Intents.all" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A factory method that creates a <a href="#discord.Intents" title="discord.Intents"><code>Intents</code></a> with everything enabled.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*classmethod* none()<a href="#discord.Intents.none" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A factory method that creates a <a href="#discord.Intents" title="discord.Intents"><code>Intents</code></a> with everything disabled.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*classmethod* default()<a href="#discord.Intents.default" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A factory method that creates a <a href="#discord.Intents" title="discord.Intents"><code>Intents</code></a> with everything enabled except <a href="#discord.Intents.presences" title="discord.Intents.presences"><code>presences</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Intents.members" title="discord.Intents.members"><code>members</code></a>, and <a href="#discord.Intents.message_content" title="discord.Intents.message_content"><code>message_content</code></a>.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>guilds<a href="#discord.Intents.guilds" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Whether guild related events are enabled.

This corresponds to the following events:

- <a href="#discord.on_guild_join" title="discord.on_guild_join"><code>on_guild_join()</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.on_guild_remove" title="discord.on_guild_remove"><code>on_guild_remove()</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.on_guild_available" title="discord.on_guild_available"><code>on_guild_available()</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.on_guild_unavailable" title="discord.on_guild_unavailable"><code>on_guild_unavailable()</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.on_guild_channel_update" title="discord.on_guild_channel_update"><code>on_guild_channel_update()</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.on_guild_channel_create" title="discord.on_guild_channel_create"><code>on_guild_channel_create()</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.on_guild_channel_delete" title="discord.on_guild_channel_delete"><code>on_guild_channel_delete()</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.on_guild_channel_pins_update" title="discord.on_guild_channel_pins_update"><code>on_guild_channel_pins_update()</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.on_thread_create" title="discord.on_thread_create"><code>on_thread_create()</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.on_thread_join" title="discord.on_thread_join"><code>on_thread_join()</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.on_thread_update" title="discord.on_thread_update"><code>on_thread_update()</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.on_thread_delete" title="discord.on_thread_delete"><code>on_thread_delete()</code></a>

This also corresponds to the following attributes and classes in terms of cache:

- <a href="#discord.Client.guilds" title="discord.Client.guilds"><code>Client.guilds</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.Guild" title="discord.Guild"><code>Guild</code></a> and all its attributes.
- <a href="#discord.Client.get_channel" title="discord.Client.get_channel"><code>Client.get_channel()</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.Client.get_all_channels" title="discord.Client.get_all_channels"><code>Client.get_all_channels()</code></a>

It is highly advisable to leave this intent enabled for your bot to function.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>message_content<a href="#discord.Intents.message_content" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Whether message content, attachments, embeds and components will be available in messages which do not meet the following criteria:

- The message was sent by the client
- The message was sent in direct messages
- The message mentions the client

This applies to the following events:

- <a href="#discord.on_message" title="discord.on_message"><code>on_message()</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.on_message_edit" title="discord.on_message_edit"><code>on_message_edit()</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.on_message_delete" title="discord.on_message_delete"><code>on_message_delete()</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.on_raw_message_edit" title="discord.on_raw_message_edit"><code>on_raw_message_edit()</code></a>

For more information go to the <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/intents.html#need-message-content-intent">message content intent documentation</a>.

Note

Currently, this requires opting in explicitly via the developer portal as well. Bots in over 100 guilds will need to apply to Discord for verification.

New in version 2.0.

### MemberCacheFlags ¶

Attributes

- [joined](#discord.MemberCacheFlags.joined)
- [value](#discord.MemberCacheFlags.value)
- [voice](#discord.MemberCacheFlags.voice)

Methods

- cls [MemberCacheFlags.all](#discord.MemberCacheFlags.all)
- cls [MemberCacheFlags.from\_intents](#discord.MemberCacheFlags.from_intents)
- cls [MemberCacheFlags.none](#discord.MemberCacheFlags.none)

<dl><dt>*class*discord.MemberCacheFlags(***kwargs*)<a href="#discord.MemberCacheFlags" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Controls the library’s cache policy when it comes to members.

This allows for finer grained control over what members are cached. Note that the bot’s own member is always cached. This class is passed to the <code>member_cache_flags</code> parameter in <a href="#discord.Client" title="discord.Client"><code>Client</code></a>.

Due to a quirk in how Discord works, in order to ensure proper cleanup of cache resources it is recommended to have <a href="#discord.Intents.members" title="discord.Intents.members"><code>Intents.members</code></a> enabled. Otherwise the library cannot know when a member leaves a guild and is thus unable to cleanup after itself.

To construct an object you can pass keyword arguments denoting the flags to enable or disable.

The default value is all flags enabled.

New in version 1.5.

<dl><dt>x == y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two flags are equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x != y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two flags are not equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x | y, x |= y</dt>
<dd>

Returns a MemberCacheFlags instance with all enabled flags from both x and y.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x &amp; y, x &amp;= y</dt>
<dd>

Returns a MemberCacheFlags instance with only flags enabled on both x and y.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x ^ y, x ^= y</dt>
<dd>

Returns a MemberCacheFlags instance with only flags enabled on only one of x or y, not on both.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>~x</dt>
<dd>

Returns a MemberCacheFlags instance with all flags inverted from x.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>hash(x)</dt>
<dd>

Return the flag’s hash.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>iter(x)</dt>
<dd>

Returns an iterator of <code>(name, value)</code> pairs. This allows it to be, for example, constructed as a dict or a list of pairs.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>bool(b)</dt>
<dd>

Returns whether any flag is set to <code>True</code>.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl>

<dl><dt>value<a href="#discord.MemberCacheFlags.value" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The raw value. You should query flags via the properties rather than using this raw value.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*classmethod* all()<a href="#discord.MemberCacheFlags.all" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A factory method that creates a <a href="#discord.MemberCacheFlags" title="discord.MemberCacheFlags"><code>MemberCacheFlags</code></a> with everything enabled.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*classmethod* none()<a href="#discord.MemberCacheFlags.none" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A factory method that creates a <a href="#discord.MemberCacheFlags" title="discord.MemberCacheFlags"><code>MemberCacheFlags</code></a> with everything disabled.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>voice<a href="#discord.MemberCacheFlags.voice" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Whether to cache members that are in voice.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.voice_states" title="discord.Intents.voice_states"><code>Intents.voice_states</code></a>.

Members that leave voice are no longer cached.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>joined<a href="#discord.MemberCacheFlags.joined" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Whether to cache members that joined the guild or are chunked as part of the initial log in flow.

This requires <a href="#discord.Intents.members" title="discord.Intents.members"><code>Intents.members</code></a>.

Members that leave the guild are no longer cached.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*classmethod* from_intents(*intents*)<a href="#discord.MemberCacheFlags.from_intents" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A factory method that creates a <a href="#discord.MemberCacheFlags" title="discord.MemberCacheFlags"><code>MemberCacheFlags</code></a> based on the currently selected <a href="#discord.Intents" title="discord.Intents"><code>Intents</code></a>.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**intents** (<a href="#discord.Intents" title="discord.Intents"><code>Intents</code></a>) – The intents to select from.

</dd><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

The resulting member cache flags.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="#discord.MemberCacheFlags" title="discord.MemberCacheFlags"><code>MemberCacheFlags</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl>

<dl><dt>*class*discord.ChannelFlags(***kwargs*)<a href="#discord.ChannelFlags" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Wraps up the Discord <a href="#discord.abc.GuildChannel" title="discord.abc.GuildChannel"><code>GuildChannel</code></a> or <a href="#discord.Thread" title="discord.Thread"><code>Thread</code></a> flags.

<dl><dt>x == y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two channel flags are equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x != y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two channel flags are not equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x | y, x |= y</dt>
<dd>

Returns a ChannelFlags instance with all enabled flags from both x and y.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x &amp; y, x &amp;= y</dt>
<dd>

Returns a ChannelFlags instance with only flags enabled on both x and y.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x ^ y, x ^= y</dt>
<dd>

Returns a ChannelFlags instance with only flags enabled on only one of x or y, not on both.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>~x</dt>
<dd>

Returns a ChannelFlags instance with all flags inverted from x.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>hash(x)</dt>
<dd>

Return the flag’s hash.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>iter(x)</dt>
<dd>

Returns an iterator of <code>(name, value)</code> pairs. This allows it to be, for example, constructed as a dict or a list of pairs. Note that aliases are not shown.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>bool(b)</dt>
<dd>

Returns whether any flag is set to <code>True</code>.

</dd></dl>

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>*class*discord.File(*fp*, *filename=None*, ***, *spoiler=...*, *description=None*)<a href="#discord.File" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A parameter object used for <a href="#discord.abc.Messageable.send" title="discord.abc.Messageable.send"><code>abc.Messageable.send()</code></a> for sending file objects.

Note

File objects are single use and are not meant to be reused in multiple <a href="#discord.abc.Messageable.send" title="discord.abc.Messageable.send"><code>abc.Messageable.send()</code></a>s.

<dl><dt>fp<a href="#discord.File.fp" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A file-like object opened in binary mode and read mode or a filename representing a file in the hard drive to open.

Note

If the file-like object passed is opened via <code>open</code> then the modes ‘rb’ should be used.

To pass binary data, consider usage of <code>io.BytesIO</code>.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Union\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>os.PathLike</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/io.html#io.BufferedIOBase" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>io.BufferedIOBase</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>spoiler<a href="#discord.File.spoiler" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Whether the attachment is a spoiler. If left unspecified, the <a href="#discord.File.filename" title="discord.File.filename"><code>filename</code></a> is used to determine if the file is a spoiler.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>

The file description to display, currently only supported for images.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*filename<a href="#discord.File.filename" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The filename to display when uploading to Discord. If this is not given then it defaults to <code>fp.name</code> or if <code>fp</code> is a string then the <code>filename</code> will default to the string given.

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*property*uri<a href="#discord.File.uri" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*classmethod* from_str(*value*)<a href="#discord.Colour.from_str" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Constructs a <a href="#discord.Colour" title="discord.Colour"><code>Colour</code></a> from a string.

The following formats are accepted:

- <code>0x&lt;hex&gt;</code>
- <code>#&lt;hex&gt;</code>
- <code>0x#&lt;hex&gt;</code>
- <code>rgb(&lt;number&gt;, &lt;number&gt;, &lt;number&gt;)</code>

Like CSS, <code>&lt;number&gt;</code> can be either 0-255 or 0-100% and <code>&lt;hex&gt;</code> can be either a 6 digit hex number or a 3 digit hex shortcut (e.g. #FFF).

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>Raises</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError" title="(in Python v3.14)">**ValueError**</a> – The string could not be converted into a colour.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*classmethod* default()<a href="#discord.Colour.default" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*classmethod* random(***, *seed=None*)<a href="#discord.Colour.random" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A factory method that returns a <a href="#discord.Colour" title="discord.Colour"><code>Colour</code></a> with a random hue.

Note

The random algorithm works by choosing a colour with a random hue but with maxed out saturation and value.

New in version 1.6.

### BaseActivity ¶

Attributes

- [created\_at](#discord.BaseActivity.created_at)

<dl><dt>*class*discord.BaseActivity(***kwargs*)<a href="#discord.BaseActivity" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The base activity that all user-settable activities inherit from. A user-settable activity is one that can be used in <a href="#discord.Client.change_presence" title="discord.Client.change_presence"><code>Client.change_presence()</code></a>.

The following types currently count as user-settable:

- <a href="#discord.Activity" title="discord.Activity"><code>Activity</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.Game" title="discord.Game"><code>Game</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.Streaming" title="discord.Streaming"><code>Streaming</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.CustomActivity" title="discord.CustomActivity"><code>CustomActivity</code></a>

Note that although these types are considered user-settable by the library, Discord typically ignores certain combinations of activity depending on what is currently set. This behaviour may change in the future so there are no guarantees on whether Discord will actually let you set these types.

New in version 1.3.

<dl><dt>*property*created_at<a href="#discord.BaseActivity.created_at" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

When the user started doing this activity in UTC.

New in version 1.3.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.datetime</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl>

<dl><dt>*class*discord.Activity(***kwargs*)<a href="#discord.Activity" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Represents an activity in Discord.

This could be an activity such as streaming, playing, listening or watching.

For memory optimisation purposes, some activities are offered in slimmed down versions:

- <a href="#discord.Game" title="discord.Game"><code>Game</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.Streaming" title="discord.Streaming"><code>Streaming</code></a>

<dl><dt>application_id<a href="#discord.Activity.application_id" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The application ID of the game.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>name<a href="#discord.Activity.name" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>url<a href="#discord.Activity.url" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

</dd></dl></dd>

</dl><dl><dt>timestamps<a href="#discord.Activity.timestamps" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A dictionary of timestamps. It contains the following optional keys:

- <code>start</code>: Corresponds to when the user started doing the activity in milliseconds since Unix epoch.
- <code>end</code>: Corresponds to when the user will finish doing the activity in milliseconds since Unix epoch.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>dict</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>assets<a href="#discord.Activity.assets" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A dictionary representing the images and their hover text of an activity. It contains the following optional keys:

- <code>large_image</code>: A string representing the ID for the large image asset.
- <code>large_text</code>: A string representing the text when hovering over the large image asset.
- <code>large_url</code>: A string representing the URL of the large image asset.
- <code>small_image</code>: A string representing the ID for the small image asset.
- <code>small_text</code>: A string representing the text when hovering over the small image asset.
- <code>small_url</code>: A string representing the URL of the small image asset.

<dl><dt>*class*discord.Permissions(*permissions=0*, ***kwargs*)<a href="#discord.Permissions" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Wraps up the Discord permission value.

The properties provided are two way. You can set and retrieve individual bits using the properties as if they were regular bools. This allows you to edit permissions.

Changed in version 1.3: You can now use keyword arguments to initialize <a href="#discord.Permissions" title="discord.Permissions"><code>Permissions</code></a> similar to <a href="#discord.Permissions.update" title="discord.Permissions.update"><code>update()</code></a>.

<dl><dt>x == y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two permissions are equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x != y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two permissions are not equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x &lt;= y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if a permission is a subset of another permission.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x &gt;= y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if a permission is a superset of another permission.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x &lt; y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if a permission is a strict subset of another permission.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x &gt; y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if a permission is a strict superset of another permission.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x | y, x |= y</dt>
<dd>

Returns a Permissions instance with all enabled flags from both x and y.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x &amp; y, x &amp;= y</dt>
<dd>

Returns a Permissions instance with only flags enabled on both x and y.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x ^ y, x ^= y</dt>
<dd>

Returns a Permissions instance with only flags enabled on only one of x or y, not on both.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>~x</dt>
<dd>

Returns a Permissions instance with all flags inverted from x.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>hash(x)</dt>
<dd>

Return the permission’s hash.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>iter(x)</dt>
<dd>

Returns an iterator of <code>(perm, value)</code> pairs. This allows it to be, for example, constructed as a dict or a list of pairs. Note that aliases are not shown.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>bool(b)</dt>
<dd>

Returns whether the permissions object has any permissions set to <code>True</code>.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl>

<dl><dt>value<a href="#discord.Permissions.value" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The raw value. This value is a bit array field of a 53-bit integer representing the currently available permissions. You should query permissions via the properties rather than using this raw value.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

- <a href="#discord.Permissions.change_nickname" title="discord.Permissions.change_nickname"><code>change_nickname</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_nicknames" title="discord.Permissions.manage_nicknames"><code>manage_nicknames</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.Permissions.kick_members" title="discord.Permissions.kick_members"><code>kick_members</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.Permissions.ban_members" title="discord.Permissions.ban_members"><code>ban_members</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.Permissions.administrator" title="discord.Permissions.administrator"><code>administrator</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.Permissions.create_expressions" title="discord.Permissions.create_expressions"><code>create_expressions</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.Permissions.moderate_members" title="discord.Permissions.moderate_members"><code>moderate_members</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.Permissions.create_events" title="discord.Permissions.create_events"><code>create_events</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_events" title="discord.Permissions.manage_events"><code>manage_events</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.Permissions.view_creator_monetization_analytics" title="discord.Permissions.view_creator_monetization_analytics"><code>view_creator_monetization_analytics</code></a>

Changed in version 1.7: Added <a href="#discord.Permissions.stream" title="discord.Permissions.stream"><code>stream</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Permissions.priority_speaker" title="discord.Permissions.priority_speaker"><code>priority_speaker</code></a> and <a href="#discord.Permissions.use_application_commands" title="discord.Permissions.use_application_commands"><code>use_application_commands</code></a> permissions.

Changed in version 2.0: Added <a href="#discord.Permissions.create_public_threads" title="discord.Permissions.create_public_threads"><code>create_public_threads</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Permissions.create_private_threads" title="discord.Permissions.create_private_threads"><code>create_private_threads</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Permissions.manage_threads" title="discord.Permissions.manage_threads"><code>manage_threads</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Permissions.use_external_stickers" title="discord.Permissions.use_external_stickers"><code>use_external_stickers</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Permissions.send_messages_in_threads" title="discord.Permissions.send_messages_in_threads"><code>send_messages_in_threads</code></a> and <a href="#discord.Permissions.request_to_speak" title="discord.Permissions.request_to_speak"><code>request_to_speak</code></a> permissions.

Changed in version 2.7: Added <a href="#discord.Permissions.pin_messages" title="discord.Permissions.pin_messages"><code>pin_messages</code></a> and <a href="#discord.Permissions.bypass_slowmode" title="discord.Permissions.bypass_slowmode"><code>bypass_slowmode</code></a> permissions.

Changed in version 2.3: Added <a href="#discord.Permissions.create_expressions" title="discord.Permissions.create_expressions"><code>create_expressions</code></a> permission.

Changed in version 2.4: Added <a href="#discord.Permissions.view_creator_monetization_analytics" title="discord.Permissions.view_creator_monetization_analytics"><code>view_creator_monetization_analytics</code></a> permission.

### PermissionOverwrite ¶

Methods

- cls [PermissionOverwrite.from\_pair](#discord.PermissionOverwrite.from_pair)
- def [is\_empty](#discord.PermissionOverwrite.is_empty)
- def [pair](#discord.PermissionOverwrite.pair)
- def [update](#discord.PermissionOverwrite.update)

<dl><dt>*class*discord.PermissionOverwrite(***kwargs*)<a href="#discord.PermissionOverwrite" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

A type that is used to represent a channel specific permission.

Unlike a regular <a href="#discord.Permissions" title="discord.Permissions"><code>Permissions</code></a>, the default value of a permission is equivalent to <code>None</code> and not <code>False</code>. Setting a value to <code>False</code> is **explicitly** denying that permission, while setting a value to <code>True</code> is **explicitly** allowing that permission.

The values supported by this are the same as <a href="#discord.Permissions" title="discord.Permissions"><code>Permissions</code></a> with the added possibility of it being set to <code>None</code>.

<dl><dt>x == y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two overwrites are equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x != y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two overwrites are not equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>iter(x)</dt>
<dd>

Returns an iterator of <code>(perm, value)</code> pairs. This allows it to be, for example, constructed as a dict or a list of pairs. Note that aliases are not shown.

</dd></dl>

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**\*\*kwargs** – Set the value of permissions by their name.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>pair()<a href="#discord.PermissionOverwrite.pair" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Tuple\[<a href="#discord.Permissions" title="discord.Permissions"><code>Permissions</code></a>, <a href="#discord.Permissions" title="discord.Permissions"><code>Permissions</code></a>]: Returns the (allow, deny) pair from this overwrite.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*classmethod* from_pair(*allow*, *deny*)<a href="#discord.PermissionOverwrite.from_pair" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Creates an overwrite from an allow/deny pair of <a href="#discord.Permissions" title="discord.Permissions"><code>Permissions</code></a>.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>is_empty()<a href="#discord.PermissionOverwrite.is_empty" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Checks if the permission overwrite is currently empty.

An empty permission overwrite is one that has no overwrites set to <code>True</code> or <code>False</code>.

<dl><dt>Returns</dt>
<dd>

Indicates if the overwrite is empty.

</dd><dt>Return type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>update(***kwargs*)<a href="#discord.PermissionOverwrite.update" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Bulk updates this permission overwrite object.

Allows you to set multiple attributes by using keyword arguments. The names must be equivalent to the properties listed. Extraneous key/value pairs will be silently ignored.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

**\*\*kwargs** – A list of key/value pairs to bulk update with.

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl>

Attributes

- [join\_notifications](#discord.SystemChannelFlags.join_notifications)

- [role\_subscription\_purchase\_notifications](#discord.SystemChannelFlags.role_subscription_purchase_notifications)
- [value](#discord.SystemChannelFlags.value)

<dl><dt>*class*discord.SystemChannelFlags(***kwargs*)<a href="#discord.SystemChannelFlags" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Wraps up a Discord system channel flag value.

Similar to <a href="#discord.Permissions" title="discord.Permissions"><code>Permissions</code></a>, the properties provided are two way. You can set and retrieve individual bits using the properties as if they were regular bools. This allows you to edit the system flags easily.

To construct an object you can pass keyword arguments denoting the flags to enable or disable.

<dl><dt>x == y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two flags are equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x != y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two flags are not equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x | y, x |= y</dt>
<dd>

Returns a SystemChannelFlags instance with all enabled flags from both x and y.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x &amp; y, x &amp;= y</dt>
<dd>

Returns a SystemChannelFlags instance with only flags enabled on both x and y.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x ^ y, x ^= y</dt>
<dd>

Returns a SystemChannelFlags instance with only flags enabled on only one of x or y, not on both.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>~x</dt>
<dd>

Returns a SystemChannelFlags instance with all flags inverted from x.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>hash(x)</dt>
<dd>

Return the flag’s hash.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>iter(x)</dt>
<dd>

Returns an iterator of <code>(name, value)</code> pairs. This allows it to be, for example, constructed as a dict or a list of pairs.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>bool(b)</dt>
<dd>

Returns whether any flag is set to <code>True</code>.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl>

<dl><dt>value<a href="#discord.SystemChannelFlags.value" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The raw value. This value is a bit array field of a 53-bit integer representing the currently available flags. You should query flags via the properties rather than using this raw value.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>join_notifications<a href="#discord.SystemChannelFlags.join_notifications" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Returns <code>True</code> if the system channel is used for member join notifications.

<dd>

<dl><dt>*class*discord.MessageFlags(***kwargs*)<a href="#discord.MessageFlags" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Wraps up a Discord Message flag value.

See <a href="#discord.SystemChannelFlags" title="discord.SystemChannelFlags"><code>SystemChannelFlags</code></a>.

<dl><dt>x == y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two flags are equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x != y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two flags are not equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x | y, x |= y</dt>
<dd>

Returns a MessageFlags instance with all enabled flags from both x and y.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x &amp; y, x &amp;= y</dt>
<dd>

Returns a MessageFlags instance with only flags enabled on both x and y.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x ^ y, x ^= y</dt>
<dd>

Returns a MessageFlags instance with only flags enabled on only one of x or y, not on both.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>~x</dt>
<dd>

Returns a MessageFlags instance with all flags inverted from x.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>hash(x)</dt>
<dd>

Return the flag’s hash.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>iter(x)</dt>
<dd>

Returns an iterator of <code>(name, value)</code> pairs. This allows it to be, for example, constructed as a dict or a list of pairs.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>bool(b)</dt>
<dd>

Returns whether any flag is set to <code>True</code>.

New in version 2.0.

</dd></dl>

New in version 1.3.

<dl><dt>value<a href="#discord.MessageFlags.value" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The raw value. This value is a bit array field of a 53-bit integer representing the currently available flags. You should query flags via the properties rather than using this raw value.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>

<dl><dt>*class*discord.AttachmentFlags(***kwargs*)<a href="#discord.AttachmentFlags" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Wraps up the Discord Attachment flags

New in version 2.4.

<dl><dt>x == y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two AttachmentFlags are equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x != y</dt>
<dd>

Checks if two AttachmentFlags are not equal.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x | y, x |= y</dt>
<dd>

Returns a AttachmentFlags instance with all enabled flags from both x and y.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x &amp; y, x &amp;= y</dt>
<dd>

Returns a AttachmentFlags instance with only flags enabled on both x and y.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>x ^ y, x ^= y</dt>
<dd>

Returns a AttachmentFlags instance with only flags enabled on only one of x or y, not on both.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>~x</dt>
<dd>

Returns a AttachmentFlags instance with all flags inverted from x.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>hash(x)</dt>
<dd>

Return the flag’s hash.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>iter(x)</dt>
<dd>

Returns an iterator of <code>(name, value)</code> pairs. This allows it to be, for example, constructed as a dict or a list of pairs. Note that aliases are not shown.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>bool(b)</dt>
<dd>

Returns whether any flag is set to <code>True</code>.

</dd></dl>

<dl><dt>value<a href="#discord.AttachmentFlags.value" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The raw value. You should query flags via the properties rather than using this raw value.

<dl><dt>*class*discord.Poll(*question*, *duration*, ***, *multiple=False*, *layout_type=&lt;PollLayoutType.default: 1&gt;*)<a href="#discord.Poll" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Represents a message’s Poll.

New in version 2.4.

<dl><dt>Parameters</dt>
<dd>

- **question** (Union\[<a href="#discord.PollMedia" title="discord.PollMedia"><code>PollMedia</code></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>]) – The poll’s displayed question. The text can be up to 300 characters.
- **duration** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.timedelta" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>datetime.timedelta</code></a>) – The duration of the poll. Duration must be in hours.
- **multiple** (<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>bool</code></a>) – Whether users are allowed to select more than one answer. Defaults to <code>False</code>.

## Exceptions ¶

The following exceptions are thrown by the library.

<dl><dt>*exception*discord.DiscordException<a href="#discord.DiscordException" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Base exception class for discord.py

Ideally speaking, this could be caught to handle any exceptions raised from this library.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*exception*discord.ClientException<a href="#discord.ClientException" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Exception that’s raised when an operation in the <a href="#discord.Client" title="discord.Client"><code>Client</code></a> fails.

These are usually for exceptions that happened due to user input.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*exception*discord.LoginFailure<a href="#discord.LoginFailure" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Exception that’s raised when the <a href="#discord.Client.login" title="discord.Client.login"><code>Client.login()</code></a> function fails to log you in from improper credentials or some other misc. failure.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*exception*discord.HTTPException(*response*, *message*)<a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Exception that’s raised when an HTTP request operation fails.

<dl><dt>response<a href="#discord.HTTPException.response" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The response of the failed HTTP request. This is an instance of <a href="https://docs.aiohttp.org/en/stable/client_reference.html#aiohttp.ClientResponse" title="(in aiohttp v3.13)"><code>aiohttp.ClientResponse</code></a>. In some cases this could also be a <a href="https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/#requests.Response" title="(in Requests v2.33.0.dev1)"><code>requests.Response</code></a>.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.aiohttp.org/en/stable/client_reference.html#aiohttp.ClientResponse" title="(in aiohttp v3.13)"><code>aiohttp.ClientResponse</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>text<a href="#discord.HTTPException.text" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The text of the error. Could be an empty string.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>status<a href="#discord.HTTPException.status" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The status code of the HTTP request.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>code<a href="#discord.HTTPException.code" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The Discord specific error code for the failure.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*exception*discord.RateLimited(*retry_after*)<a href="#discord.RateLimited" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Exception that’s raised for when status code 429 occurs and the timeout is greater than the configured maximum using the <code>max_ratelimit_timeout</code> parameter in <a href="#discord.Client" title="discord.Client"><code>Client</code></a>.

This is not raised during global ratelimits.

Since sometimes requests are halted pre-emptively before they’re even made, this **does not** subclass <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException"><code>HTTPException</code></a>.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>retry_after<a href="#discord.RateLimited.retry_after" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The amount of seconds that the client should wait before retrying the request.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#float" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>float</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*exception*discord.Forbidden(*response*, *message*)<a href="#discord.Forbidden" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Exception that’s raised for when status code 403 occurs.

Subclass of <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException"><code>HTTPException</code></a>

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*exception*discord.NotFound(*response*, *message*)<a href="#discord.NotFound" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Exception that’s raised for when status code 404 occurs.

Subclass of <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException"><code>HTTPException</code></a>

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*exception*discord.DiscordServerError(*response*, *message*)<a href="#discord.DiscordServerError" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Exception that’s raised for when a 500 range status code occurs.

Subclass of <a href="#discord.HTTPException" title="discord.HTTPException"><code>HTTPException</code></a>.

New in version 1.5.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*exception*discord.InvalidData<a href="#discord.InvalidData" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Exception that’s raised when the library encounters unknown or invalid data from Discord.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*exception*discord.GatewayNotFound<a href="#discord.GatewayNotFound" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

An exception that is raised when the gateway for Discord could not be found

</dl><dl><dt>reason<a href="#discord.ConnectionClosed.reason" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>

The reason provided for the closure.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>

<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>str</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>shard_id<a href="#discord.ConnectionClosed.shard_id" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The shard ID that got closed if applicable.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*exception*discord.PrivilegedIntentsRequired(*shard_id*)<a href="#discord.PrivilegedIntentsRequired" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Exception that’s raised when the gateway is requesting privileged intents but they’re not ticked in the developer page yet.

Go to <a href="https://discord.com/developers/applications/">https://discord.com/developers/applications/</a> and enable the intents that are required. Currently these are as follows:

- <a href="#discord.Intents.members" title="discord.Intents.members"><code>Intents.members</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.Intents.presences" title="discord.Intents.presences"><code>Intents.presences</code></a>
- <a href="#discord.Intents.message_content" title="discord.Intents.message_content"><code>Intents.message_content</code></a>

<dl><dt>shard_id<a href="#discord.PrivilegedIntentsRequired.shard_id" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The shard ID that got closed if applicable.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

Optional\[<a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#int" title="(in Python v3.14)"><code>int</code></a>]

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*exception*discord.InteractionResponded(*interaction*)<a href="#discord.InteractionResponded" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Exception that’s raised when sending another interaction response using <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.InteractionResponse" title="discord.InteractionResponse"><code>InteractionResponse</code></a> when one has already been done before.

An interaction can only respond once.

New in version 2.0.

<dl><dt>interaction<a href="#discord.InteractionResponded.interaction" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

The interaction that’s already been responded to.

<dl><dt>Type</dt>
<dd>

<a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.Interaction" title="discord.Interaction"><code>Interaction</code></a>

</dd></dl></dd>
</dl></dd>
</dl><dl><dt>*exception*discord.MissingApplicationID(*message=None*)<a href="#discord.MissingApplicationID" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

An exception raised when the client does not have an application ID set.

An application ID is required for syncing application commands and various other application tasks such as SKUs or application emojis.

This inherits from <a href="https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html#discord.app_commands.AppCommandError" title="discord.app_commands.AppCommandError"><code>AppCommandError</code></a> and <a href="#discord.ClientException" title="discord.ClientException"><code>ClientException</code></a>.

New in version 2.0.

Changed in version 2.5: This is now exported to the <code>discord</code> namespace and now inherits from <a href="#discord.ClientException" title="discord.ClientException"><code>ClientException</code></a>.

</dd></dl><dl><dt>*exception*discord.FFmpegProcessError<a href="#discord.FFmpegProcessError" title="Permalink to this definition">¶</a></dt>
<dd>

Exception that’s raised when an FFmpeg process fails.

New in version 2.7.
